knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Minimization Viewpoint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal evaluation as strongly convex quadratic regularization on a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). The proximal evaluation of \(f\) at \(x\in H\) is the unique solution
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=\underset{y\in H}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\}.\]
Thus the proximal operator is an optimization interface that replaces direct minimization of \(f\) by minimization of \(f\) plus a quadratic penalty centered at the query point \(x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal evaluation uniquely minimizes the function plus a quadratic penalty for moving away from the query point.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a real Hilbert space}
f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}

notation.meaning: proximal operator of the scaled function

source_refs.locator: 10.5 The Proximal Point Method p. 288

source_witnesses.locator: 10.5 The Proximal Point Method p. 288

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal minimization with a linear perturbation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the possibly empty or set-valued regularized minimization interface for a general prox-function and feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a nonempty set \(Q_1\subseteq\mathbb E_1\), a prox-function \(d_1:Q_1\to\mathbb R\), and \(s\in\mathbb E_1^*\), define
\[
\mathcal P_{d_1,Q_1}(s)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in Q_1}\left\{d_1(x)+\langle s,x\rangle_{\mathbb E_1}\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal evaluation with linear perturbation s returns the minimizer set over the feasible set of the prox-function plus the linear pairing with s. The definition alone does not assert existence or uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, and let \(\lambda>0\). Its resolvent is the everywhere-defined single-valued mapping
\[J_{\lambda A}:=(I+\lambda A)^{-1}.\]
Equivalently, \(y=J_{\lambda A}(x)\) precisely when \(x\in y+\lambda A(y)\). If \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex and \(A=\partial f\), then
\[J_{\lambda\partial f}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The resolvent of a maximal monotone operator is an everywhere-defined single-valued map that solves an implicit inclusion; for a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function on the Hilbert space, its proximal operator is the resolvent of its subdifferential.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Point Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zeros of a maximal monotone operator represented as resolvent fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone and let \(\lambda>0\). The zero set of \(A\) admits the fixed-point representation
\[\operatorname{zer}A:=\{x\in H:0\in A(x)\}=\operatorname{Fix}J_{\lambda A}:=\{x\in H:J_{\lambda A}(x)=x\}.\]
Consequently, solving the inclusion \(0\in A(x)\) is equivalent to finding a fixed point of the single-valued resolvent \(J_{\lambda A}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point solves the monotone inclusion exactly when it is a fixed point of the operator's resolvent.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a real Hilbert space}

notation.meaning: set of zeros of the operator

knowledge_statements.title: Resolvent–Fixed-Point Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise correspondence linking resolvent evaluation, graph membership, and zero residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a maximal monotone operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\), parameter \(\lambda>0\), and points \(x,y\in H\),
\[y=J_{\lambda A}(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \frac{x-y}{\lambda}\in A(y).\]
In particular, the resolvent residual \(R_{\lambda A}:=I-J_{\lambda A}\) satisfies
\[R_{\lambda A}(x)=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad x=J_{\lambda A}(x)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in A(x).\]
Hence graph membership under the resolvent and fixed-point solution of the original inclusion are equivalent descriptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resolvent evaluation is equivalent to scaled graph membership, while a zero resolvent residual is equivalent to solving the original inclusion.
assumptions_latex: A:H\rightrightarrows H\text{ is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y=J_{\lambda A}x\iff (x-y)/\lambda\in A(y),\qquad R_{\lambda A}x=0\iff0\in A(x)

children.title: Implicit Discretization Viewpoint
children.top_down_role: Proximal iterations organized as implicit discretizations of optimization dynamics.

knowledge_statements.title: Implicit Discretization Viewpoint
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backward-Euler discretization of convex subgradient flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given a proper, lower-semicontinuous convex function \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), a step size \(h>0\), an initial point \(x^0\in H\), and an iteration limit \(N\), apply backward Euler to the differential inclusion \(\dot x(t)+\partial f(x(t))\ni0\). For \(k=0,\ldots,N-1\), compute \(x^{k+1}\) from
\[\frac{x^{k+1}-x^k}{h}+\partial f(x^{k+1})\ni0,\]
equivalently \(x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{hf}(x^k)\). Stop early if \(x^{k+1}=x^k\); otherwise output \(x^N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-point step is backward Euler applied to subgradient flow, evaluating the subdifferential at the new iterate.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a real Hilbert space}

children.title: Convex Proximal Map Regime
children.top_down_role: Single-valued and stable proximal geometry for convex functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Proximal Map Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existence, uniqueness, and firm nonexpansiveness in convex proximal geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). Then \(P:=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\) is defined uniquely at every \(x\in H\) and is firmly nonexpansive:
\[\lVert P(x)-P(y)\rVert^2\leq\langle P(x)-P(y),x-y\rangle\qquad(x,y\in H).\]
Consequently, \(P\) is nonexpansive and continuous, satisfying \(\lVert P(x)-P(y)\rVert\leq\lVert x-y\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function, the proximal map is everywhere single-valued, firmly nonexpansive, and therefore Lipschitz continuous with constant one.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a real Hilbert space}
f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\text{ is single-valued and firmly nonexpansive}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and uniqueness of the convex proximal point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Well-posedness of Euclidean proximal evaluation for proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. Then, for every \(x\in\mathbb E\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_f(x)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{u\in\mathbb E}\left\{f(u)+\frac12\lVert u-x\rVert^2\right\}
\]
is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every point x, a proper closed convex function has exactly one proximal point.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean proximal map in Douglas–Rachford splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the Euclidean proximal oracle used for two-function convex splitting and records the source's Bregman-divergence extension remark.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal H\) be a Euclidean space, let \(F,G:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be closed convex functions, and suppose their proximal maps are readily computable. Douglas–Rachford splitting applies to \(\min_{x\in\mathcal H}\{F(x)+G(x)\}\). For \(\tau>0\) and \(x\in\mathcal H\),
\[
\operatorname{Prox}_{\tau F}(x):=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x'\in\mathcal H}\left\{\frac12\lVert x-x'\rVert^2+\tau F(x')\right\}.
\]
The source notes that replacing the squared Euclidean distance by a Bregman divergence yields a generalized proximal construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Douglas–Rachford splitting is intended for a sum of two closed convex functions whose proximal maps can be computed efficiently. The Euclidean proximal map minimizes the function plus a squared-distance term. The source also notes a Bregman-divergence generalization.
assumptions_latex: F,G:\mathcal H\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ are closed and convex}
\operatorname{Prox}_{\tau F}\text{ and }\operatorname{Prox}_{\tau G}\text{ are readily computable}

children.title: Nonconvex Proximal Map Regimes
children.top_down_role: Local, set-valued, and regularization-dependent proximal geometry outside convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Proximal Map Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional proximal geometry below the prox-boundedness threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and prox-bounded, with threshold \(\lambda_f>0\). For \(0<\lambda<\lambda_f\), define
\[P_\lambda f(x):=\underset{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\}.\]
For every \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), this set is nonempty and compact. Unlike the convex regime, it need not be a singleton, and a single-valued selection need not be globally nonexpansive or continuous. At or above \(\lambda_f\), finiteness or attainment can fail.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the prox-boundedness threshold, nonconvex proximal values exist compactly but may be multiple; at larger parameters, even finiteness or attainment may fail.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and prox-bounded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_\lambda f(x)\text{ is nonempty and compact, but may be set-valued}

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Fixed-Point Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed points represented by centered regularized minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a proper function \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(\lambda>0\), interpret the proximal mapping set-valuedly. Its fixed-point set is
\[\operatorname{Fix}P_\lambda f=\left\{x\in H:x\in P_\lambda f(x)\right\}=\left\{x\in H:f(x)\leq f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\ \text{for every }y\in H\right\}.\]
Thus a proximal fixed point is exactly a point that globally minimizes its own quadratically regularized subproblem; convexity is not required for this representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point is a proximal fixed point exactly when it globally solves the proximal subproblem centered at itself.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a real Hilbert space}

notation.meaning: points belonging to their own proximal value

children.title: Global Minimizer Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Regimes where proximal fixed points correspond to global minimizers.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Minimizer Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact convex correspondence between global minimizers and proximal fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). Then
\[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}f(x)=\operatorname{Fix}(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}).\]
Indeed, the common set is also \(\{x\in H:0\in\partial f(x)\}\). The equality holds for every positive proximal parameter, including when both sets are empty. Thus global minimization of \(f\) is equivalent to fixed-point solution of any convex proximal map generated by \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function, global minimizers are exactly the fixed points of its proximal operator for every positive parameter.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a real Hilbert space}
f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}

children.title: Stationary-Point Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Regimes where fixed points encode stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationary-Point Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex subdifferential stationarity represented by proximal fixed points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. For any \(x\in H\), the following are equivalent:
\[0\in\partial f(x),\qquad x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\text{ for some }\lambda>0,\qquad x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\text{ for every }\lambda>0.\]
Under convexity these conditions are also equivalent to \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f\). Hence convex first-order stationarity, global optimality, and proximal fixed-point stationarity coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex function, subgradient stationarity is equivalent to being a proximal fixed point for one, hence every, positive parameter.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a real Hilbert space}
f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\partial f(x)\iff x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\text{ for some, equivalently every, }\lambda>0

children.title: Nonconvex Correspondence Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of minimizer interpretations outside convex settings.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Correspondence Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal fixed point need not minimize a nonconvex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(f(t)=(t^2-1)^2\), and choose \(0<\lambda\leq1/4\). At the center \(x=0\),
\[f(t)+\frac{t^2}{2\lambda}=t^4+\left(\frac{1}{2\lambda}-2\right)t^2+1\geq1,\]
with equality at \(t=0\). Therefore \(0\in P_\lambda f(0)\), so \(0\) is a proximal fixed point. However, \(f(0)=1\), whereas \(f(1)=f(-1)=0\). Thus the convex equality between proximal fixed points and global minimizers fails without convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the double-well quartic, zero is a proximal fixed point at small parameters but is not a global minimizer.

children.title: Moreau Envelope Geometry
children.top_down_role: Value approximation, smoothing, and landscape relationships induced by Moreau regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Moreau Envelope Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex Moreau smoothing, gradient geometry, and preservation of minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\lambda>0\). Its Moreau envelope
\[e_\lambda f(x):=\inf_{y\in H}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert y-x\rVert^2\right\}\]
is finite, convex, and continuously Fréchet differentiable, with
\[\nabla e_\lambda f(x)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\left(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\right).\]
Moreover, \(e_\lambda f(x)\leq f(x)\), \(\inf e_\lambda f=\inf f\), and \(\operatorname*{argmin}e_\lambda f=\operatorname*{argmin}f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moreau regularization gives a smooth convex lower approximation whose gradient is the scaled proximal displacement and whose minimizers are unchanged.
assumptions_latex: H\text{ is a real Hilbert space}
f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Infimal-Convolution Representation and Convexity of the Moreau Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic value and convexity properties of Moreau regularization for proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, let \(\mu>0\), and let \(\omega_\mu\) be the kernel defining the Moreau envelope. Then \[M_f^\mu=f\square\omega_\mu,\] and \(M_f^\mu:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) is real-valued and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function and a positive envelope parameter, the Moreau envelope is its infimal convolution with the defining kernel; it is finite everywhere and convex.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M_f^\mu=f\square\omega_\mu,\qquad M_f^\mu:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\text{ is convex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm Proximal Map and Huber Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form proximal mapping and Moreau envelope of the Euclidean norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(f(x)=\|x\|\). For every \(x\in\mathbb E\) and \(\mu>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\mu f}(x)=\left(1-\frac{\mu}{\max\{\|x\|,\mu\}}\right)x,
\]
and
\[
M_f^\mu(x)=
\begin{cases}
\dfrac{1}{2\mu}\|x\|^2,&\|x\|\leq\mu,\\[2mm]
\|x\|-\dfrac{\mu}{2},&\|x\|>\mu.
\end{cases}
\]
Consequently, \(M_{\|\cdot\|}^\mu=H_\mu\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of the Euclidean norm is radial shrinkage. Its Moreau envelope is the Huber function: quadratic when the norm is at most mu and linear with an offset outside that region.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) be given by \(f(x)=\lVert x\rVert_1\), let \(g(t)=|t|\), and write \(H_\mu=M_g^\mu\). For every \(\mu>0\) and \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), \[M_f^\mu(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n M_g^\mu(x_i)=\sum_{i=1}^n H_\mu(x_i).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Moreau envelope of the ℓ1 norm decomposes coordinatewise into scalar absolute-value envelopes, denoted by H_mu in the extract.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Partial Moreau envelope in the first argument
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic infimal regularization of a two-argument function with respect to its first argument.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\lambda>0\), the partial Moreau envelope of \(\psi\) with respect to its first argument is
\[
e_\lambda\varphi(x):=\inf_{u\in X}\left\{\psi(u,x)+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|u-x\|^2\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For x in R^n and positive lambda, the partial Moreau envelope of psi in its first argument is the infimum over u in X of psi(u,x) plus lambda over two times the squared distance from u to x.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Moreau Envelope
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and proximal representation for a proper closed convex function on a Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(\mu>0\). For every \(x\in\mathbb E\), the Moreau envelope is
\[
M_f^\mu(x):=\min_{u\in\mathbb E}\left\{f(u)+\frac{1}{2\mu}\|x-u\|^2\right\}.
\]
The minimizer is unique and equals \(\operatorname{prox}_{\mu f}(x)\). Consequently, \(M_f^\mu(x)\in\mathbb R\) and
\[
M_f^\mu(x)=f\!\left(\operatorname{prox}_{\mu f}(x)\right)+\frac{1}{2\mu}\left\|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\mu f}(x)\right\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function and a positive smoothing parameter, the Moreau envelope at x is the minimum of the function value plus a scaled squared distance from x. Its unique minimizer is the proximal point, so the envelope is finite and has the stated proximal-value representation.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.title: Moreau Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled Hilbert-space decomposition for a proper lower-semicontinuous convex function and its Fenchel conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\gamma>0\). For every \(x\in H\), both proximal points below are uniquely defined and satisfy
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)+\gamma\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\gamma}(x/\gamma)=x.
\]
Equivalently, if \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)\), then \((x-p)/\gamma=\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\gamma}(x/\gamma)\), with \((x-p)/\gamma\in\partial f(p)\) and \(p\in\partial f^*((x-p)/\gamma)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every point splits uniquely into a proximal point of a convex function and a scaled proximal point of its Fenchel conjugate.

notation.meaning: minimizer of f(y) plus the squared distance to the input divided by 2 gamma
proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on H

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal map of the sum of the k largest components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational specialization of Moreau decomposition expressing the proximal map through Euclidean projection onto a capped simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x_{[i]}$ denote the $i$th largest component of $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Define $f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^k x_{[i]}$ and $C=\{y\in\mathbb{R}^n:e^Ty=k,\ 0\leq y\leq e\}$. Then, for every $\lambda>0$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=x-\lambda P_C(x/\lambda)$, where $P_C$ is Euclidean projection onto $C$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the function equal to the sum of the k largest components, the proximal map at any vector is the vector minus lambda times the Euclidean projection of the scaled vector onto the capped simplex whose coordinates lie between zero and one and sum to k.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support and proximal representations of the sum of the k largest absolute components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function representation of the top-k absolute-value sum and its resulting Moreau-decomposition formula using projection onto the intersection of an l1 ball and a box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, $k\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let $x_{\langle i\rangle}$ be a component of $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$ having the $i$th largest absolute value. Define $f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^k|x_{\langle i\rangle}|$ and $C=\{z\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|z\|_1\leq k,\ -e\leq z\leq e\}$. Then $f(x)=\max_{z\in C}z^Tx$ for every $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$. Consequently, for every $\lambda>0$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}^n$, $\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=x-\lambda P_C(x/\lambda)$, where $P_C$ is Euclidean projection onto $C$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The sum of the k largest absolute component values is the support function of the vectors whose l1 norm is at most k and whose coordinates lie between minus one and one. Its proximal map equals the input minus lambda times the Euclidean projection of the scaled input onto that set.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Norm–dual-ball Moreau decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialization of Moreau decomposition to a norm and the ball of its dual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\) be a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), let \(\Omega^*\) be its dual norm, and let \(\mu>0\). Define
\[
B_{\Omega^*}(\mu):=\{v\in\mathbb{R}^d:\Omega^*(v)\leq\mu\}.
\]
The dual proximal operator is the Euclidean projector onto \(B_{\Omega^*}(\mu)\), and
\[
\operatorname{Prox}_{\mu\Omega}=I_d-\operatorname{Proj}_{B_{\Omega^*}(\mu)}.
\]
Thus, for every \(u\in\mathbb{R}^d\),
\[
\operatorname{Prox}_{\mu\Omega}(u)=u-\operatorname{Proj}_{B_{\Omega^*}(\mu)}(u).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a norm Ω and positive μ, the dual proximal operator is Euclidean projection onto the radius-μ ball of the dual norm. The proximal map of μΩ equals the identity minus that projection.

children.title: Conjugate Proximal Maps
children.top_down_role: Proximal mappings organized through convex conjugacy.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugate Proximal Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computational conversion between scaled proximal maps of a convex function and its conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the Hilbert-space assumptions of Moreau decomposition, either conjugate proximal map determines the other. For every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\gamma}(x/\gamma)
=\frac{x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)}{\gamma},
\qquad
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)
=x-\gamma\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\gamma}(x/\gamma).
\]
Thus evaluation of one map supplies a dual variable in \(\partial f(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x))\) without separately solving the conjugate proximal problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of the conjugate is the scaled displacement from the proximal map of the primal function, and conversely.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Envelope Relations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled Moreau-envelope identity coupling a convex function with its Fenchel conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), define \(e_\gamma f(x)=\inf_{y\in H}\{f(y)+\|x-y\|^2/(2\gamma)\}\). Then, for every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
e_\gamma f(x)+e_{1/\gamma}f^*(x/\gamma)=\frac{\|x\|^2}{2\gamma}.
\]
Moreover, \(e_\gamma f\) is Fréchet differentiable and
\[
\nabla e_\gamma f(x)=\frac{x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)}{\gamma}
=\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\gamma}(x/\gamma).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The primal and conjugate Moreau envelopes sum to a quadratic, while the primal envelope gradient equals the conjugate proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\).

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of f with parameter gamma

children.top_down_role: Structural regimes limiting the available dual interpretations.

knowledge_statements.title: Duality Applicability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the convex Moreau decomposition when proper closed convexity is removed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The Moreau decomposition above is not valid for an arbitrary nonconvex extended-real function. On \(H=\mathbb R\), take \(f(y)=-y^2/2\) and \(\gamma=1\). For \(x\ne0\), the proximal objective is
\[
f(y)+\frac{|x-y|^2}{2}=rac{x^2}{2}-xy,
\]
which is unbounded below, so \(\operatorname{prox}_{f}(x)=\varnothing\). Its Fenchel conjugate is identically \(+\infty\), hence is not proper. Consequently neither conjugate proximal evaluation nor the primal–dual decomposition is defined. Proper lower-semicontinuous convexity, or assumptions ensuring analogous resolvent identities, is therefore essential.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without convexity and properness, proximal points or the conjugate can cease to exist, so Moreau’s primal–dual decomposition need not be meaningful.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{f}(x)=\varnothing\) and \(f^*\equiv+\infty\), so the convex Moreau decomposition is inapplicable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is algebraically sound, but it has no cited authoritative source. In addition, the proximal-objective display contains the malformed text '=rac{x^2}{2}-xy', which must be repaired to '\(=x^2/2-xy\)' when a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Proximal Displacement Residuals
children.top_down_role: Residual interfaces derived from displacement under proximal evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Displacement Residuals
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual and envelope-gradient interfaces obtained from displacement under exact proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)\) and define the proximal displacement residual by \(r_\gamma(x)=(x-p)/\gamma\). Proximal optimality gives
\[
r_\gamma(x)\in\partial f(p),
\qquad
x-p=\gamma r_\gamma(x).
\]
Furthermore, \(r_\gamma(x)=\nabla e_\gamma f(x)\). Hence \(r_\gamma(x)=0\) if and only if \(x=p\), equivalently \(0\in\partial f(x)\); in that case \(x\) minimizes \(f\). The norm \(\|r_\gamma(x)\|\) is therefore a stationarity residual measured at the proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The scaled proximal displacement is both a subgradient at the proximal point and the Moreau-envelope gradient; it vanishes exactly at minimizers.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\).

children.title: Exact Proximal Oracles
children.top_down_role: Interfaces returning exact proximal evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Proximal Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic oracle returning the unique exact minimizer of a convex proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), an exact proximal oracle is a mapping \(\mathcal O_f:H\times(0,\infty)\to H\) satisfying, for every query \((x,\gamma)\),
\[
\mathcal O_f(x,\gamma)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in H}
\left\{f(z)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|z-x\|^2\right\}
=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x).
\]
Equivalently, its output \(z\) satisfies the verifiable optimality inclusion \(0\in\partial f(z)+(z-x)/\gamma\). Exactness means zero proximal-objective gap and zero optimality-inclusion error; it does not prescribe how the oracle computes \(z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact proximal oracle returns the unique minimizer of every queried convex proximal subproblem, equivalently a point satisfying its optimality inclusion exactly.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\).

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-gap model for deterministic inexact solution of a convex proximal subproblem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix a tolerance rule \(\varepsilon:H\times(0,\infty)\to[0,+\infty)\). An objective-gap inexact proximal oracle for \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\) returns \(z=\mathcal O_f^\varepsilon(x,\gamma)\) such that
\[
f(z)+\frac{\|z-x\|^2}{2\gamma}
\le
\inf_{y\in H}\left\{f(y)+\frac{\|y-x\|^2}{2\gamma}\right\}
+\varepsilon(x,\gamma).
\]
The exact oracle is recovered when \(\varepsilon(x,\gamma)=0\). Because the proximal objective is \(1/\gamma\)-strongly convex, this condition implies \(\|z-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)\|\le\sqrt{2\gamma\varepsilon(x,\gamma)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An inexact proximal oracle returns a point whose proximal-objective value is within a prescribed tolerance, which also bounds its distance from the exact proximal point.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\).

children.title: Oracle Accuracy Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Accuracy information exposed to outer methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Accuracy Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Three explicit interfaces for reporting error in a convex proximal-oracle response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a response \(z\) to query \((x,\gamma)\), common accuracy interfaces are: objective gap \(\Phi_{x,\gamma}(z)-\inf\Phi_{x,\gamma}\le\varepsilon\); point error \(\|z-p\|\le\delta\), where \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)\); and inclusion residual, requiring some \(v\in\partial f(z)\) with \(\|x-z-\gamma v\|\le\eta\). Here \(\Phi_{x,\gamma}(y)=f(y)+\|y-x\|^2/(2\gamma)\). Strong convexity always converts the objective interface to the point interface via
\[
\delta\le\sqrt{2\gamma\varepsilon}.
\]
Conversions in the reverse direction require additional regularity or computable bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proximal-oracle error may be reported by objective gap, distance to the exact point, or an optimality-inclusion residual; objective gap controls point error.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space, \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), and \(\gamma>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The three interfaces and the objective-gap-to-point-error implication are plausible and correctly formulated, but no source with a specific locator supports the taxonomy or the stated reverse-conversion boundary.

children.title: Uncontrolled Oracle Error Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure boundary for approximation without usable error control.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncontrolled Oracle Error Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent unregulated proximal-oracle errors can destroy convergence even for a trivial convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the inexact proximal-point update \(x_{k+1}=\widetilde{\operatorname{prox}}_{\gamma f}(x_k)\) on \(H=\mathbb R\) with \(f\equiv0\) and fixed \(\gamma>0\). The exact proximal map is the identity. If the oracle instead returns
\[
\widetilde{\operatorname{prox}}_{\gamma f}(x_k)=x_k+e_k
\]
with the uncontrolled error \(e_k=1\), then \(x_k=x_0+k\), so the iterates diverge although every point minimizes \(f\). Thus convergence guarantees cannot follow from merely labeling an oracle inexact; they require quantitative error control such as summability, decay, relative accuracy, or an algorithm-specific stochastic condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constant additive oracle error makes proximal-point iterates drift without bound, showing that an unspecified inexactness label gives no convergence guarantee.

notation.meaning: additive proximal-oracle error at iteration k

children.title: Stochastic Proximal Oracles
children.top_down_role: Sample-dependent and expectation-based proximal access.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Proximal Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Measurable sample-dependent proximal access for random convex integrands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((\Xi,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)\) be a probability space, let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, and suppose \(f_\xi\in\Gamma_0(H)\) for almost every \(\xi\). A sample-dependent stochastic proximal oracle is a measurable mapping \(\mathcal O:H\times(0,\infty)\times\Xi\to H\) satisfying, for every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\mathcal O(x,\gamma,\xi)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_\xi}(x)
\quad\text{almost surely}.
\]
A call draws or receives \(\xi\) and returns this random proximal point. If the pointwise expected function \(\bar f(y)=\mathbb E[f_\xi(y)]\) is well-defined and belongs to \(\Gamma_0(H)\), and the displayed proximal-point expectation exists, there is in general no identity
\[
\mathbb E[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_\xi}(x)]
=
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\bar f}(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic proximal oracle returns the proximal point of a sampled convex function. Even when the expected function and the relevant expectations are well-defined, averaging sampled proximal points generally differs from proximal evaluation of the expected function.
assumptions_latex: \((\Xi,\mathcal A,\mathbb P)\) is a probability space and \(H\) is a real Hilbert space.
\(f_\xi\in\Gamma_0(H)\) almost surely, and \(\mathcal O\) is measurable.
For the expectation comparison, \(\bar f(y)=\mathbb E[f_\xi(y)]\) is well-defined, \(\bar f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), and \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_\xi}(x)]\) exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal O(x,\gamma,\xi)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_\xi}(x)\) almost surely; in general, \(\mathbb E[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_\xi}(x)]\ne\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\bar f}(x)\).

children.title: Structured Proximal Oracles
children.top_down_role: Proximal access supported by separability, projection, thresholding, or spectral structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Structured Proximal Oracles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal evaluation reduced to simpler operations by algebraic or spectral structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A structured proximal oracle represents \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}\) through simpler exact primitives. Canonical instances are
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\sum_i f_i}(x_1,\ldots,x_m)
=(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_i}(x_i))_{i=1}^m
\]
when the Hilbert space and function are block-separable; \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\iota_C}=P_C\) for a nonempty closed convex set \(C\); and entrywise soft thresholding for \(f(x)=\lambda\|x\|_1\). For unitarily invariant matrix functions, proximal evaluation reduces to applying the associated symmetric proximal map to singular values and restoring the singular vectors. Each representation requires its stated separability, set, or invariance structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured proximal oracles exploit separability, projections, thresholding, or spectral invariance to reduce a proximal problem to simpler exact primitives.
assumptions_latex: Each component function is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on its stated Hilbert space.
Projection sets are nonempty, closed, and convex.
Spectral formulas are used only for the corresponding unitarily invariant convex function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The proximal map is computable by the displayed componentwise, projection, thresholding, or spectral primitive whenever its structural hypotheses hold.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation role fits the structured-oracle topic, but no authoritative locator supports the collection of separable, projection, thresholding, and spectral formulas. The broad spectral assertion particularly requires a precise theorem or section reference.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constant-shift invariance for the scalar cardinality proximal operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialized constant-shift invariance for the scalar functions used by the hard-thresholding oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I,J:\mathbb R\to(-\infty,\infty]\) satisfy \(I(t)=J(t)+\lambda\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\). Then, for every \(s\in\mathbb R\), \[\operatorname{prox}_I(s)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in\mathbb R}\left\{I(t)+\tfrac12(t-s)^2\right\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{t\in\mathbb R}\left\{J(t)+\tfrac12(t-s)^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_J(s).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the scalar cardinality functions I and J, adding the constant lambda does not change the proximal minimizers, so their proximal operators agree at every scalar input.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar shrinkage map for a nonnegative threshold; the threshold domain is implicit in the displayed equivalent formulas rather than stated separately in the extract.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a threshold $\lambda\ge 0$, define $\mathcal T_\lambda:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ by $$\mathcal T_\lambda(y)=[|y|-\lambda]_+\operatorname{sgn}(y)=\begin{cases}y-\lambda,&y\ge\lambda,\\0,&|y|<\lambda,\\y+\lambda,&y\le-\lambda.\end{cases}$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft thresholding reduces an input's magnitude by the nonnegative threshold when the magnitude reaches that threshold and maps smaller magnitudes to zero.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Blockwise proximal mapping of the second odd–even TV term
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The displayed definition and concluding formula determine the pairs (2i,2i+1); the conflicting prose description and malformed expanded expression are omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(n\ge 2\), \(\lambda>0\), \(h(u,v)=|u-v|\), and
\[
g_2(\mathbf x)=\lambda\sum_{i=1}^{\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor}|x_{2i}-x_{2i+1}|.
\]
Then, for every \(\mathbf x\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(i=1,\ldots,\lfloor (n-1)/2\rfloor\),
\[
\bigl((\operatorname{prox}_{g_2}(\mathbf x))_{2i},(\operatorname{prox}_{g_2}(\mathbf x))_{2i+1}\bigr)
=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda h}(x_{2i},x_{2i+1}).
\]
Every coordinate outside these disjoint pairs is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because g2 is a sum of terms on disjoint coordinate pairs, its proximal mapping applies the two-variable proximal mapping of lambda times |u-v| independently to (2,3), (4,5), and so on. Coordinates outside those pairs are unchanged.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Operator of a Separable Function
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space proximal calculus for a function separable across Euclidean factors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\mathbb E_1,\ldots,\mathbb E_m$ be Euclidean spaces and let $f:\mathbb E_1\times\cdots\times\mathbb E_m\to(-\infty,\infty]$ satisfy $f(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)$. Then, for every $(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in\mathbb E_1\times\cdots\times\mathbb E_m$, $$\operatorname{prox}_f(x_1,\ldots,x_m)=\operatorname{prox}_{f_1}(x_1)\times\cdots\times\operatorname{prox}_{f_m}(x_m).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal operator of a function separable across product-space factors is the Cartesian product of the component proximal operators.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Map of a Separable Logarithmic Barrier
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form coordinatewise proximal evaluation for the positive-orthant logarithmic barrier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $\lambda>0$ and define $g:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]$ by $$g(x)=\begin{cases}-\lambda\sum_{j=1}^n\log x_j,&x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n,\\+\infty,&x\notin\mathbb R_{++}^n.\end{cases}$$ Equivalently, $g(x)=\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi(x_j)$, where $\varphi(t)=-\lambda\log t$ for $t>0$ and $\varphi(t)=+\infty$ otherwise. Then, for every $x\in\mathbb R^n$, $$\operatorname{prox}_g(x)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_\varphi(x_j)\bigr)_{j=1}^n=\left(\frac{x_j+\sqrt{x_j^2+4\lambda}}{2}\right)_{j=1}^n.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of the scaled logarithmic barrier on the positive orthant is coordinatewise, with output coordinate equal to one half of the input coordinate plus the square root of its square plus four lambda.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cardinality penalty and its hard-thresholding proximal oracle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable scalar representation of the cardinality penalty and the set-valued proximal evaluation of its constant-shifted component.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda>0\), define \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\) by \(f(x)=\lambda\|x\|_0\), and set \[I(t)=\begin{cases}\lambda,&t\ne0,\\0,&t=0,\end{cases}\qquad J(t)=\begin{cases}0,&t\ne0,\\-\lambda,&t=0.\end{cases}\] Then \[f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n I(x_i)\quad\text{for every }x\in\mathbb R^n,\qquad I=J+\lambda,\] and \[\operatorname{prox}_J(s)=\mathcal H_{\sqrt{2\lambda}}(s)\quad\text{for every }s\in\mathbb R.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The cardinality penalty separates into scalar zero-versus-nonzero penalties. Subtracting lambda produces the scalar function J, whose proximal operator is hard thresholding at square root of twice lambda, including the set-valued equality case inherited from the hard-thresholding definition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall x\in\mathbb R^n,\ f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n I(x_i),\qquad I=J+\lambda,\qquad \forall s\in\mathbb R,\ \operatorname{prox}_J(s)=\mathcal H_{\sqrt{2\lambda}}(s)

children.title: Proximal Evaluation Calculus
children.top_down_role: Reusable transformations and structures for evaluating proximal maps.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection onto a Convex Sublevel Set via a Proximal Operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents Euclidean projection onto a nonempty convex sublevel set through a scalar proximal parameter; strict feasibility is included to exclude degenerate level sets for which no finite multiplier need exist.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbf R^n\to\mathbf R\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex, and let \(\mathcal S=\{x\mid f(x)\le t\}\) satisfy \(\inf f<t\). If \(v\in\mathcal S\), then \(\Pi_{\mathcal S}(v)=v\). If \(v\notin\mathcal S\), then there exist \(x=\Pi_{\mathcal S}(v)\) and \(\lambda>0\) such that \(0\in x-v+\lambda\partial f(x)\) and \(f(x)=t\). Hence \(x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(v)\), with \(f(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(v))=t\). The latter quantity is nonincreasing in \(\lambda\), permitting scalar bracketing and bisection for a suitable parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex function and a strictly feasible sublevel threshold, a point inside the sublevel set projects to itself. An exterior point projects to a boundary point that is a proximal evaluation of the function for some positive parameter. That parameter can be located by scalar bracketing and bisection because the attained function value is nonincreasing with the parameter.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbf R^n\to\mathbf R\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: v\in\mathcal S\Rightarrow\Pi_{\mathcal S}(v)=v;\qquad v\notin\mathcal S\Rightarrow\exists\lambda>0:\ \Pi_{\mathcal S}(v)=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(v),\quad f(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(v))=t.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Proximal Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise factorization of a proximal map on a Hilbert direct sum.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H_1\oplus\cdots\oplus H_m\) with product norm \(\|x\|^2=\sum_{i=1}^m\|x_i\|^2\), and let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\), where \(f_i\in\Gamma_0(H_i)\). Then for every \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\), the proximal objective separates into independent component objectives and
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)
=igl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_1}(x_1),\ldots,
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_m}(x_m)\bigr).
\]
Thus the full proximal evaluation may be performed independently and in parallel across components.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a sum of functions on independent product-space coordinates, the proximal map is exactly the tuple of the component proximal maps.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\bigoplus_{i=1}^m H_i\) has the standard product norm.

notation.meaning: finite Hilbert direct sum with product norm
convex function acting only on component i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The separable proximal formula is standard and the property content kind is appropriate, but no source is cited. Its displayed tuple also contains the malformed text '=igl(' instead of '\(=\bigl(\)', which must be corrected in a sourced replacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Blockwise Proximal Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate representation for a separable convex function on a finite product Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=H_1\times\cdots\times H_m\) have product norm, let \(f_i:H_i\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex, and define \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\). For every \(\gamma>0\) and \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\in H\), the proximal minimization separates into independent block problems, and
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_1}(x_1),\ldots,\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_m}(x_m)\bigr).
\]
Thus all block proximal mappings may be evaluated independently, including concurrently, without altering the exact proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a sum of independent block functions is obtained by applying each block’s proximal map independently.
assumptions_latex: \(H=\prod_{i=1}^m H_i\) is a finite product Hilbert space.

notation.meaning: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on the Hilbert space H.
Unique minimizer of f(u) plus the squared distance from u to the input divided by twice gamma.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Block Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact selected-block proximal update for a separable function; unselected blocks remain unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x=(x_i)_{i=1}^m\), a nonempty selected set \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,m\}\), stepsize \(\gamma>0\), and \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m f_i(x_i)\), initialize \(y=x\) and evaluate
\[
y_i=\begin{cases}\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_i}(x_i),&i\in S,\\x_i,&i\notin S.\end{cases}
\]
Return \(y=P_S^\gamma x\). The output equals the full proximal point only when every block requiring a nontrivial change is selected; otherwise it is a partial block operator suitable for block-coordinate schemes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply proximal updates only to selected blocks and copy every unselected block unchanged; this generally differs from a full proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((P_S^\gamma x)_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f_i}(x_i)\) for \(i\in S\), and \((P_S^\gamma x)_i=x_i\) otherwise.

notation.meaning: Set of blocks selected for evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Cross-Block Coupling Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coupled quadratic demonstrates why coordinatewise proximal evaluation requires separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb R^2\), set \(f(u,v)=\tfrac12(u-v)^2\). For \(\gamma>0\) and \(x=(x_1,x_2)\), direct minimization gives
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=\frac{1}{1+2\gamma}\bigl((1+\gamma)x_1+\gamma x_2,\;\gamma x_1+(1+\gamma)x_2\bigr).
\]
Each output block depends on both input blocks. Hence a cross-block term destroys independent blockwise evaluation, even though the coupled proximal problem remains convex and has a unique solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A quadratic coupling makes each proximal output depend on both inputs, so independent block evaluation is no longer exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)_1\) depends on \(x_2\), and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)_2\) depends on \(x_1\).

knowledge_statements.title: Projection-Based Proximal Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identification of a metric projection as the proximal map of a closed convex-set indicator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\) be a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space \(H\), and let \(\delta_C\) be its convex indicator. For every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}(x)=\underset{u\in H}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left\{\delta_C(u)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\lVert u-x\rVert^2\right\}=\underset{u\in C}{\operatorname{argmin}}\,\lVert u-x\rVert^2=P_Cx.
\]
The result is independent of the positive value of \(\gamma\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map of a closed convex-set indicator is exactly the metric projection onto that set, independently of the positive stepsize.
assumptions_latex: \(C\subseteq H\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.

notation.meaning: Zero on C and positive infinity outside C.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection onto the nonnegative orthant
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form Euclidean projection used in projection-based proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every $v\in\mathbb{R}^n$, the Euclidean projection onto $\mathbb{R}_+^n$ is
\[
\Pi_{\mathbb{R}_+^n}(v)=v_+,
\qquad (v_+)_i=\max\{v_i,0\}.
\]
Thus each negative component is replaced by zero and each nonnegative component is unchanged.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Euclidean projection of a real vector onto the nonnegative orthant replaces every negative component by zero and leaves every nonnegative component unchanged.

knowledge_statements.title: Thresholding-Based Proximal Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinatewise soft-thresholding representation of the finite-dimensional ℓ1 proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=\lambda\lVert x\rVert_1\) on \(\mathbb R^n\), with \(\lambda\ge 0\) and \(\gamma>0\), the proximal problem separates by coordinates and
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)\bigr)_j=\operatorname{sign}(x_j)\max\{|x_j|-\gamma\lambda,0\},\qquad j=1,\ldots,n.
\]
Thus entries with magnitude at most \(\gamma\lambda\) are set to zero, while every other magnitude is reduced by \(\gamma\lambda\) without changing its sign.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The ℓ1 proximal map soft-thresholds each coordinate: small entries become zero and larger entries shrink toward zero by the threshold.

notation.meaning: Positive part, equal to the maximum of t and zero.
Scalar sign function, with sign of zero equal to zero.

knowledge_statements.title: Indicator-Function Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent projection, normal-cone resolvent, and indicator-proximal interfaces for convex constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a nonempty closed convex set \(C\) in a real Hilbert space, its indicator satisfies \(\partial\delta_C=N_C\). Consequently, for every \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}=(I+\gamma\partial\delta_C)^{-1}=(I+\gamma N_C)^{-1}=P_C.
\]
Moreover, \(p=P_Cx\) is equivalently certified by
\[
p\in C\quad\text{and}\quad x-p\in N_C(p),
\]
which is also equivalent to \(\langle x-p,z-p\rangle\le0\) for every \(z\in C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex constraint can be accessed interchangeably through its indicator proximal map, metric projection, or normal-cone resolvent.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is a nonempty closed convex subset of a real Hilbert space.

notation.meaning: Resolvent of the scaled normal-cone operator.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal Mapping of an Indicator as Metric Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is a set-valued identity requiring only nonemptiness of the set. Without closedness or convexity, the common minimizer set may be empty or non-singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb E\) be nonempty and let \(g=\delta_C\). For every \(x\in\mathbb E\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{g}(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\mathbb E}\left\{\delta_C(u)+\tfrac12\lVert u-x\rVert^2\right\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in C}\lVert u-x\rVert^2=P_C(x).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every point, the proximal mapping of a nonempty set's indicator is the set of nearest points in that set.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)\bigr)_{G_g}=\left(1-\gamma\lambda w_g/\lVert x_{G_g}\rVert_2\right)_+x_{G_g}\) for \(g=1,\ldots,m\), with the value defined as zero when \(x_{G_g}=0\).

notation.meaning: Subvector of x indexed by group G_g.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block soft-thresholding interface for a disjoint-group ℓ2,1 penalty.

source_refs.locator: 6.2 First Set of Examples of Proximal Mappings p. 131

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) partition \(\{1,\ldots,n\}\), let \(w_g>0\), and define \(f(x)=\lambda\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\lVert x_{G_g}\rVert_2\) with \(\lambda\ge0\). For \(\gamma>0\), each group is evaluated independently by
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)\bigr)_{G_g}=\left(1-\frac{\gamma\lambda w_g}{\lVert x_{G_g}\rVert_2}\right)_+x_{G_g},\qquad g=1,\ldots,m,
\]
where the displayed value is defined as zero when \(x_{G_g}=0\). Entire groups whose norms do not exceed their thresholds are therefore removed together.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a disjoint-group penalty on a vector in R^n, the proximal map independently shrinks each group radially and sets the whole group to zero when its norm does not exceed its threshold.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection onto the positive semidefinite cone
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Spectral evaluation of the Frobenius-norm projection onto the positive semidefinite cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $V\in\mathbb S^n$ have an orthonormal eigendecomposition
\[
V=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i u_i u_i^T.
\]
Its Frobenius-norm projection onto $\mathbb S_+^n$ is
\[
\Pi_{\mathbb S_+^n}(V)=\sum_{i=1}^n(\lambda_i)_+u_i u_i^T,
\qquad (\lambda_i)_+=\max\{\lambda_i,0\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To project a symmetric matrix onto the positive semidefinite cone, retain its eigenvectors and replace each negative eigenvalue by zero.
assumptions_latex: V=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i u_i u_i^T\text{ is an orthonormal eigendecomposition}

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Proximal Evaluation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of a unitarily invariant matrix proximal problem to a proximal problem on singular values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(X)=\phi(\sigma(X))\) on \(\mathbb R^{p\times q}\), where \(\phi\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and absolutely symmetric. If \(X=U\operatorname{Diag}(s)V^{\mathsf T}\) is a singular-value decomposition with \(s=\sigma(X)\), then for every \(\gamma>0\),
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(X)=U\operatorname{Diag}\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(s)\bigr)V^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Thus the matrix proximal evaluation preserves a compatible pair of singular-vector factors and reduces the nonlinear computation to the singular-value vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A unitarily invariant convex matrix function is proximally evaluated by applying its scalar spectral proximal map to the singular values.

notation.meaning: Vector of singular values of X in nonincreasing order.
Rectangular diagonal matrix with diagonal vector s.

knowledge_statements.title: Eigenvalue-Based Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eigenvalue reduction for proximal mappings of orthogonally invariant convex functions on symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathbb S^n\) carry the Frobenius norm, and let \(f(X)=\phi(\lambda(X))\), where \(\phi:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, convex, and permutation invariant. If \(X=Q\operatorname{Diag}(d)Q^{\mathsf T}\) with \(d=\lambda(X)\), then
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(X)=Q\operatorname{Diag}\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\phi}(d)\bigr)Q^{\mathsf T},\qquad \gamma>0.
\]
Hence evaluation reduces to the eigenvalue vector while retaining an eigenbasis compatible with the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an orthogonally invariant convex function of a symmetric matrix, evaluate the vector proximal map on eigenvalues and reconstruct in the same eigenbasis.

notation.meaning: Real symmetric n by n matrices.
Eigenvalue vector of X in a fixed monotone order.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Eigenvalue reduction for spectral proximal maps and projections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex spectral functions and symmetric convex spectral sets on real symmetric matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb S^n\to\mathbb R\) satisfy \(F(UXU^T)=F(X)\) for all \(X\in\mathbb S^n\) and orthogonal \(U\). Then \(F=f\circ\sigma\) for a symmetric \(f:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\), where \(\sigma(X)\) lists the eigenvalues in nonincreasing order. If \(F\) is convex, \(\lambda>0\), and \(A=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma(A))U^T\), then \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda F}(A)=U\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(\sigma(A)))U^T\). If \(S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is symmetric, then \(T=\sigma^{-1}(S)\) is convex if and only if \(S\) is convex; when \(S\) is convex, \(\Pi_T(A)=U\operatorname{diag}(\Pi_S(\sigma(A)))U^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A spectral function of a symmetric matrix is a symmetric function of its eigenvalues. For a convex spectral function, its proximal map is computed by applying the vector proximal map to the eigenvalues and restoring the eigenvectors. Likewise, projection onto a symmetric convex spectral set reduces to projection of the eigenvalue vector.
assumptions_latex: F\text{ convex and }\lambda>0\text{ for the proximal formula}
S\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ symmetric; }S\text{ convex for the projection formula}

children.top_down_role: Proximal evaluation for singular-value structured functions.

knowledge_statements.title: Singular-Value-Based Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value thresholding interface for the nuclear-norm proximal mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\in\mathbb R^{p\times q}\) have singular-value decomposition \(X=U\operatorname{Diag}(s)V^{\mathsf T}\). For \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(\gamma>0\), the nuclear-norm proximal mapping is
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\lambda\lVert\cdot\rVert_*}(X)=U\operatorname{Diag}\bigl((s_i-\gamma\lambda)_+\bigr)V^{\mathsf T}.
\]
Therefore singular values not exceeding \(\gamma\lambda\) are deleted, the remaining singular values are reduced by that threshold, and compatible left and right singular vectors are retained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nuclear-norm proximal map soft-thresholds singular values and reconstructs the matrix using compatible singular vectors.

notation.meaning: Nuclear norm, equal to the sum of singular values.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Ky Fan norm proximal reduction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition and singular-value reduction for the Ky Fan k-norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(1\le k\le\min\{m,n\}\), the Ky Fan \(k\)-norm is \(\|A\|_{(k)}=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_i(A)\), where the singular values are ordered nonincreasingly. Let \(g(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{k}|x|_{[i]}\), where \(|x|_{[i]}\) denotes the \(i\)-th largest absolute coordinate. If \(A=P\operatorname{diag}(\sigma_s(A))Q^T\) is an SVD and \(\lambda>0\), then \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\|\cdot\|_{(k)}}(A)=P\operatorname{diag}(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}(\sigma_s(A)))Q^T\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Ky Fan k-norm is the sum of the k largest singular values. Its proximal operator is evaluated by applying the vector proximal operator for the sum of the k largest absolute coordinates to the singular-value vector and then restoring the singular vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonspectral Matrix Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A coordinate-dependent matrix function shows where singular-value-only proximal reduction fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb R^{2\times2}\), let \(f(X)=\tfrac12X_{11}^2\). Its proximal map scales only the first entry:
\[
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(X)\bigr)_{11}=\frac{X_{11}}{1+\gamma},\qquad
\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(X)\bigr)_{ij}=X_{ij}\ \text{for}\ (i,j)\ne(1,1).
\]
For the all-ones rank-one matrix, the output has determinant \(-\gamma/(1+\gamma)\ne0\). It therefore cannot arise merely by transforming the input’s single nonzero singular value while retaining its singular vectors. Coordinate dependence lies outside the spectral proximal interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalty on one matrix entry can change rank and singular vectors, so singular-value-only proximal evaluation is not valid for nonspectral functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) does not admit the singular-vector-preserving proximal representation applicable to unitarily invariant functions.

notation.meaning: Entry in row i and column j of X.

knowledge_statements.title: Conjugacy Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau decomposition reducing a proximal evaluation to the proximal map of the Fenchel conjugate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\), and let \(f^*\) denote its Fenchel conjugate. For every \(x\in H\) and \(\gamma>0\), Moreau’s decomposition states
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)+\gamma\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\gamma}(x/\gamma)=x.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma f}(x)=x-\gamma\operatorname{prox}_{f^*/\gamma}(x/\gamma).
\]
Thus an available proximal routine for the scaled conjugate provides an exact evaluation of the original proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Moreau decomposition computes a function’s proximal map from the proximal map of its scaled Fenchel conjugate.

notation.meaning: Function mapping y to f star of y divided by gamma.

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scalar input and objective scaling identities for convex proximal mappings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(\gamma>0\). For every \(a\in\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\}\) and \(x\in H\), input scaling reduces according to \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(f\circ(aI))}(x)=a^{-1}\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma a^{2}f}(ax).\] Moreover, for every \(c>0\), objective scaling is absorbed into the proximal parameter: \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(cf)}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{(\gamma c)f}(x).\] Thus scaling preserves proximal evaluability when the resulting parameterized proximal map of \(f\) is available.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Scaling the argument transforms the proximal input and parameter; multiplying the objective by a positive scalar only rescales the proximal parameter.

notation.meaning: Proper lower-semicontinuous convex functions on the Hilbert space.
The minimizer of the function value plus squared distance divided by twice the parameter.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine-Composition Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tight-frame affine-composition rule for proximal evaluation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) and \(G\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(g\in\Gamma_0(G)\), let \(L:H\to G\) be bounded and linear, and suppose \(LL^*=\kappa I_G\) for some \(\kappa>0\). For \(b\in G\), \(\gamma>0\), and \(x\in H\), the affine-composition proximal map satisfies \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma(g\circ(L\cdot+b))}(x)=x+\kappa^{-1}L^*\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{\kappa\gamma g}(Lx+b)-(Lx+b)\bigr).\] Hence one evaluation of the proximal map of \(g\), together with applications of \(L\) and \(L^*\), evaluates the composite proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight-frame affine composition has an explicit proximal formula using one proximal evaluation of the outer function and applications of the linear map and its adjoint.

notation.meaning: Hilbert-space adjoint of the bounded linear map.
Positive tight-frame constant satisfying the stated coisometry relation.

knowledge_statements.title: Reduction Applicability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the tight-frame affine reduction without the coisometry condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The affine-composition formula requiring \(LL^*=\kappa I\) does not extend to arbitrary linear maps by inserting a scalar \(\kappa\). In \(H=G=\mathbb{R}^2\), take \(L=\operatorname{diag}(1,2)\), \(g(z)=\tfrac12\lVert z\rVert^2\), and \(\gamma=1\). Then \[\operatorname{prox}_{g\circ L}(x)=(I+L^*L)^{-1}x=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,1/5)x.\] The tight-frame expression with \(\kappa=1\) instead gives \[x+L^*(\operatorname{prox}_{g}(Lx)-Lx)=\operatorname{diag}(1/2,-1)x,\] which differs from the true proximal map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Without the tight-frame identity, the scalar affine-composition reduction can fail; a diagonal linear map and quadratic outer function give an explicit mismatch.

notation.meaning: Diagonal linear operator with diagonal entries shown.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantified descent and implicit-subgradient identity for exact proximal-point steps
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Quantified descent and implicit-subgradient identity for exact proximal-point steps
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n, and let \eta_t>0. For the exact proximal-point update x^{t+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta_t f}(x^t), one has \[f(x^{t+1})\leq f(x^t)-\frac{1}{2\eta_t}\|x^{t+1}-x^t\|^2,\qquad x^{t+1}-x^t\in-\eta_t\partial f(x^{t+1}).\] Consequently, f(x^{t+1})<f(x^t) whenever x^{t+1}\neq x^t.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every exact proximal-point step for a proper closed convex objective satisfies a quantified objective decrease and is an implicit subgradient step. The objective decreases strictly whenever the iterate changes.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x^{t+1})\leq f(x^t)-\frac{\|x^{t+1}-x^t\|^2}{2\eta_t},\qquad x^{t+1}-x^t\in-\eta_t\partial f(x^{t+1}),\qquad x^{t+1}\neq x^t\Longrightarrow f(x^{t+1})<f(x^t).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Firm nonexpansiveness and fixed-point characterization of exact proximal minimizers
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and fix \eta>0. The proximal map \operatorname{prox}_{\eta f} is firmly nonexpansive, and its fixed points are exactly the minimizers of f: \[x=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta f}(x)\iff 0\in\partial f(x)\iff x\in\operatorname*{argmin}f.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For each fixed positive proximal parameter, the proximal map is firmly nonexpansive, and a point is unchanged by a proximal step exactly when it minimizes the convex objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected outer-iteration displacement and inner-solution error bounds for randomized accelerated proximal point
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected outer-iteration displacement and inner-solution error bounds for randomized accelerated proximal point
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=6(5+2L/\mu), let s\geq\left\lceil-\log(7M/6)/\log\alpha\right\rceil, let \bar x^1,\ldots,\bar x^k be generated by Algorithm 6.8, and let \widehat\ell be randomly selected from [k]. If x^* solves (6.6.1) and x_*^\ell solves the \ell-th subproblem (6.6.7), then, with \Delta_0=f(\bar x^0)-f(x^*), \[\mathbb E\|x_*^{\widehat\ell}-\bar x^{\widehat\ell-1}\|^2\leq\frac{4(1-M\alpha^s)}{k\mu(6-7M\alpha^s)}\Delta_0,\] and \[\mathbb E\|x_*^{\widehat\ell}-\bar x^{\widehat\ell}\|^2\leq\frac{2M\alpha^s}{3k\mu(6-7M\alpha^s)}\Delta_0.\]

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f\in\Gamma_0(H)\) have a nonempty minimizer set. For every \(x\in H\), convex optimality gives \[x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in H}f(z)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad 0\in\partial f(x).\] Given \(x^k\in H\) and \(\gamma_k>0\), the proximal-point subproblem is \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{2\gamma_k}\lVert x-x^k\rVert^2\right\}=\bigl(I+\gamma_k\partial f\bigr)^{-1}(x^k).\] The quadratic regularization makes the subproblem strongly convex, so its minimizer is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point minimizes the convex objective exactly when its subdifferential contains zero. A proximal-point step uniquely minimizes the objective plus a quadratic centered at the current iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone with \(\operatorname{zer}A\ne\varnothing\). The operator problem is to find \(x^\star\in H\) satisfying \[0\in A(x^\star).\] For \(\gamma_k>0\), the proximal-point step is the resolvent evaluation \[x^{k+1}=J_{\gamma_kA}(x^k):=(I+\gamma_kA)^{-1}(x^k),\] equivalently \[\frac{x^k-x^{k+1}}{\gamma_k}\in A(x^{k+1}).\] Maximal monotonicity ensures that the resolvent is everywhere defined and single-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The general proximal-point problem finds a zero of a maximal-monotone operator, using its single-valued resolvent at each iteration.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(b\in Y\). For the problem \[\min_{x\in X} f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=b,\] define the concave dual function by \[d(y)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl\{f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\bigr\},\qquad y\in Y.\] Suppose the primal problem is feasible, strong duality holds, and the dual solution set is nonempty. For \(y^k\in Y\) and \(\rho_k>0\), the dual proximal-point step is \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmax}_{y\in Y}\left\{d(y)-\frac{1}{2\rho_k}\lVert y-y^k\rVert^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, \[y^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\rho_k(-d)}(y^k)=(I+\rho_k\partial(-d))^{-1}(y^k).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional equality-constrained convex problem with strong duality and a dual solution, maximizing the dual function with a quadratic proximal term is a proximal-point step for the convex function given by the negative dual objective.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(b\in Y\). Define \[\mathcal{L}_{\rho}(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2.\] Assume strong duality, existence of a dual solution, and attainment of each augmented-Lagrangian subproblem below. Given \(y^0\in Y\) and positive parameters \((\rho_k)\), compute for \(k=0,1,\ldots\) \[x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\mathcal{L}_{\rho_k}(x,y^k),\qquad y^{k+1}=y^k+\rho_k(Ax^{k+1}-b).\] With exact primal minimization, the multiplier update is the proximal-point update for the concave dual problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite-dimensional equality-constrained convex problem, the exact method of multipliers minimizes the augmented Lagrangian and then adds the scaled constraint residual to the multiplier. Under strong duality and attainment, this realizes a dual proximal-point step.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) and \(Y\) be finite-dimensional real Hilbert spaces, let \(f\in\Gamma_0(X)\), let \(A:X\to Y\) be linear, and let \(b\in Y\). Define \[d(u)=\inf_{x\in X}\bigl\{f(x)+\langle u,Ax-b\rangle\bigr\}\] and \[\mathcal{L}_\rho(x,y)=f(x)+\langle y,Ax-b\rangle+\frac{\rho}{2}\lVert Ax-b\rVert^2.\] Suppose there exists \(\bar x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) with \(A\bar x=b\), let \(\rho>0\), and assume the augmented-Lagrangian minimum is attained at \(x_\rho(y)\). Then \[\inf_{x\in X}\mathcal{L}_\rho(x,y)=\sup_{u\in Y}\left\{d(u)-\frac{1}{2\rho}\lVert u-y\rVert^2\right\},\] and a maximizing dual variable is \[u_\rho(y)=y+\rho(Ax_\rho(y)-b).\] Thus the minimized augmented Lagrangian is the concave Moreau envelope of \(d\), and the residual update evaluates the proximal map of \(-d\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under a finite-dimensional relative-interior qualification and attainment of the augmented-Lagrangian subproblem, its minimized value is the concave Moreau envelope of the dual function, and the residual multiplier update is the corresponding dual proximal point.
knowledge_statements.title: Augmented-Lagrangian Connection

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal point iteration and basic convergence variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact fixed-parameter proximal minimization, its variable-parameter version, and the stated summably inexact extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} be closed, proper, and convex, with \operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing. For \lambda>0, the proximal point iteration is x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x^k). Then \operatorname{dist}(x^k,\operatorname*{argmin}f)\to0 and f(x^k)\to\min f. The variable-parameter iteration x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f}(x^k) also converges under \lambda_k>0 and \sum_{k=1}^{\infty}\lambda_k=\infty. Approximate proximal minimizations are admissible when their errors satisfy an appropriate condition, such as summability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed proper convex function that attains its minimum, exact proximal-point iterates with a fixed positive parameter approach the minimizer set and attain the optimal objective value asymptotically. Positive varying parameters are allowed when their sum diverges. Inexact proximal solves require a suitable error condition, with summability given as an example.
assumptions_latex: \text{for inexact minimizations, the errors satisfy an applicable convergence condition}

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a real Hilbert space \(H\), a maximal-monotone operator \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) with \(\operatorname{zer}A\ne\varnothing\), an initial point \(x^0\in H\), and positive parameters \((\gamma_k)\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Proximal-Point Step as Backward Euler
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Despite being called proximal gradient in the extract, the displayed update is the exact proximal-point iteration rather than a forward–backward composite-gradient step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\eta>0\),
\[
x_{n+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta f}(x_n).
\]
If \(f\) is continuously differentiable, the proximal optimality condition gives
\[
x_{n+1}=x_n-\eta\nabla f(x_{n+1}),
\]
which is the backward-Euler discretization of \(\dot x(t)=-\nabla f(x(t))\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact proximal point iteration and its basic properties
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal-point minimization for a proper lower-semicontinuous convex objective, including descent, resolvent, implicit-subgradient, and fixed-point characterizations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, let \(x^0\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(\eta_t>0\). The exact proximal-point iteration is
\[
x^{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{2\eta_t}\|x-x^t\|^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta_t f}(x^t)=(I+\eta_t\partial f)^{-1}(x^t).
\]
It satisfies
\[
f(x^{t+1})\le f(x^t)-\frac{1}{2\eta_t}\|x^{t+1}-x^t\|^2,
\qquad x^{t+1}-x^t\in-\eta_t\partial f(x^{t+1}).
\]
Hence \(f(x^t)\) decreases strictly whenever \(x^{t+1}\ne x^t\). For each fixed \(\eta_t\), the proximal map is firmly nonexpansive, and
\[
x^{t+1}=x^t\iff 0\in\partial f(x^t)\iff x^t\in\operatorname*{argmin}f.
\]
If \(f_0\) is minimized over a nonempty closed convex set \(C\), the constraint can be represented by replacing the objective with \(f=f_0+\delta_C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex objective and positive proximal parameters, the exact proximal-point method minimizes the objective plus a quadratic centered at the current iterate. The update is equivalently a proximal-map evaluation, a resolvent evaluation, and an implicit subgradient step. It satisfies a quantified descent inequality, its proximal map is firmly nonexpansive, and its fixed points are exactly the minimizers. Closed convex constraints can be incorporated through an indicator function.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\text{ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{t+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta_t f}(x^t)=(I+\eta_t\partial f)^{-1}(x^t),\quad f(x^{t+1})\le f(x^t)-\frac{\|x^{t+1}-x^t\|^2}{2\eta_t},\quad x^{t+1}-x^t\in-\eta_t\partial f(x^{t+1}),\quad [x^{t+1}=x^t\iff 0\in\partial f(x^t)\iff x^t\in\operatorname*{argmin}f]
