knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection characterization and comparison inequality for a constrained proximal step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes an exact constrained proximal update as an implicit projected subgradient step and states its fundamental comparison inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and let \(f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be closed, proper, and convex with \(\operatorname{ri}(X)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\neq\varnothing\). For \(x_k\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(\alpha_k>0\), define
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
Then there exists \(g_{k+1}\in\partial f(x_{k+1})\) such that
\[
x_{k+1}=P_X(x_k-\alpha_k g_{k+1}).
\]
Moreover, for every \(y\in X\),
\[
\lVert x_{k+1}-y\rVert^2\leq \lVert x_k-y\rVert^2-2\alpha_k\bigl(f(x_{k+1})-f(y)\bigr)-\lVert x_k-x_{k+1}\rVert^2
\]
and consequently
\[
\lVert x_{k+1}-y\rVert^2\leq \lVert x_k-y\rVert^2-2\alpha_k\bigl(f(x_{k+1})-f(y)\bigr).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the relative-interior qualification, an exact proximal step over a closed convex set equals the projection of an implicit subgradient step evaluated at the new iterate. Its squared distance to every feasible comparison point satisfies the stated inequality, including the nonpositive step-length correction.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}
f:\mathbb R^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is closed, proper, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists g_{k+1}\in\partial f(x_{k+1})\text{ such that }x_{k+1}=P_X(x_k-\alpha_k g_{k+1}),\quad \forall y\in X:\ \lVert x_{k+1}-y\rVert^2\leq\lVert x_k-y\rVert^2-2\alpha_k(f(x_{k+1})-f(y))-\lVert x_k-x_{k+1}\rVert^2.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone. Given \(x^0\in H\), positive parameters \((\gamma_k)\), and relaxation factors \(\lambda_k\in(0,2)\), compute \[p^k=J_{\gamma_kA}(x^k),\qquad x^{k+1}=x^k+\lambda_k(p^k-x^k),\qquad k=0,1,\ldots.\] Values \(0<\lambda_k<1\) define under-relaxation, \(\lambda_k=1\) gives the exact proximal-point step, and \(1<\lambda_k<2\) defines over-relaxation. A natural stopping quantity is \(\lVert p^k-x^k\rVert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a real Hilbert space, a relaxed proximal-point step moves by a relaxation factor times the displacement from the current iterate to its exact resolvent point. Factors below, equal to, or above one give under-relaxed, exact, or over-relaxed steps.
knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Proximal Point Iterations

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, let \(x^k\in H\), let \(\gamma_k>0\), and let \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\). An inexact proximal point \(x^{k+1}\in H\) satisfies the absolute error criterion if \[\left\lVert x^{k+1}-J_{\gamma_kA}(x^k)\right\rVert\le\varepsilon_k.\] Equivalently, there exists \(e^k\in H\) with \(\lVert e^k\rVert\le\varepsilon_k\) such that \[x^{k+1}=J_{\gamma_kA}(x^k)+e^k.\] This is an ambient-norm distance criterion and does not by itself impose a relative-error or inclusion-residual bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a real Hilbert space, an inexact update meets the absolute error criterion when its norm distance from the exact resolvent point is at most the prescribed nonnegative tolerance. Equivalently, it is the exact resolvent plus a norm-bounded additive error.

knowledge_statements.title: Summable Error Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Absolute perturbation criterion for an inexact resolvent iteration in a Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, and let \(\lambda_k>0\). For the exact resolvent point \(p_{k+1}=J_{\lambda_k A}x_k\), an inexact update \(x_{k+1}=p_{k+1}+e_k\) satisfies the absolute-summable error criterion when there exist prescribed tolerances \(\eta_k\geq 0\) such that \(\|e_k\|\leq\eta_k\) for every \(k\) and \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k<\infty.\] Consequently, the accumulated deviation from the exact proximal steps is finite: \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_{k+1}-J_{\lambda_kA}x_k\|<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each inexact proximal update deviates from its exact resolvent point by a tolerance whose total over all iterations is finite.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, choose \(x_0\in H\) and parameters \(\lambda_k>0\), and let \(B>0\) be a total error budget. Choose weights \(w_k\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}w_k\leq1\), and set \(\eta_k=Bw_k\). At iteration \(k\), compute \(x_{k+1}\in H\) satisfying \[\|x_{k+1}-J_{\lambda_kA}x_k\|\leq\eta_k.\] For every infinite sequence satisfying these tests, \[\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\|x_{k+1}-J_{\lambda_kA}x_k\|\leq\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\eta_k\leq B.\] A separately specified outer termination test may be applied after each update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate nonnegative shares of a finite total error budget to the iterations and require each approximate proximal step to respect its assigned share; the cumulative absolute proximal error is then at most the total budget.

children.title: Nonsummable Error Boundary
children.top_down_role: Convergence limitations when cumulative error control is unavailable.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsummable Error Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure of convergence when absolute proximal errors vanish but are not summable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=\mathbb{R}\), let \(A(x)=\{0\}\) for every \(x\), and take \(\lambda_k=1\). Then \(J_{\lambda_kA}=I\) and \(\operatorname{zer}A=\mathbb{R}\). Starting from \(x_0=0\), define the inexact proximal iteration \[x_{k+1}=J_{\lambda_kA}x_k+e_k=x_k+\frac{1}{k+1}.\] Although \(e_k\to0\), the errors are nonsummable because \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|e_k|=\infty\). Moreover, \(x_k=\sum_{j=1}^{k}1/j\to+\infty\), so the iterates do not converge. Thus vanishing absolute errors alone cannot replace summability in a general convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the zero operator, harmonic additive errors vanish individually but accumulate without bound, causing the inexact proximal iterates to diverge.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is mathematically coherent and counterexample is the correct kind for this failure-boundary leaf: harmonic additive errors for the zero operator produce divergent partial sums. No evidence record or source locator is supplied, so the nontrivial failure claim cannot enter candidate-review memory under the evidence contract.

children.title: Relative Error Criteria
children.top_down_role: Inexact regimes coupling inner accuracy to proximal progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Relative Error Criteria
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual criterion scaling inner proximal accuracy by the displacement of the current proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, and fix \(\sigma\in[0,1)\). Given \(x_k\in H\) and \(\lambda_k>0\), a pair \((y_k,v_k)\) satisfies the relative proximal error criterion if \(v_k\in A(y_k)\) and \[\|\lambda_kv_k+y_k-x_k\|\leq\sigma\|y_k-x_k\|.\] The left side is the resolvent-equation residual, while the right side scales with the proposed proximal displacement. When \(y_k=x_k\), the condition forces \(v_k=0\); when \(\sigma=0\), it gives the exact resolvent equation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal residual must be no larger than a fixed fraction of the proposed step length, coupling inner accuracy to outer progress.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone.

knowledge_statements.title: Hybrid Proximal–Extragradient Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard enlargement-based HPE iteration for a maximal monotone inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, choose \(x_0\in H\) and \(\sigma\in[0,1)\). At iteration \(k\), choose \(\lambda_k>0\) and find \((y_k,v_k,\varepsilon_k)\) with \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), \(v_k\in A^{\varepsilon_k}(y_k)\), and \[\|\lambda_kv_k+y_k-x_k\|^2+2\lambda_k\varepsilon_k\leq\sigma^2\|y_k-x_k\|^2.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x_k-\lambda_kv_k\). Stop when a prescribed test on \(\|v_k\|\) and \(\varepsilon_k\) holds; otherwise continue. The triple provides an extragradient-style certificate for the inexact proximal step.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find an enlarged-operator certificate satisfying a relative residual inequality, then update from the old point along the certified operator value.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Choose \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), parameters \(\lambda_k>0\), and tolerances \(\eta_k\geq0\). At outer iteration \(k\), apply an iterative inner solver to \(\phi_k(z)=f(z)+\|z-x_k\|^2/(2\lambda_k)\), producing iterates \(z_{k,t}\in\operatorname{dom}f\). Stop at the first index \(t_k\) for which there exists \[r_{k,t_k}\in\partial f(z_{k,t_k})+\frac{z_{k,t_k}-x_k}{\lambda_k}\quad\text{with}\quad\|r_{k,t_k}\|\leq\eta_k,\] and set \(x_{k+1}=z_{k,t_k}\). Consequently, \[\operatorname{dist}\!\left(0,\partial f(x_{k+1})+\frac{x_{k+1}-x_k}{\lambda_k}\right)\leq\eta_k.\] Apply a separately specified outer termination test after each completed inner solve.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each outer iteration, approximately minimize the regularized proximal subproblem with an inner solver and accept its first iterate whose optimality residual is at most the assigned tolerance.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Proximal Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preconditioned resolvent iteration with uniformly positive definite iteration-dependent metrics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone. Choose \(x_0\in H\), \(\lambda_k>0\), and bounded self-adjoint operators \(M_k\) satisfying \(mI\preceq M_k\preceq MI\) for constants \(0<m\leq M<\infty\). Compute \[x_{k+1}=(I+\lambda_kM_k^{-1}A)^{-1}x_k,\] equivalently require \(0\in A(x_{k+1})+M_k(x_{k+1}-x_k)/\lambda_k\). Stop when a prescribed inclusion-residual or displacement test holds. Each step is a proximal point step in the norm \(\|z\|_{M_k}^2=\langle M_kz,z\rangle\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, apply the resolvent in a uniformly positive definite metric, thereby preconditioning the proximal inclusion.
assumptions_latex: \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) is maximal monotone on a real Hilbert space.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\mathbb{R}^n\), let \(C\subseteq X\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, let \(f:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and let \(h:X\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a Legendre function. For \(x\in\operatorname{dom}h\) and \(y\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), define \[D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle\nabla h(y),x-y\rangle.\] From \(x_k\in C\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), choose \(\lambda_k>0\) and compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{f(x)+\frac{1}{\lambda_k}D_h(x,x_k)\right\},\] assuming this argmin contains a point in \(C\cap\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\). knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Proximal Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nesterov-type inertial outer iteration built from exact proximal evaluations of a convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, and fix \(\lambda>0\). Choose \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\), set \(y_0=x_0\) and \(t_0=1\). For \(k\geq0\), compute \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(y_k),\qquad t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2},\] and set \(y_{k+1}=x_{k+1}+((t_k-1)/t_{k+1})(x_{k+1}-x_k)\). Stop when a prescribed proximal residual or objective-gap test holds; otherwise return the latest \(x_{k+1}\) after the iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Apply exact proximal evaluations at extrapolated points and update the extrapolation coefficient with the standard Nesterov recurrence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted primal–dual potential inequality for randomized accelerated proximal-point iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A terminal expected-potential bound under explicit parameter coupling and stability inequalities for Algorithm 6.11.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let (\mathbf x^{t},y^{t}) for t=1,\ldots,s be generated by Algorithm 6.11, and let (\mathbf x^{*},y^{*}) be a saddle point of (6.6.49). Suppose that, for every t=1,\ldots,s-1, \alpha_{t+1}=(m-1)\widetilde\alpha_{t+1}, \gamma_t=\gamma_{t+1}\widetilde\alpha_{t+1}, \gamma_{t+1}((m-1)\eta_{t+1}+(m-2)\mu)\le (m-1)\gamma_t(\eta_t+\mu), \gamma_{t+1}\tau_{t+1}\le\gamma_t(\tau_t+1), and 2(m-1)\widetilde\alpha_{t+1}\bar A^{2}\le\bar\mu\eta_t\tau_{t+1}, where \bar A=\max_{i\in[m-1]}\|\mathbf A_i\|. knowledge_statements.title: Halpern-Type Resolvent Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Anchored Halpern iteration applied to the firmly nonexpansive resolvent of a maximal monotone operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone with \(\operatorname{zer}A\neq\varnothing\), fix \(\lambda>0\), and choose an anchor \(u\in H\) and initial point \(x_0\in H\). For \(k\geq0\), choose \(\alpha_k\in(0,1)\) and compute \[x_{k+1}=\alpha_k u+(1-\alpha_k)J_{\lambda A}x_k.\] A standard admissible schedule satisfies \(\alpha_k\to0\), \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\alpha_k=\infty\), and \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}|\alpha_{k+1}-\alpha_k|<\infty\), for example \(\alpha_k=1/(k+2)\). Stop when \(\|x_k-J_{\lambda A}x_k\|\) meets the requested tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Blend each resolvent evaluation with a diminishing but nonsummable weight on a fixed anchor, and monitor the resolvent fixed-point residual.
assumptions_latex: \(\lambda>0\), \(u,x_0\in H\), and the stated conditions on \(\alpha_k\) hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Catalyst Outer–Inner Acceleration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Strongly convex Catalyst specialization using inertial outer centers and approximate regularized subproblem solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex. Choose \(\kappa>0\), define \(q=\mu/(\mu+\kappa)\), \(\alpha=\sqrt q\), and \(\beta=(1-\alpha)/(1+\alpha)\), and set \(y_0=x_0\). At iteration \(k\), use a chosen inner method to obtain \(x_{k+1}\) satisfying \[f(x_{k+1})+\frac{\kappa}{2}\|x_{k+1}-y_k\|^2-\min_x\left\{f(x)+\frac{\kappa}{2}\|x-y_k\|^2\right\}\leq\varepsilon_k.\] Then set \(y_{k+1}=x_{k+1}+\beta(x_{k+1}-x_k)\). Stop under the prescribed outer accuracy test.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve a sequence of quadratically regularized subproblems and extrapolate their solutions using parameters determined by strong convexity and regularization.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\).
\(\kappa>0\), \(\varepsilon_k\geq0\), and each regularized subproblem has a minimizer.

children.title: Incremental Proximal Point Methods
children.top_down_role: Componentwise proximal-point families for finite sums and structured collections.

knowledge_statements.title: Incremental Proximal Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Componentwise proximal updates for minimizing a finite sum of proper closed convex functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{m}f_i(x)\), where each \(f_i:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex. Choose \(x_0\in H\), stepsizes \(\lambda_k>0\), and indices \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), selected cyclically or by a specified sampling rule. Perform \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f_{i_k}}(x_k)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{f_{i_k}(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\|x-x_k\|^2\right\}.\] Stop after the prescribed number of component updates or when a stated aggregate optimality test holds, and output the last iterate or a prespecified weighted average.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimize a finite sum by applying one component’s proximal mapping per iteration, using a cyclic or explicitly sampled component schedule.
assumptions_latex: \(f_i\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex for each \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).
\(\lambda_k>0\), and the index rule specifies \(i_k\) at every iteration.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise proximal update is a coherent incremental proximal algorithm and makes no unsupported convergence claim, but the record has no citation or evidence entry. A source with an algorithm, definition, or section locator for incremental proximal minimization is required.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Incremental proximal point update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratically regularized componentwise proximal minimization for a convex finite-sum problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{x\in X}\left\{f_{i_k}(x)+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\right\},\qquad \alpha_k>0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex component functions and a nonempty closed convex set X, the incremental proximal point method minimizes one selected component plus a quadratic penalty for displacement from the current iterate. It is especially useful when the component proximal subproblem is available in closed form or is inexpensive.
assumptions_latex: X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}

children.title: Sampled Proximal Point Methods
children.top_down_role: Proximal-point methods driven by sampled objective models.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampled Proximal Point Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal updates using independently sampled convex loss functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space, let \((\xi_k)_{k\geq 0}\) be sampled observations, and let \(f(\cdot;\xi):H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex for almost every \(\xi\). Given \(x_0\in H\) and parameters \(\lambda_k>0\), compute
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{f(x;\xi_k)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\right\}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f(\cdot;\xi_k)}(x_k).
\]
After \(N\) samples, output either \(x_N\) or a prespecified weighted average of \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, sample one loss function and take its exact proximal step from the current iterate; return the last iterate or a prescribed average.
assumptions_latex: \(f(\cdot;\xi)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex almost surely.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the sampled proximal-point leaf and the update is mathematically standard, but the record has no citation or inspectable locator for the sampled-objective formulation and output policy. Source support is required before candidate review.

children.title: Stochastic Proximal Stabilization Policies
children.top_down_role: Averaging and stabilization mechanisms for stochastic proximal-point iterates.

children.title: Iterate Averaging
children.top_down_role: Policies averaging stochastic proximal-point iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted averaging policy for stochastic proximal iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given iterates \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\in H\) and deterministic or data-adapted weights \(w_k\geq 0\) satisfying \(W_N:=\sum_{k=1}^N w_k>0\), define the averaged output by
\[
\bar x_N:=\frac{1}{W_N}\sum_{k=1}^N w_kx_k.
\]
The weights must be chosen without using future samples; formally, \(w_k\) is measurable with respect to the information available when \(x_k\) is formed. Uniform averaging uses \(w_k=1\), whereas stepsize averaging uses \(w_k=\lambda_{k-1}\). The algorithm returns \(\bar x_N\) instead of the final iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return a nonnegative weighted average of the stochastic proximal iterates, with each weight chosen using no future sample information.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits an iterate-averaging policy, and the weighted-average formula is standard. However, no source is cited, and the measurability requirement refers to an information structure that is not defined. An authoritative locator should also specify the admissible filtration or adaptation convention.

children.title: Tail Averaging
children.top_down_role: Averaging policies restricted to later iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Tail Averaging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Averaging restricted to a terminal segment of proximal iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_1,\ldots,x_N\in H\), choose a tail index \(m_N\in\{1,\ldots,N\}\) and nonnegative weights \(w_k\) with \(W_{m_N:N}:=\sum_{k=m_N}^Nw_k>0\). Define
\[
\bar x_N^{\mathrm{tail}}:=\frac{1}{W_{m_N:N}}\sum_{k=m_N}^Nw_kx_k.
\]
Uniform tail averaging takes \(w_k=1\); a fixed tail fraction takes \(m_N=\lfloor\alpha N\rfloor+1\) for \(0\leq\alpha<1\). The output discards all iterates with indices below \(m_N\) and returns \(\bar x_N^{\mathrm{tail}}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Discard an initial segment and return a weighted average of the remaining iterates; uniform averaging over a fixed terminal fraction is a standard instance.

notation.meaning: total weight on the retained tail

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and terminal-tail averaging formula fit the leaf, but the record supplies no source or inspectable locator supporting this policy and its fixed-tail-fraction instance.

children.title: Stochastic Stabilization
children.top_down_role: Mechanisms reducing variability or erratic proximal-point behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Stabilization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification condition for sampled weakly convex proximal models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be a sampled model that is \(\rho_k\)-weakly convex, meaning \(x\mapsto m_k(x)+(\rho_k/2)\lVert x\rVert^2\) is convex. The stabilized subproblem
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{m_k(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda_k}\lVert x-x_k\rVert^2\right\}
\]
is strongly convex whenever \(0<\lambda_k<1/\rho_k\), with the convention \(1/0=+\infty\). Its strong-convexity modulus is \(1/\lambda_k-\rho_k\); hence, when a minimizer exists, it is unique and defines a single-valued stabilized update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal quadratic makes a sampled weakly convex model strongly convex when its inverse stepsize exceeds the model’s weak-convexity parameter.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the stabilization leaf, and the stated weak-convexity threshold and strong-convexity modulus are standard. The record nevertheless has no citation or locator supporting the sampled-model stabilization claim.

children.title: Stabilization Bias Boundary
children.top_down_role: Tradeoffs where stabilization alters limiting behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Bias Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent anchoring can change the population minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}F\neq\varnothing\). For a fixed anchor \(c\in H\) and finite \(\lambda>0\), let
\[
x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in H}\left\{F(x)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\lVert x-c\rVert^2\right\}.
\]
Then \(F(x_\lambda)-\inf F\leq \operatorname{dist}(c,X^*)^2/(2\lambda)\), but generally \(x_\lambda\notin X^*\). Thus a nonvanishing fixed-anchor stabilization may retain optimization bias; exact recovery is guaranteed when \(c\in X^*\), or asymptotically when \(\lambda\to+\infty\) under suitable compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed finite proximal anchoring can shift the optimizer. Its objective bias is bounded by the squared anchor-to-solution distance divided by twice the proximal parameter.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(X^*\neq\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: set of minimizers of the unstabilized objective

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the finite-parameter bias bound is plausible and precisely stated. No source is supplied, and the additional asymptotic recovery assertion invokes unspecified suitable compactness, so its exact hypotheses cannot be reviewed reliably.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence of the Exact Proximal Point Algorithm
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-value and iterate convergence under a divergent sum of positive proximal parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\) be closed, proper, and convex, and let \(\{x_k\}\) be generated by the exact proximal-point iteration with \(c_k>0\). If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}c_k=\infty\), then \[f(x_k)\downarrow f^*:=\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x).\] If additionally \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}f(x)\neq\varnothing\), then \(x_k\) converges to a point of \(X^*\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the positive proximal parameters have divergent sum, the objective values decrease to the infimum. If a minimizer exists, the iterates converge to a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,\infty]\text{ is closed, proper, and convex}

children.title: Global Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence guarantees from admissible initial points.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional global convergence of the exact proximal point method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, with \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). Starting from \(x_0\in\mathbb R^d\), set \(x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f}(x_k)\), where \(\inf_k\lambda_k>0\). For every \(x^*\in X^*\),
\[
\lVert x_{k+1}-x^*\rVert^2\leq\lVert x_k-x^*\rVert^2-\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2.
\]
Consequently, the sequence is bounded, every accumulation point belongs to \(X^*\), and the entire sequence converges to some \(\bar x\in X^*\) from every initial point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For any starting point, exact proximal iterations with stepsizes bounded away from zero converge in finite dimensions to a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on \(\mathbb R^d\), with \(X^*\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Asymptotic Limit Behavior
children.top_down_role: Long-run behavior of proximal-point iterates and residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Asymptotic Limit Behavior
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fejér monotonicity, vanishing steps, and objective convergence for exact proximal iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under the exact proximal iteration \(x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f}(x_k)\) on a real Hilbert space, assume \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex, \(X^*\neq\varnothing\), and \(\underline\lambda:=\inf_k\lambda_k>0\). Then \((x_k)\) is Fejér monotone with respect to \(X^*\),
\[
\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert^2<+\infty,
\qquad
r_{k+1}:=\frac{x_k-x_{k+1}}{\lambda_k}\in\partial f(x_{k+1}),
\]
and \(\lVert r_{k+1}\rVert\to0\). Moreover, \(f(x_k)\) is nonincreasing and converges to \(\inf f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact proximal iterates are Fejér monotone; their steps and subgradient residuals vanish, while their objective values decrease to the optimum.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(X^*\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Weak Limit Regimes
children.top_down_role: Limit behavior expressed through weak convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Weak Limit Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak convergence of proximal point iterates in Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(X^*:=\operatorname*{argmin}f\neq\varnothing\). If
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f}(x_k)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\inf_k\lambda_k>0,
\]
then there exists \(\bar x\in X^*\) such that \(x_k\rightharpoonup\bar x\). This conclusion is weak convergence in the ambient Hilbert topology; without finite dimensionality, compactness, uniform convexity, or another regularizing condition, norm convergence does not follow from these hypotheses alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In a Hilbert space, exact proximal iterations converge weakly to a minimizer; the basic assumptions alone do not guarantee norm convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is a real Hilbert space and \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with \(X^*\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Strong Limit Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural settings supporting strong convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Limit Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Norm convergence under strong convexity of the objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H\) be a real Hilbert space and let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex for some \(\mu>0\). Its unique minimizer is denoted by \(x^*\). For proximal iterations \(x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_k f}(x_k)\) with \(\lambda_k>0\),
\[
\lVert x_{k+1}-x^*\rVert\leq\frac{1}{1+\mu\lambda_k}\lVert x_k-x^*\rVert,
\qquad
\lVert x_N-x^*\rVert\leq\prod_{k=0}^{N-1}(1+\mu\lambda_k)^{-1}\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert.
\]
If \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lambda_k=+\infty\), then \(x_k\to x^*\) in norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strong convexity makes each proximal map contractive. If the stepsizes have infinite sum, the iterates converge in norm to the unique minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\mu\)-strongly convex with \(\mu>0\).

children.title: Residual-Objective Complexity Pair
children.top_down_role: Nonasymptotic convergence families expressed through residual and objective criteria.

children.title: Residual Complexity
children.top_down_role: Nonasymptotic guarantees measured by proximal residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Residual Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Best-iterate subgradient-residual bound for constant-step proximal point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with a minimizer \(x^*\). For a constant \(\lambda>0\), generate \(x_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x_{i-1})\) and define
\[
r_i:=\frac{x_{i-1}-x_i}{\lambda}\in\partial f(x_i),
\qquad 1\leq i\leq N.
\]
Then
\[
\min_{1\leq i\leq N}\lVert r_i\rVert\leq\frac{\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert}{\lambda\sqrt N}.
\]
Thus at most \(\lceil\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2/(\lambda^2\varepsilon^2)\rceil\) exact proximal-oracle calls suffice to produce an iterate whose subgradient residual norm is at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Among the first N proximal iterates, one has subgradient residual at most the initial solution distance divided by the stepsize and square root of N.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with a minimizer \(x^*\).

children.title: Objective-Gap Complexity
children.top_down_role: Nonasymptotic guarantees measured by objective-value gaps.

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Gap Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Last-iterate objective rate for constant-step proximal point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with minimizer \(x^*\), and let \(x_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x_{i-1})\) for a constant \(\lambda>0\). Since \(f(x_i)\) is nonincreasing, after \(N\geq1\) exact proximal-oracle calls,
\[
0\leq f(x_N)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2}{2\lambda N}.
\]
Consequently, \(N\geq\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2/(2\lambda\varepsilon)\) guarantees \(f(x_N)-\inf f\leq\varepsilon\), giving an \(O(1/\varepsilon)\) proximal-oracle complexity for objective accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a constant proximal stepsize, the last-iterate objective gap decreases as one over the number of exact proximal-oracle calls.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with minimizer \(x^*\).

children.title: Ergodic Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity guarantees for averaged outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Ergodic Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-average objective bound for variable-step proximal point iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with minimizer \(x^*\). Generate \(x_i=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda_{i-1}f}(x_{i-1})\) with \(\lambda_{i-1}>0\), and define
\[
\Lambda_N:=\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_{i-1},
\qquad
\bar x_N:=\frac{1}{\Lambda_N}\sum_{i=1}^N\lambda_{i-1}x_i.
\]
Then convexity and the proximal descent inequality give
\[
0\leq f(\bar x_N)-f(x^*)\leq\frac{\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2}{2\Lambda_N}.
\]
Hence ergodic objective accuracy \(\varepsilon\) is ensured once \(\Lambda_N\geq\lVert x_0-x^*\rVert^2/(2\varepsilon)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The stepsize-weighted average has objective gap bounded by the initial squared solution distance divided by twice the accumulated stepsize.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex with minimizer \(x^*\).

children.title: Certificate Conversion
children.top_down_role: Relationships between residual-based and value-based guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Conversion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Converts an exact proximal residual into a convex objective-gap certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:H\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex on a Hilbert space, with nonempty solution set \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}f\). For \(\lambda>0\), set \(x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) and \(r=(x-x^+)/\lambda\). Proximal optimality gives \(r\in\partial f(x^+)\). Consequently, for every \(x^\star\in S\), \[0\le f(x^+)-f(x^\star)\le \langle r,x^+-x^\star\rangle\le \|r\|\,\|x^+-x^\star\|.\] Thus any verified bounds \(\|r\|\le\varepsilon\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(x^+,S)\le R\) certify \(f(x^+)-\inf f\le R\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal residual bound becomes an objective-gap bound when combined with a verified distance-to-solution bound.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex.

children.title: Linear Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regularity settings supporting geometric proximal-point convergence.

knowledge_statements.title: Linear Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local linear distance convergence of exact proximal point iteration under metric subregularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, let \(S=T^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\), and generate \(x^{k+1}=J_{\lambda_kT}x^k\). Suppose that near a limit point in \(S\), \(T\) is metrically subregular for \(0\) with modulus \(\kappa>0\), and \(\lambda_k\ge\underline\lambda>0\). Once \(x^{k+1}\) lies in the subregularity neighborhood, firm nonexpansiveness and \((x^k-x^{k+1})/\lambda_k\in T(x^{k+1})\) imply \[\operatorname{dist}(x^{k+1},S)\le \frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2+\lambda_k^2}}\operatorname{dist}(x^k,S)\le q\operatorname{dist}(x^k,S),\] where \(q=\kappa/\sqrt{\kappa^2+\underline\lambda^2}<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity and proximal parameters bounded away from zero yield local Q-linear contraction of distance to the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is locally metrically subregular for \(0\) with modulus \(\kappa\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The local contraction factor is plausible under the stated metric-subregularity regime, but the exact formula and hypotheses require an authoritative theorem or page locator.

children.title: Superlinear Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Strengthened local settings supporting faster-than-linear behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Superlinear Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local superlinear distance convergence obtained by increasing exact proximal regularization parameters.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone, let \(S=T^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\), and suppose \(x^k\to\bar x\in S\) under \(x^{k+1}=J_{\lambda_kT}x^k\). Assume that \(T\) is metrically subregular for \(0\) at \(\bar x\), uniformly with modulus \(\kappa>0\), and that \(\lambda_k\to+\infty\). For all sufficiently large \(k\), \[\frac{\operatorname{dist}(x^{k+1},S)}{\operatorname{dist}(x^k,S)}\le \frac{\kappa}{\sqrt{\kappa^2+\lambda_k^2}}\longrightarrow0,\] whenever the denominator is nonzero. Hence the distances to \(S\) converge Q-superlinearly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under local metric subregularity, proximal parameters tending to infinity force the distance contraction factors to vanish, giving local Q-superlinear convergence.
assumptions_latex: \(x^k\to\bar x\in T^{-1}(0)\) under exact proximal iterations.
\(T\) is metrically subregular for \(0\) at \(\bar x\) with modulus \(\kappa\).

notation.meaning: zero set of the maximal monotone operator

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated superlinear regime is plausible, but the precise contraction estimate under increasing parameters requires an authoritative source establishing all localization conditions.

children.title: Metric-Subregularity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Fast convergence organized through metric subregularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Metric-Subregularity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local error-bound condition connecting distance to zeros with operator residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a set-valued operator \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\), a point \(\bar x\in T^{-1}(0)\), and \(\kappa\ge0\), metric subregularity of \(T\) for \(0\) at \(\bar x\) means that there exist neighborhoods \(U\) of \(\bar x\) and \(V\) of \(0\) such that \[\operatorname{dist}(x,T^{-1}(0))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,T(x)\cap V)\qquad\text{for every }x\in U,\] with \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\varnothing)=+\infty\). In the commonly used localized-residual form, it suffices to require \(\operatorname{dist}(x,T^{-1}(0))\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,T(x))\) throughout a neighborhood of \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Metric subregularity is a local error bound controlling distance to the zero set by the smallest nearby operator residual.

notation.meaning: distance induced by the Hilbert-space norm

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard definition uses the local inequality dist(x,T^{-1}(0)) <= kappa dist(0,T(x)). The alternative expression involving T(x) intersected with V is not established here as an equivalent definition and may be strictly weaker; an authoritative variational-analysis locator is required.

children.title: Fast-Rate Locality Boundary
children.top_down_role: Distinction between local fast behavior and globally valid rates.

knowledge_statements.title: Fast-Rate Locality Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fast proximal rates are generally local unless the governing error bound is global.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Local metric subregularity yields a fast-rate estimate only after the proximal iterates and their residuals enter its validity neighborhood; it does not imply a uniform global contraction. Concretely, for \(f:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) defined by \(f(x)=x^4/4\), the minimizer is \(0\), but \(\partial f(x)=\{x^3\}\) is not metrically subregular for \(0\) at \(0\), since \(|x|\le\kappa|x|^3\) fails near zero for every finite \(\kappa\). The exact proximal iteration satisfies \(x^k=x^{k+1}+\lambda_k(x^{k+1})^3\), so no fixed local Q-linear factor follows from convexity alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fast local rates cannot be globalized without a global error bound; a quartic convex objective already lacks the subregularity needed for linear contraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Convexity and exact proximal steps alone do not ensure a local or global Q-linear rate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quartic example is self-checkable and fits the failure-boundary leaf, but the nontrivial rate-boundary claim has no cited evidence.

children.title: Inexact Proximal Point Convergence
children.top_down_role: Convergence families distinguished by inner-error certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Proximal Point Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak convergence under summable absolute errors in evaluating maximal-monotone resolvents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(T:H\rightrightarrows H\) be maximal monotone on a Hilbert space with \(S=T^{-1}(0)\neq\varnothing\). Let \(0<\underline\lambda\le\lambda_k\le\overline\lambda<+\infty\), and suppose the computed iterates satisfy \[\|x^{k+1}-J_{\lambda_kT}(x^k)\|\le\varepsilon_k,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<+\infty.\] Then \((x^k)\) is quasi-Fejér with respect to \(S\), its exact-resolvent residuals converge to zero, and \((x^k)\) converges weakly to a point of \(S\). In finite-dimensional spaces the convergence is in norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If every proximal subproblem is solved with summable absolute error and parameters stay uniformly positive and finite, the outer iterates converge to a zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^k\rightharpoonup x^\star\in T^{-1}(0)\); in finite dimensions, \(x^k\to x^\star\).

children.title: Accelerated Outer–Inner Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity and oracle tradeoffs for accelerated proximal-point frameworks.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Outer–Inner Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates accelerated outer iterations from the aggregate work used to approximate proximal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider an accelerated proximal-point scheme for minimizing a proper closed convex function \(f\), using a fixed parameter \(\lambda>0\). Under exact proximal evaluations, its outer guarantee has the form \[f(x^K)-\inf f\le \frac{C\|x^0-x^\star\|^2}{\lambda(K+1)^2},\] for a method-specific constant \(C>0\), hence \(K=O(\sqrt{\|x^0-x^\star\|^2/(\lambda\epsilon)})\) outer proximal calls suffice for objective accuracy \(\epsilon\). If outer call \(k\) is implemented by \(N_k\) inner-oracle steps, total inner work is \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}N_k\); preservation of the accelerated rate additionally requires the method-specific weighted inner-error accumulation to remain bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration reduces outer proximal calls to order one over square-root accuracy, while total work is the sum of inner solves and depends on weighted error control.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, closed, and convex with a minimizer \(x^\star\).
The accelerated scheme uses a fixed \(\lambda>0\).
Inexact calls satisfy the scheme's weighted error condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Outer complexity is \(O(\epsilon^{-1/2})\), while inner complexity equals \(\sum_{k<K}N_k\).

children.title: Regularization Parameter Policies
children.top_down_role: Fixed and adaptive parameter-selection families for proximal-point methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Regularization Parameter Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible fixed and adaptive parameter policies for exact or certified inexact proximal iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a maximal monotone operator \(T\), an initial point \(x^0\), bounds \(0<\lambda_{\min}\le\lambda_{\max}<+\infty\), and a stopping tolerance \(\tau\ge0\). At iteration \(k\), choose either a fixed parameter \(\lambda_k\equiv\lambda\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\) or an adaptive \(\lambda_k\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\) determined from previously computed iterates and residuals. Compute a certified exact or inexact proximal point \(x^{k+1}\approx J_{\lambda_kT}(x^k)\), form \(r^{k+1}=(x^k-x^{k+1})/\lambda_k\), and stop with output \(x^{k+1}\) when its valid residual certificate is at most \(\tau\); otherwise increment \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose fixed or history-adaptive proximal parameters within positive finite bounds, solve the subproblem, and stop when a certified residual meets tolerance.
assumptions_latex: Every inexact solve supplies a valid residual certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The policy produces proximal iterates with \(\lambda_k\in[\lambda_{\min},\lambda_{\max}]\) and terminates upon the prescribed certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Accuracy Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable absolute inner errors sufficient for convergence of the inexact proximal outer sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an inexact proximal sequence, define the certified absolute inner error by \(\varepsilon_k\ge\|x^{k+1}-J_{\lambda_kT}(x^k)\|\). A convergence-safe accuracy schedule satisfies \[\varepsilon_k\ge0,\qquad \sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<+\infty.\] One implementable choice is \(\varepsilon_k=c(k+1)^{-1-\delta}\) with \(c>0\) and \(\delta>0\). The inner solver at outer iteration \(k\) must continue until its computable certificate implies the displayed absolute-error bound. This schedule controls accumulated perturbations; accelerated or relative-error proximal frameworks may require different, typically weighted, predicates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Require each certified proximal error to follow a summable schedule, such as a power law with exponent strictly greater than one.
assumptions_latex: The inner certificate upper-bounds the absolute resolvent error.

children.title: Warm-Start Management
children.top_down_role: Reuse of prior inner-solver states for subsequent subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Management
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonexpansiveness quantifies why the preceding proximal solution is a controlled inner initialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(\lambda>0\) and a maximal monotone operator \(T\). Let consecutive exact proximal subproblem solutions be \(p_k=J_{\lambda T}(x^k)\) and \(p_{k-1}=J_{\lambda T}(x^{k-1})\). Because the resolvent is firmly nonexpansive, \[\|p_k-p_{k-1}\|\le\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|.\] Therefore initializing the inner method for subproblem \(k\) at the preceding solution \(z_k^0=p_{k-1}\) gives initial distance \(\|z_k^0-p_k\|\le\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|\). If only an approximation \(\tilde p_{k-1}\) is retained, the bound becomes \(\|\tilde p_{k-1}-p_k\|\le\|\tilde p_{k-1}-p_{k-1}\|+\|x^k-x^{k-1}\|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a fixed proximal parameter, the previous subproblem solution is no farther from the new solution than the change in outer centers.
assumptions_latex: The same parameter \(\lambda>0\) is used in both subproblems.

children.title: Continuation Across Subproblems
children.top_down_role: Transfer policies across changing proximal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Continuation Across Subproblems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfers inner state between successive proximal subproblems while preserving independent termination certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input outer centers \((x^k)\), parameters \((\lambda_k)\), an inner solver with state \(s\), and tolerances \((\varepsilon_k)\). Initialize the first inner state arbitrarily. For each \(k\), form the subproblem operator \(G_k(z)=T(z)+(z-x^k)/\lambda_k\), initialize with the terminal state from subproblem \(k-1\), and iterate until a computable certificate guarantees \(\operatorname{dist}(0,G_k(z))\le\varepsilon_k\). Set \(x^{k+1}=z\), retain the terminal state for iteration \(k+1\), and stop the outer process when its prescribed residual test holds. State transfer changes initialization only; every accepted point must satisfy the current subproblem's certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Carry the terminal inner state into the next proximal subproblem, but accept it only after certifying the new subproblem’s own tolerance.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) and each \(\lambda_k>0\) define the current proximal inclusion.
The inner solver exposes a transferable state and a valid residual certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is coherent and correctly keeps acceptance certificates specific to the current subproblem, but no authoritative locator supports this continuation framework.

children.title: Inner-Cost Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between inner effort and outer progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Cost Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logarithmic inner work under a linearly contracting subproblem solver and certified target accuracies.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose the inner solver for proximal subproblem \(k\) produces states \(z_k^m\) satisfying \(E_k^m\le\rho_k^mE_k^0\), where \(E_k^m\) is a certified nonnegative error measure and \(0<\rho_k<1\). To achieve \(E_k^m\le\varepsilon_k\), it suffices to use \[N_k=\left\lceil\frac{\log(E_k^0/\varepsilon_k)}{\log(1/\rho_k)}\right\rceil_+\] inner iterations, where \(\lceil a\rceil_+=\max\{0,\lceil a\rceil\}\). After \(K\) outer steps, total inner work is at most \(\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}N_k\). Tighter tolerances increase this work logarithmically, while warm starts reduce it through smaller initial errors \(E_k^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a linearly convergent inner solver, attaining tolerance costs logarithmically in the initial-error-to-tolerance ratio; warm starts reduce that ratio.

children.title: Subproblem Well-Posedness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Existence, uniqueness, and stability limits for proximal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Subproblem Well-Posedness Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp weak-convexity boundary for exact Euclidean proximal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, meaning that \(f+(\rho/2)\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex. For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), the function \(z\mapsto f(z)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|z-x\|^2\) is coercive and \((1/\lambda-\rho)\)-strongly convex; hence its minimizer exists and is unique. Moreover, \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}\) is Lipschitz with constant at most \((1-\lambda\rho)^{-1}\). Sharpness is witnessed by \(f(z)=-(\rho/2)\|z\|^2\): at \(\lambda=1/\rho\) and \(x=0\), every point minimizes, while for \(\lambda>1/\rho\) the infimum is \(-\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weakly convex function, proximal subproblems are uniquely solvable and stable below the reciprocal-curvature threshold; at or above it, uniqueness or existence can fail.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\) exists uniquely and is \((1-\lambda\rho)^{-1}\)-Lipschitz; the threshold \(\lambda=1/\rho\) is sharp.
review_flags: Exact weak-convexity threshold and Lipschitz bound require an authoritative locator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary content kind and weak-convexity result fit the terminal container, but the record has no cited source for the exact threshold and Lipschitz constant. The sharpness clause also requires rho>0; under the stated rho=0 convention, lambda=1/rho is not a finite boundary at which the example can be evaluated.

children.title: Proximal Oracle Cost Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes in which inner solution cost overwhelms outer progress.

assumptions_latex: \(K(\varepsilon)<\infty\) is the required number of outer iterations.
Each outer iteration has \(\Theta(1)\) overhead apart from its inner proximal solve.
\(C_k(\delta_k)\ge 0\) is the elementary-operation cost of the inner solve at iteration \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W(\varepsilon)=\Theta(K(\varepsilon))\) exactly when \(K(\varepsilon)^{-1}\sum_{k<K(\varepsilon)}C_k(\delta_k)=O(1)\); inner work dominates when this average tends to infinity.

notation.meaning: cost of the iteration-k proximal solve

review_flags: A source specifically supporting the inner-versus-outer cost model is required; the cited proximal-point section may not support this accounting boundary.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-work boundary separating inexpensive proximal access from inner-solve domination.

source_refs.locator: 2.6 Proximal point method p. 44
source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an outer proximal method requires \(K(\varepsilon)\) iterations and, at iteration \(k\), invokes an inner proximal solver with tolerance \(\delta_k\) and cost \(C_k(\delta_k)\ge 0\). Under an accounting model with \(\Theta(1)\) non-inner overhead per outer iteration, its total elementary work satisfies \[W(\varepsilon)=\Theta\!\left(K(\varepsilon)+\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}C_k(\delta_k)\right).\] Consequently, \(W(\varepsilon)=\Theta(K(\varepsilon))\) exactly when \(\sum_{k<K(\varepsilon)}C_k(\delta_k)=O(K(\varepsilon))\), while inner work dominates when that sum is \(\omega(K(\varepsilon))\). If \(C_k(\delta_k)=C(\varepsilon)\) for every executed iteration and \(C(\varepsilon)\to\infty\), then \(W(\varepsilon)=\Theta(K(\varepsilon)C(\varepsilon))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With constant-order outer overhead, total work is the outer iteration count plus all inner-solve costs. Outer iteration complexity remains a valid total-work bound exactly when average inner cost stays bounded; a diverging average inner cost dominates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accelerated two-block dual proximal gradient with an O(1/k^2) squared primal-recovery bound
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose p=2, f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty] is proper, closed, and \sigma-strongly convex with \sigma>0, each g_i:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty] is proper, closed, and convex, and \operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g_1)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g_2)\neq\varnothing. Let \{\mathbf{y}^k\}_{k\geq0} be generated by ADBPG, let \mathbf{y}^* be any dual optimal solution, and let \mathbf{x}^* be the primal optimal solution. For k\geq1, define \mathbf{x}^k=\arg\max_{\mathbf{x}}\{\langle\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}^k\rangle-f(\mathbf{x})-g_1(\mathbf{x})\}. Then \[\|\mathbf{x}^k-\mathbf{x}^*\|^2\leq\frac{4\|\mathbf{y}^0-\mathbf{y}^*\|^2}{\sigma^2(k+1)^2}.\]

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-step ISTA with an O(1/t) objective-gap bound
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fixed-step ISTA with an O(1/t) objective-gap bound
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=f+g on \mathbb{R}^n, where f is convex, differentiable, and \beta-smooth, g is convex, and the displayed proximal subproblem is attained and computationally accessible. If x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}F and \eta=1/\beta, define \[x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{g(x)+\frac{1}{2\eta}\left\|x-\bigl(x_t-\eta\nabla f(x_t)\bigr)\right\|_2^2\right\}.\] Then, for t\geq1, \[F(x_t)-F(x^*)\leq\frac{\beta\|x_1-x^*\|_2^2}{2t}.\] If g(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n g_i(x_i), the proximal update separates coordinatewise; for g(x)=\lambda\|x\|_1 it is soft thresholding with \tau_{\lambda\eta}(u)=(|u|-\lambda\eta)_+\operatorname{sign}(u).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For convex composite minimization, ISTA with step size 1/beta has a pointwise objective gap bounded by beta times the squared distance from x1 to a minimizer divided by 2t. Separable regularizers yield coordinatewise proximal steps, and the l1 case yields soft thresholding.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and the proximal subproblem is attained and computationally accessible}.

step_and_control_rule: forward gradient step followed by a proximal step

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strongly convex proximal gradient with an explicit linear distance contraction
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f have an L-Lipschitz gradient and strong-convexity modulus m>0, let \psi be convex, and let x^* be the unique minimizer of \phi=f+\tau\psi. For proximal-gradient iterates using \alpha=2/(m+L), \[\|x^k-x^*\|\leq\left(\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1}\right)^k\|x^0-x^*\|,\qquad \kappa=\frac{L}{m}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the smooth component is strongly convex and has an L-Lipschitz gradient, proximal gradient with step size 2/(m+L) converges globally and linearly in distance to the unique composite minimizer, with contraction factor (kappa-1)/(kappa+1).

conclusion.target: the unique minimizer of the strongly convex composite objective

The prescribed step size is 2/(m+L), not the 1/L or 1/beta step used in the basic ISTA objective-rate statement.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonsmooth Proximal Oracle
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact Euclidean proximal access to the simple composite term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. For \(\gamma>0\), a nonsmooth proximal oracle accepts \(v\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and returns the unique point \[\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(v)=\underset{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}{\operatorname{argmin}}\left\{g(z)+\frac{1}{2\gamma}\|z-v\|^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, its output \(z\) satisfies \(0\in\partial g(z)+\gamma^{-1}(z-v)\), or \(v-z\in\gamma\partial g(z)\). Thus the oracle evaluates the resolvent \((I+\gamma\partial g)^{-1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nonsmooth oracle minimizes the simple term plus a quadratic, equivalently evaluating the subdifferential resolvent at the supplied point.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Composite Specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Projected-gradient specialization obtained by using a feasibility indicator as the simple term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty, closed, and convex, and define its indicator by \(\delta_C(x)=0\) for \(x\in C\) and \(\delta_C(x)=+\infty\) otherwise. Then \[\underset{x\in C}{\operatorname{minimize}}\ f(x)=\underset{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}{\operatorname{minimize}}\ \bigl(f(x)+\delta_C(x)\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}(v)=P_C(v).\] Consequently, proximal gradient for \(f+\delta_C\) is projected gradient: \(x^{k+1}=P_C(x^k-\gamma_k\nabla f(x^k))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Representing feasibility by a convex-set indicator turns its proximal mapping into Euclidean projection and proximal gradient into projected gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma\delta_C}=P_C\), so forward-backward iteration specializes to projected gradient.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m\ge 1\) be an integer. Given differentiable losses \(\ell_i:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\) for \(i\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\), a proper closed convex regularizer \(R:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and \(\lambda>0\), regularized estimation has the composite form \[F(x)=f(x)+g(x),\qquad f(x)=\frac{1}{m}\sum_{i=1}^m\ell_i(x),\qquad g(x)=\lambda R(x).\] If \(\nabla f\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma_k\lambda R}\) are computable for a stepsize \(\gamma_k>0\), one proximal-gradient update is \[x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma_k\lambda R}\bigl(x^k-\gamma_k\nabla f(x^k)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A regularized estimation objective can be represented as a differentiable average data loss plus a proximable convex structural penalty, yielding the displayed proximal-gradient update.

abla f(x)+\partial g(x)\). Define \[T_\gamma=(I+\gamma\partial g)^{-1}(I-\gamma
abla f)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(I-\gamma
abla f).\] Then \(0\in
abla f(x)+\partial g(x)\) if and only if \(x=T_\gamma x\). Thus fixed-stepsize proximal gradient has the fixed-point representation \(x^{k+1}=T_\gamma x^k\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=f+g\), a base point \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), and \(\gamma>0\), define the local model \[Q_\gamma(z;x)=f(x)+\langle
abla f(x),z-xangle+ rac{1}{2\gamma}\|z-x\|^2+g(z).\] If \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, then \[\underset{z}{\operatorname{argmin}}\ Q_\gamma(z;x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma
abla f(x)).\] If additionally \(
abla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(0<\gamma\le 1/L\), then \(F(z)\le Q_\gamma(z;x)\) for every \(z\), so the model majorizes the objective while agreeing with it at \(z=x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-gradient step exactly minimizes a linearized smooth term plus the original simple term and a quadratic; suitable stepsizes make this model a majorizer.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Gradient Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scaled proximal-gradient displacement used as a composite stationarity measure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), with \(f\) differentiable, \(g\) proper, closed, and convex, and \(\gamma>0\), the composite gradient mapping is \[G_\gamma(x)= rac1\gamma\left(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\gamma g}(x-\gamma
abla f(x))ight).\] Writing \(x^+=x-\gamma G_\gamma(x)\), proximal optimality gives \(G_\gamma(x)-
abla f(x)\in\partial g(x^+)\). Moreover, \(G_\gamma(x)=0\) if and only if \(0\in
abla f(x)+\partial g(x)\); for convex \(F\), this is equivalent to \(x\in\operatorname{argmin}F\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f,g_1,\ldots,g_p\) satisfy Assumption 11.1(A)–(B). For \(L>0\), \(i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), and \(x\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\), define
\[
G_L^i(x)=L\bigl(x_i-T_L^i(x)\bigr).

If \(g_i\equiv0\), then

G_L^i(x)=\nabla_i f(x).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected gradient point and reduced gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The constrained Euclidean gradient mapping, viewed as the indicator-function specialization of the composite gradient-mapping framework.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n$ be nonempty, closed, and convex, let $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable, and let $\gamma>0$. children.title: Objective-Gap Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Objective-Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal suboptimality certificate relative to an attained or certified lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) have finite optimum \(F^*=\inf_xF(x)\). For any feasible \(x\), the objective gap is \(\Delta_F(x)=F(x)-F^*\ge0\), and \(\Delta_F(x)\le\varepsilon\) certifies \(\varepsilon\)-optimality. If \(F^*\) is unknown but a verifiable lower bound \(L\le F^*\) is available, then \(F(x)-F^*\le F(x)-L\); therefore \(F(x)-L\le\varepsilon\) is a computable sufficient certificate. Without an exact optimum or certified lower bound, the raw objective value alone does not certify suboptimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subtracting the optimum gives the exact suboptimality certificate; subtracting any certified lower bound gives a computable conservative certificate.
assumptions_latex: When used, \(L\le F^*\) is independently certified.

notation.meaning: certified lower bound on the optimum

children.title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificates

knowledge_statements.title: Primal–Dual Gap Certificates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel primal–dual gap for linearly composed convex objectives.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the primal problem \(P^*=\inf_x\{P(x)=g(x)+f(Ax)\}\), where \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex and \(A\) is linear. Its Fenchel dual objective is \(D(y)=-f^*(y)-g^*(-A^*y)\). For any \(x\in\operatorname{dom}P\) and dual-feasible \(y\), weak duality gives the computable gap \[\mathcal{G}(x,y)=P(x)-D(y)=g(x)+f(Ax)+f^*(y)+g^*(-A^*y)\ge0.\] Moreover, \(P(x)-P^*\le\mathcal{G}(x,y)\); hence \(\mathcal{G}(x,y)\le\varepsilon\) certifies primal \(\varepsilon\)-optimality, regardless of whether strong duality is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible primal–dual pair yields a nonnegative Fenchel gap that upper-bounds primal suboptimality and therefore supplies a computable stopping certificate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) are proper, closed, and convex.
\(x\) and \(y\) make all displayed primal and dual terms finite.

knowledge_statements.title: Computable Gap Surrogates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A proximal-gradient residual yields a computable objective-gap surrogate when a solution-distance bound is known.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(f\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. For \(0<t\leq 1/L\), define \(x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(x-t
abla f(x))\), \(G_t(x)=t^{-1}(x-x^+)\), and \(v^+=G_t(x)+
abla f(x^+)-
abla f(x)\). Then \(v^+\in\partial F(x^+)\) and \(\|v^+\|\leq(1+Lt)\|G_t(x)\|\). If a minimizer \(x^\star\) exists and a known bound \(\|x^+-x^\star\|\leq R\) holds, then \[0\leq F(x^+)-F(x^\star)\leq R(1+Lt)\|G_t(x)\|.\] Thus the displayed right-hand side is a computable objective-gap surrogate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal-gradient mapping supplies a computable subgradient residual; with a known distance-to-solution bound, its norm gives an explicit upper bound on objective suboptimality.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and has an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
A minimizer and a certified bound \(\|x^+-x^\star\|\leq R\) are available.

notation.meaning: Computable subgradient of the composite objective at the proximal-gradient point.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Availability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes unconditional residual computation from objective- and primal–dual-gap certification, which require additional global information.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=f+g\) with a computable gradient and proximal map, the residual \(\|G_t(x)\|\) is available after one proximal-gradient step. An objective-gap certificate \(F(x)-F^\star\leq\varepsilon\) is available only when a valid computable lower bound \(\ell\leq F^\star\) is also known, in which case \(F(x)-\ell\leq\varepsilon\) suffices. For a Fenchel formulation \(\min_x h(Ax)+g(x)\), a primal–dual gap is available when one can construct \(y\) satisfying dual feasibility and evaluate \[\mathcal G(x,y)=h(Ax)+g(x)+h^*(y)+g^*(-A^*y).\] Then \(\mathcal G(x,y)\geq F(x)-F^\star\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residuals require only the gradient and proximal map. Objective gaps need a lower bound; primal–dual gaps additionally need a feasible dual point and evaluable conjugates.
assumptions_latex: All displayed function and conjugate values are finite and computable at the certificate points.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal G(x,y)\geq F(x)-F^\star\), while \(F(x)-\ell\) certifies the objective gap whenever \(\ell\leq F^\star\).

knowledge_statements.title: Basic Proximal Gradient Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-step forward–backward iteration for minimizing a smooth-plus-proximable composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), choose \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}g\) and \(t\in(0,1/L]\). For \(k=0,1,\ldots\), compute \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(x_k-t\nabla f(x_k))=\arg\min_z\left\{g(z)+\langle\nabla f(x_k),z-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2t}\|z-x_k\|^2\right\}.\] Stop when a prescribed iteration limit is reached or a computable criterion such as \(\|t^{-1}(x_k-x_{k+1})\|\leq\varepsilon\) holds, and return \(x_{k+1}\). For convex \(f\) and \(g\), every cluster point is a minimizer when minimizers exist; in finite dimensions the iterates converge to a minimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from a point in the domain of the nonsmooth term, repeatedly take a gradient step on the smooth term and apply the proximal map. Under the stated convexity, smoothness, stepsize, and existence assumptions, the finite-dimensional iterate sequence converges to a minimizer.

\(g\) is proper, closed, and convex with a computable proximal map.
The minimizer set of \(F=f+g\) is nonempty.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Euclidean proximal-gradient model update
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the Euclidean forward-backward update in model-minimization form. The extract does not restate step-parameter, convexity, existence, or uniqueness assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{In the Euclidean setting,}\qquad \mathbf x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb E}\left\{f(\mathbf x^k)+\langle\nabla f(\mathbf x^k),\mathbf x-\mathbf x^k\rangle+g(\mathbf x)+\frac{L_k}{2}\|\mathbf x-\mathbf x^k\|^2\right\}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In Euclidean geometry, the proximal-gradient update is written as the minimizer of the first-order model of f at x^k plus g and the quadratic proximity term (L_k/2)||x−x^k||².
assumptions_latex: \mathbb E\text{ is endowed with Euclidean geometry}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb E}\left\{f(\mathbf x^k)+\langle\nabla f(\mathbf x^k),\mathbf x-\mathbf x^k\rangle+g(\mathbf x)+\frac{L_k}{2}\|\mathbf x-\mathbf x^k\|^2\right\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Proximal-gradient update for an additive composite objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the basic forward-backward step and its two optimization representations; it makes no convergence claim. Well-definedness is retained because the extracted span does not restate the standing assumptions on the proximal operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(F(x)=f(x)+g(x)\) on \(\mathbb E\), let \(f\) be differentiable at \(x^k\), let \(t_k>0\), and suppose the displayed proximal minimization is well-defined. Then
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb E}\left\{f(x^k)+\langle\nabla f(x^k),x-x^k\rangle+g(x)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb E}\left\{t_kg(x)+\frac12\left\|x-\bigl(x^k-t_k\nabla f(x^k)\bigr)\right\|^2\right\}
=\operatorname{prox}_{t_kg}\!\left(x^k-t_k\nabla f(x^k)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proximal-gradient step minimizes the smooth term's linearization plus the original nonsmooth term and a quadratic regularizer. Equivalently, it applies the proximal operator of the scaled nonsmooth term after a gradient step on the smooth term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{t_kg}(x^k-t_k\nabla f(x^k))\text{ with the two displayed equivalent argmin representations}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Basic proximal-gradient algorithm with reciprocal curvature steps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the initialization and deterministic iteration rule. The update is defined only at iterations where the gradient and proximal evaluation exist; no stepsize acceptance rule or convergence guarantee is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\). For each \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), choose \(L_k>0\) and, whenever the displayed quantities are well-defined, set
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{g/L_k}\!\left(x^k-\frac{1}{L_k}\nabla f(x^k)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize in the interior of the domain of f. At each well-defined iteration, choose a positive curvature parameter, take a gradient step of length 1/L_k, and apply the proximal operator of g/L_k. The extract does not impose a line-search or convergence condition on L_k.
assumptions_latex: \nabla f(x^k)\text{ and }\operatorname{prox}_{g/L_k}(x^k-L_k^{-1}\nabla f(x^k))\text{ are well-defined at each executed iteration}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Prox-grad operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the deterministic forward-backward update mapping. Its stated codomain presupposes that the gradient and proximal evaluation are single-valued and well-defined on the indicated domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(L>0\), the prox-grad operator \(T_L^{f,g}:\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)\to\mathbb E\) is defined by
\[
T_L^{f,g}(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{g/L}\!\left(x-\frac{1}{L}\nabla f(x)\right).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a positive parameter L, the prox-grad operator maps a point in the interior of the domain of f to the result of a gradient step of length 1/L followed by the proximal operator of g/L.
assumptions_latex: \nabla f(x)\text{ and }\operatorname{prox}_{g/L}(x-L^{-1}\nabla f(x))\text{ are single-valued and well-defined}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected Gradient Iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Smooth optimization over a closed convex set using Euclidean projection and descent-enforcing step lengths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Omega\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be closed and convex, let \(\nabla f\) be \(L\)-Lipschitz continuous, and take \(x^0\in\Omega\). The projected-gradient iteration is
\[
x^{k+1}=P_{\Omega}\!\left(x^k-\alpha_k\nabla f(x^k)\right),\qquad \alpha_k>0,
\]
where \(\alpha_k\) is selected to ensure descent in \(f\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Projected gradient takes a negative-gradient step and projects it onto the closed convex feasible set. Its positive step length is selected to ensure descent.
assumptions_latex: \alpha_k>0\text{ is selected to ensure descent in }f

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convergence and Finite Termination of Fixed-Step Projected Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global convergence under convex smoothness, with stronger conclusions under strong convexity, Hessian bounds, or sharpness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let $Q\subset\mathbb{R}^n$ be closed and convex, let $f$ be convex and differentiable with $L$-Lipschitz gradient on $Q$, and suppose $X^*=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in Q}f(x)\neq\varnothing$. For
\[
x^{k+1}=P_Q(x^k-\gamma\nabla f(x^k)),\qquad 0<\gamma<2/L,
\]
the iterates converge to some $x^*\in X^*$. If $f$ is strongly convex, convergence is geometric. If, additionally, $f$ is twice differentiable and
\[
\ell I\preceq\nabla^2f(x)\preceq LI\quad(x\in Q),\qquad \ell>0,
\]
the progression ratio is
\[
q=\max\{|1-\gamma\ell|,|1-\gamma L|\}.
\]
If the attained minimizer is sharp, then $x^k=x^*$ for some finite $k$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-step projected gradient converges for a convex smooth objective when the step is strictly between zero and 2/L. Strong convexity gives geometric convergence, the stated Hessian bounds give an explicit ratio, and a sharp minimizer is reached finitely.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ is convex and differentiable on }Q
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^k\to x^*\in X^*;\quad f\text{ strongly convex}\Rightarrow\text{ geometric convergence};\quad \ell I\preceq\nabla^2f\preceq LI\Rightarrow q=\max\{|1-\gamma\ell|,|1-\gamma L|\};\quad x^*\text{ sharp}\Rightarrow\exists k:\ x^k=x^*

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projected-gradient update and quadratic-model representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a Euclidean projected-gradient step. Nonemptiness, closedness, and convexity of the feasible set are stated explicitly because they ensure a single-valued projection and the asserted argmin representation, although they are implicit rather than written in this extracted span.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(\min\{f(x):x\in C\}\), suppose \(C\subseteq\mathbb E\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, \(f\) is differentiable at \(x^k\), and \(t_k>0\). The projected-gradient update is
\[
x^{k+1}=P_C\!\left(x^k-t_k\nabla f(x^k)\right).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in C}\left\{f(x^k)+\langle\nabla f(x^k),x-x^k\rangle+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|x-x^k\|^2\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a differentiable objective over a nonempty closed convex feasible set, projected gradient projects an ordinary gradient step onto that set. Equivalently, the iterate uniquely minimizes the objective's linearization plus a positive quadratic regularizer over the feasible set.
assumptions_latex: C\subseteq\mathbb E\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.title: ISTA Framework
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal-gradient specialization for least-squares loss with an entrywise ℓ1 penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For data \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(\lambda>0\), consider \(F(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\). Choose \(x_0\in\mathbb{R}^n\). If \(A\neq0\), choose \(0<t\leq\|A\|_2^{-2}\); if \(A=0\), choose any \(t>0\). Iterate \[x_{k+1}=S_{t\lambda}\bigl(x_k-tA^*(Ax_k-b)\bigr),\qquad (S_\tau(z))_i=\operatorname{sign}(z_i)\max\{|z_i|-\tau,0\}.\] Stop when \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|/t\leq\varepsilon\) or an iteration limit is reached, and return \(x_{k+1}\). This is the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ISTA alternates a least-squares gradient step with coordinatewise soft thresholding at level tλ; the usual inverse-spectral-norm stepsize bound applies when the data matrix is nonzero.

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise soft-thresholding operator at level τ.
Euclidean adjoint, equivalently the transpose, of A.
