knowledge_statements.statement_title: ISTA update, objective rate, and soft-thresholding specialization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed-step ISTA for unconstrained convex composite minimization, including separable proximal subproblems and the ℓ1 soft-thresholding case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and \(\beta\)-smooth, \(g\) is convex, and the displayed proximal subproblem is attained and computationally accessible. If \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\) and \(\eta=1/\beta\), ISTA uses
\[
x_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{g(x)+\frac{1}{2\eta}\left\|x-\bigl(x_t-\eta\nabla f(x_t)\bigr)\right\|_2^2\right\}.
\]
For \(t\ge1\),
\[
F(x_t)-F(x^*)\le \frac{\beta\|x_1-x^*\|_2^2}{2t}.
\]
If \(g(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n g_i(x_i)\), the proximal update separates into \(n\) one-dimensional convex problems. In particular, if \(g(x)=\lambda\|x\|_1\), the update is coordinatewise soft thresholding with
\[
\tau_{\lambda\eta}(u)=(|u|-\lambda\eta)_+\operatorname{sign}(u).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ISTA applies a gradient step to the smooth term and then solves the proximal problem for the simple convex term. Under the convex beta-smooth composite assumptions and step size 1/beta, its objective gap is bounded by beta times the squared initial distance to a minimizer divided by 2t. Separable terms yield coordinatewise proximal problems, and an l1 term yields soft thresholding.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and the proximal subproblem is attained and computationally accessible}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: ISTA for LASSO
knowledge_statements.scope_note: LASSO-specific forward-backward soft-thresholding iteration and its stepsize guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\lambda>0\), consider \(\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\frac12\|Ax-b\|^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\). The forward-backward iteration \[x^{k+1}=S\!\left(x^k-\alpha A^\top(Ax^k-b);\alpha\lambda\right)\] is the iterative shrinkage-thresholding algorithm (ISTA), and it converges when \(0<\alpha<2/\lambda_{\max}(A^\top A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For LASSO, ISTA applies soft thresholding after a gradient step on the least-squares loss. It converges for stepsizes strictly between zero and twice the reciprocal of the largest eigenvalue of A-transpose A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^{k+1}=S\!\left(x^k-\alpha A^\top(Ax^k-b);\alpha\lambda\right)\ \text{is ISTA and converges under the stated stepsize condition.}

knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Thresholding Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form proximal representation for weighted entrywise ℓ1 regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i|x_i|\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(\lambda_i\geq0\), and let \(t>0\). The proximal map is coordinatewise: \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(z)\bigr)_i=\operatorname{sign}(z_i)\max\{|z_i|-t\lambda_i,0\}.\] Consequently, for any differentiable \(f\) and any positive proximal-gradient stepsize \(t_k>0\), \[x_{k+1,i}=\operatorname{sign}(u_{k,i})\max\{|u_{k,i}|-t_k\lambda_i,0\},\qquad u_k=x_k-t_k\nabla f(x_k).\] Zero weights leave their coordinates unchanged by the proximal operation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A weighted ℓ1 proximal step soft-thresholds each coordinate independently, subtracting its scaled weight from the magnitude and truncating at zero.
assumptions_latex: The proximal parameter \(t\) and every iteration stepsize \(t_k\) used in the displayed formulas are positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Group-Thresholding Specializations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form block proximal representation for disjoint group ℓ2 penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal G\) partition the coordinates of \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and define \(g(x)=\sum_{G\in\mathcal G}\lambda_G\|x_G\|_2\) with \(\lambda_G\geq0\). For \(t>0\), the proximal map separates by groups and obeys \[\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(z)\bigr)_G=\left(1-\frac{t\lambda_G}{\|z_G\|_2}\right)_+z_G,\] with the value defined as \(0\) when \(z_G=0\). Hence a proximal-gradient iteration applies this block-thresholding formula to \(z=x_k-t_k\nabla f(x_k)\) independently for every \(G\in\mathcal G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For disjoint group ℓ2 penalties, the proximal map shrinks each block radially and sets blocks below their thresholds to zero.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal G\) is a partition into disjoint coordinate groups.

notation.meaning: Coordinate block indexed by group G.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonseparable Regularizer Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordinate or block thresholding fails when the regularizer does not decompose over the chosen partition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex. The identity \[\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(z)=\bigl(\operatorname{prox}_{tg_i}(z_i)\bigr)_{i=1}^n\] is justified when \(g(x)=\sum_i g_i(x_i)\), and the analogous block identity requires decomposition over disjoint blocks. Without such separability, independent thresholding need not equal the proximal map. For example, with \(g(x)=\lambda|x_1-x_2|\), the proximal subproblem couples both coordinates; its solution generally cannot be obtained by soft-thresholding \(z_1\) and \(z_2\) separately. Proximal gradient remains applicable only if the coupled proximal map can be computed or acceptably approximated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Thresholding formulas depend on separability. Coupled penalties generally require a joint proximal solve, although the broader proximal-gradient method may still apply.
assumptions_latex: The proposed implementation thresholds coordinates or disjoint blocks independently.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(g\) is not separable over those blocks, independent thresholding is not generally equal to \(\operatorname{prox}_{tg}\).

notation.meaning: Coordinatewise component of a separable regularizer.

children.title: Backtracking Proximal Gradient

knowledge_statements.title: Backtracking Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward–backward iteration using backtracking until the smooth term satisfies a local quadratic upper model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x_k\), an initial trial curvature \(M>0\), and \(\eta>1\), repeatedly set \(t=1/M\) and \(z=\operatorname{prox}_{tg}(x_k-t
abla f(x_k))\). Accept \(z\) when \[f(z)\leq f(x_k)+\langle
abla f(x_k),z-x_kangle+ rac{M}{2}\|z-x_k\|^2;\] otherwise replace \(M\) by \(\eta M\) and retry. Set \(x_{k+1}=z\), optionally use the accepted curvature to initialize the next search, and stop on a prescribed residual or iteration criterion. If \(
abla f\) is globally \(L\)-Lipschitz, backtracking terminates once \(M\geq L\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increase the trial curvature until the gradient quadratic model majorizes the smooth term at the proposed proximal point, then accept that point.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex with a computable proximal map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The inner search terminates for \(M\geq L\), and the accepted point satisfies the displayed local-majorization test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Fast Proximal-Gradient Method with Backtracking
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated proximal-gradient iteration using geometric backtracking until a local quadratic-majorization test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose \(L_0>0\), \(\eta>1\), and \(x_0\in\mathbb E\); set \(y_1=x_0\) and \(t_1=1\). For each \(k\ge1\), let \(i_k\) be the smallest nonnegative integer such that, with \(\bar L=\eta^{i_k}L_{k-1}\), \[F(p_{\bar L}(y_k))\le Q_{\bar L}(p_{\bar L}(y_k),y_k).\] Set \(L_k=\eta^{i_k}L_{k-1}\) and compute \[x_k=p_{L_k}(y_k),\qquad t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2},\qquad y_{k+1}=x_k+\frac{t_k-1}{t_{k+1}}(x_k-x_{k-1}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting with L₀>0 and η>1, increase the trial curvature geometrically until the proximal point satisfies the quadratic-majorization test. Accept that curvature, take the proximal-gradient step, update the acceleration parameter, and extrapolate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \forall k\ge1:\quad i_k=\min\{i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}:F(p_{\eta^iL_{k-1}}(y_k))\le Q_{\eta^iL_{k-1}}(p_{\eta^iL_{k-1}}(y_k),y_k)\},\quad L_k=\eta^{i_k}L_{k-1},\quad x_k=p_{L_k}(y_k),\quad t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}2,\quad y_{k+1}=x_k+\frac{t_k-1}{t_{k+1}}(x_k-x_{k-1})

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Residual-Based Backtracking Procedure for Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A multiplicative search for a proximal-gradient parameter satisfying a sufficient-decrease test.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix $s>0$, $\gamma\in(0,1)$, and $\eta>1$. Given $x^k$, initialize $L_k\leftarrow s$. While $$F(x^k)-F(T_{L_k}(x^k))<\frac{\gamma}{L_k}\|G_{L_k}(x^k)\|^2,$$ replace $L_k\leftarrow\eta L_k$. Equivalently, select $L_k=s\eta^{i_k}$, where $i_k$ is the smallest $i\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ satisfying $$F(x^k)-F(T_{s\eta^i}(x^k))\ge\frac{\gamma}{s\eta^i}\|G_{s\eta^i}(x^k)\|^2.$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from s, repeatedly multiply the proximal-gradient parameter by eta until the objective decrease is at least gamma divided by the parameter times the squared gradient-mapping norm. The accepted exponent is the smallest nonnegative exponent satisfying this test.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform bounds for B3 backtracking parameters
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform bounds on the curvature parameters generated by proximal-gradient backtracking procedure B3.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb E\to\mathbb R\) be convex and \(L_f\)-smooth, with \(L_f>0\). knowledge_statements.statement_title: Persistent-curvature backtracking for proximal gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking procedure B2 retains the preceding accepted curvature estimate and increases it geometrically until the proximal-gradient trial satisfies a local quadratic upper-model test. The extracted algorithm does not independently prove that the search terminates finitely.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choose s>0 and \eta>1 and set L_{-1}=s. At iteration k\ge0, initialize L_k=L_{k-1}. While f(T_{L_k}(x^k))>f(x^k)+\langle\nabla f(x^k),T_{L_k}(x^k)-x^k\rangle+\frac{L_k}{2}\|T_{L_k}(x^k)-x^k\|^2, replace L_k\leftarrow\eta L_k. Upon termination, accept the first curvature satisfying the reversed, non-strict inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start each iteration from the previous curvature estimate and multiply it by a fixed factor greater than one until the proximal-gradient trial satisfies the local quadratic-majorization condition; accept the first successful trial.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{If the search terminates, }L_k=L_{k-1}\eta^{i_k}\text{ for the least }i_k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\text{ satisfying the local quadratic-majorization test.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backtracking by local quadratic majorization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking rule that increases the inverse stepsize until the smooth term satisfies its local quadratic upper model at the trial proximal-gradient point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(s>0\) and \(\eta>1\), and set \(L_{-1}=s\). At iteration \(k\ge0\), let \(i_k\) be the smallest integer \(i\ge0\) such that, with \(\ell=L_{k-1}\eta^i\),
\[
f(V_\ell(x^k))\le f(x^k)+\langle\nabla f(x^k),V_\ell(x^k)-x^k\rangle+\frac{\ell}{2}\|V_\ell(x^k)-x^k\|^2.
\]
Then set \(L_k=L_{k-1}\eta^{i_k}\). Equivalently, initialize \(L_k=L_{k-1}\) and repeatedly replace \(L_k\) by \(\eta L_k\) while the displayed inequality fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Begin with the preceding inverse stepsize and multiply it by eta until the trial proximal-gradient point satisfies the local quadratic upper bound for f; accept the first such value.

children.title: Spectral Stepsize Policies
children.top_down_role: Stepsize selection based on secant-style spectral information.

knowledge_statements.title: Spectral Stepsize Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Barzilai–Borwein curvature estimates used as trial stepsizes for proximal-gradient iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For consecutive iterates define \(s_k=x_k-x_{k-1}\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_k)-
abla f(x_{k-1})\). When the denominators are positive, the two standard spectral trial steps are \[t_k^{\mathrm{BB1}}= rac{\langle s_k,s_kangle}{\langle s_k,y_kangle},\qquad t_k^{\mathrm{BB2}}= rac{\langle s_k,y_kangle}{\langle y_k,y_kangle}.\] Choose one formula or a prescribed alternation, project the result onto \([t_{\min},t_{\max}]\), and use it as the trial value in \(x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{t_kg}(x_k-t_k
abla f(x_k))\). A line search or acceptance test is required when the spectral proposal alone does not guarantee descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Spectral policies estimate inverse curvature from consecutive steps and gradient changes, safeguard the estimate, and use it as a proximal-gradient trial stepsize.
assumptions_latex: Consecutive iterates and gradients are available.
The selected spectral quotient has a positive nonzero denominator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t_k=\Pi_{[t_{\min},t_{\max}]}(t_k^{\mathrm{BB1}})\) or \(t_k=\Pi_{[t_{\min},t_{\max}]}(t_k^{\mathrm{BB2}})\) is used as a trial proximal-gradient stepsize.

notation.meaning: Projection onto the safeguarded stepsize interval.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The safeguarded BB trial-step policy is standard, but the record has no citation for the two formulas or their use within proximal-gradient line search.

children.title: Adaptive Stepsize Policies
children.top_down_role: Stepsize adjustment based on observed local behavior.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Stepsize Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Iteration-dependent trial steps combined with a local majorization acceptance rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(0<t_{\min}\leq t_{\max}\), \(\eta>1\), and choose a trial proposal \(\widehat t_k\in[t_{\min},t_{\max}]\) from available iteration history. Set \(t_k=\widehat t_k\) and compute \(z_k=\operatorname{prox}_{t_kg}(x_k-t_k\nabla f(x_k))\). While \[f(z_k)>f(x_k)+\langle\nabla f(x_k),z_k-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|z_k-x_k\|^2,\] replace \(t_k\) by \(t_k/\eta\) and recompute \(z_k\). Then set \(x_{k+1}=z_k\). Stop when \(\|x_k-x_{k+1}\|/t_k\leq\varepsilon\) or an iteration limit is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Propose a history-dependent stepsize, shrink it until local majorization holds, and accept the resulting proximal-gradient point.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex with a computable proximal map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each accepted \((t_k,x_{k+1})\) satisfies the displayed local-majorization inequality.

children.title: Safeguarded Curvature Estimates
children.top_down_role: Protected use of empirical curvature information.

knowledge_statements.title: Safeguarded Curvature Estimates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Clipping and fallback conditions that keep curvature-based proximal-gradient steps positive and bounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat L_k\) be any finite raw curvature estimate and fix \(0<L_{\min}\leq L_{\max}<+\infty\). Define \[L_k=\min\{L_{\max},\max\{L_{\min},\widehat L_k\}\},\qquad t_k=L_k^{-1}.\] If the raw estimate is undefined, nonfinite, or based on a nonpositive secant denominator, replace it by a prescribed fallback in \([L_{\min},L_{\max}]\). Then \(1/L_{\max}\leq t_k\leq1/L_{\min}\). If the proximal-gradient trial point fails the local quadratic-majorization test, increase \(L_k\) geometrically, subject to revising \(L_{\max}\) when necessary, until the test holds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Clip curvature estimates to a positive finite interval, use a fallback for invalid secant data, and increase curvature when the acceptance test fails.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(1/L_{\max}\leq t_k\leq1/L_{\min}\), and invalid raw estimates cannot produce nonpositive or infinite stepsizes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Clipping and fallback conditions are plausible, but no source is supplied, and the instruction to revise \(L_{\max}\) during backtracking leaves unclear whether the previously asserted stepsize bounds use the original or updated safeguard.

children.title: Unreliable Curvature Boundary
children.top_down_role: Failure regimes for unstable or misleading local curvature estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Unreliable Curvature Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secant curvature can be undefined or nonpositive, so unsafeguarded reciprocal-curvature steps are not generally valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a spectral estimate based on \(s_k=x_k-x_{k-1}\) and \(y_k=
abla f(x_k)-
abla f(x_{k-1})\), the quotient \(\langle s_k,s_kangle/\langle s_k,y_kangle\) is unusable when \(\langle s_k,y_kangle\leq0\), and \(\langle s_k,y_kangle/\langle y_k,y_kangle\) is undefined when \(y_k=0\). For the affine function \(f(x)=a^Tx\), every pair has \(y_k=0\). For the nonconvex quadratic \(f(x)=-	frac12\|x\|^2\), one has \(y_k=-s_k\) and \(\langle s_k,y_kangle=-\|s_k\|^2<0\) whenever \(s_k
eq0\). Thus unsafeguarded spectral steps can be undefined or negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Flat gradients make spectral quotients undefined, while negative curvature can make them negative; fallback bounds or acceptance tests are therefore necessary.
assumptions_latex: The stepsize is computed solely from consecutive secant pairs.
No positivity safeguard or fallback rule is imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resulting spectral trial stepsize need not be finite or positive.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The flat-gradient and negative-curvature examples correctly exhibit undefined or negative spectral quotients and fit the failure-boundary leaf, but the record provides no inspectable citation.

children.title: Curvature-Agnostic Adaptation Policies

children.title: Universal Curvature Adaptation
children.top_down_role: Adaptation across unknown smoothness or curvature regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Universal Curvature Adaptation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A curvature-agnostic composite step based on an adaptively validated inexact quadratic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\), where \(f\) is convex and differentiable and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. Given \(y_k\), tolerance \(\delta_k\ge 0\), and a trial curvature \(M>0\), compute \[x(M)=\operatorname{prox}_{g/M}\!\left(y_k-M^{-1}\nabla f(y_k)\right).\] Increase \(M\) geometrically until \[f(x(M))\le f(y_k)+\langle\nabla f(y_k),x(M)-y_k\rangle+\frac{M}{2}\|x(M)-y_k\|^2+\frac{\delta_k}{2}.\] Set \(x_{k+1}=x(M)\) and retain the accepted \(M\) as the next trial value. The policy requires neither a supplied Lipschitz constant nor a supplied Hölder exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly enlarge a local curvature estimate until an inexact quadratic upper model is valid, then accept the associated proximal-gradient point.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable on a convex domain containing all iterates.
\(g\) is proper, closed, and convex, and its proximal map is computable.
The geometric curvature-increase factor is strictly greater than \(1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted iterate satisfies the displayed local model test without prior knowledge of a global curvature constant.

notation.meaning: allowed model error at iteration k
proximal map of g with quadratic coefficient M

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but no citation fixes the intended universal composite method. In particular, the assumptions allow delta_k=0 and give no Hölder or Lipschitz regularity sufficient to validate finite termination of the curvature search. An authoritative locator is required before the formulation can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Parameter-Free Stepsize Policies
children.top_down_role: Stepsize selection without prescribed global curvature constants.

knowledge_statements.title: Parameter-Free Stepsize Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Backtracking proximal gradient requiring no supplied smoothness constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=f+g\), choose \(x_0\), a trial stepsize \(\widehat\alpha_k>0\), and \(\beta\in(0,1)\). Starting with \(\alpha=\widehat\alpha_k\), form \[z=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha g}\!\left(x_k-\alpha\nabla f(x_k)\right).\] While \[f(z)>f(x_k)+\langle\nabla f(x_k),z-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha}\|z-x_k\|^2,\] replace \(\alpha\) by \(\beta\alpha\) and recompute \(z\). Set \(x_{k+1}=z\) and initialize the next trial from the accepted stepsize, optionally enlarged by a fixed factor. Stopping may use \(\|x_{k+1}-x_k\|/\alpha\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shrink a trial stepsize until the smooth term satisfies its local quadratic model; no Lipschitz constant is supplied to the method.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and has Lipschitz gradient on the relevant level set.
\(g\) is proper, closed, and convex with a computable proximal map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Backtracking terminates after finitely many reductions, and each accepted point is a valid proximal-gradient update.

knowledge_statements.title: Unknown-Smoothness Regimes

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An unknown-smoothness regime consists of minimizing \(F=f+g\) over a finite-dimensional normed space when there exist unknown parameters \(
u\in[0,1]\) and \(M_
u>0\) such that \[\|
abla f(x)-
abla f(y)\|_*\le M_
u\|x-y\|^
u\] for all relevant \(x,y\), while \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. The algorithm may query \(f\), \(

children.title: Adaptation-Overhead Boundary
children.top_down_role: Costs introduced by learning scale or curvature online.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptation-Overhead Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case trial count for geometric proximal-gradient backtracking under Lipschitz smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and a backtracking iteration begins with \(\widehat\alpha_k>0\), replacing \(\alpha\) by \(\beta\alpha\) with \(\beta\in(0,1)\) until the standard quadratic model test holds. Because that test holds whenever \(\alpha\le L^{-1}\), the number \(r_k\) of rejected trials satisfies \[r_k\le \max\!\left\{0,\left\lceil\log_{1/\beta}(L\widehat\alpha_k)\right\rceil\right\}.\] Thus one accepted step uses at most \(r_k+1\) model tests and proximal evaluations. This logarithmic overhead is the geometric-backtracking boundary; it does not cover arbitrary trial-growth rules or non-Lipschitz gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Geometric backtracking adds at most logarithmically many rejected trials, measured by the ratio between the initial trial stepsize and the safe Lipschitz stepsize.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz on every tested segment.
Every trial evaluates the same standard quadratic upper-model condition.

notation.meaning: number of rejected trials at iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind is appropriate, and the displayed rejected-trial bound is consistent with geometric reduction and the safe threshold alpha at most 1/L. Because the leaf is specifically a boundary claim and no citation is provided for the exact counting convention and formula, a source with a theorem, proposition, or explicit backtracking-count locator is required.

children.title: Accelerated Proximal Gradient
children.top_down_role: FISTA-type acceleration and its stabilization, restart, and inexactness variants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Backtracking line search for accelerated proximal gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric backtracking that accepts a proximal-gradient trial point when it satisfies the stated local-model inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(y^k\), \(\lambda^{k-1}\), and \(\beta\in(0,1)\), initialize \(\lambda\leftarrow\lambda^{k-1}\). Repeat:
\[
z\leftarrow\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda g}\!\left(y^k-\lambda\nabla f(y^k)\right).
\]
If \(f(z)\leq\widehat f_\lambda(z,y^k)\), return \(\lambda^k\leftarrow\lambda\) and \(x^{k+1}\leftarrow z\). Otherwise set \(\lambda\leftarrow\beta\lambda\) and repeat.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start from the preceding step size and compute a proximal-gradient trial point at the extrapolated point. Accept the trial when its smooth-function value satisfies the stated local-model bound; otherwise multiply the step size by beta and repeat.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At the first accepted trial, \(\lambda^k=\lambda\), \(x^{k+1}=z\), and \(f(z)\leq\widehat f_\lambda(z,y^k)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Accelerated proximal-gradient iteration and objective-value rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extrapolated proximal-gradient iteration with the stated momentum schedule and fixed-step objective convergence guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Set \(\omega^0=0\), and for \(k\geq 0\) define
\[
y^{k+1}=x^k+\omega^k(x^k-x^{k-1}),\qquad
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda^k g}\!\left(y^{k+1}-\lambda^k\nabla f(y^{k+1})\right).
\]
With \(\omega^k=k/(k+3)\), if \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous with constant \(L\) and \(\lambda^k=\lambda\in(0,1/L]\), the method converges in objective value at rate \(O(k^{-2})\). If \(L\) is unknown, step sizes may instead be selected by line search.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting with zero initial momentum, extrapolate from the two preceding iterates and take a proximal-gradient step at the extrapolated point. With momentum k/(k+3), an L-Lipschitz gradient, and a fixed step size in (0,1/L], objective values converge at rate O(1/k^2). When L is unknown, a line search may select the step sizes.
assumptions_latex: \(\nabla f\) is Lipschitz continuous with constant \(L\)

children.title: FISTA Family

knowledge_statements.title: FISTA Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical constant-stepsize FISTA for convex composite minimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\), where \(f\) is convex with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. Initialize \(x_0\), set \(y_1=x_0\) and \(t_1=1\). For \(k\ge1\), compute \[x_k=\operatorname{prox}_{g/L}\!\left(y_k-L^{-1}\nabla f(y_k)\right),\qquad t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2},\] and \[y_{k+1}=x_k+\frac{t_k-1}{t_{k+1}}(x_k-x_{k-1}).\] After \(N\) iterations output \(x_N\), or stop earlier when a prescribed proximal-gradient residual tolerance is met.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FISTA alternates a proximal-gradient step with Nesterov extrapolation governed by the standard quadratic momentum recurrence.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is convex and differentiable with \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient.
\(g\) is proper, closed, and convex with a computable proximal map.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every minimizer \(x^\star\), the exact method satisfies \(F(x_N)-F(x^\star)=O(L\|x_0-x^\star\|^2/N^2)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotone FISTA (MFISTA) iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded algorithm statement. The extracted recurrence invokes t_{-1} when k=0, although only t_0 is initialized; an additional surrounding convention is therefore required to make the first extrapolation step well-defined.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let F=f+g, let f and g satisfy properties (A) and (B) of Assumption 10.31, and let x^0\in\mathbb E. Initialize y^0=x^0 and t_0=1. For k=0,1,2,\ldots, choose L_k>0, set z^k=\operatorname{prox}_{g/L_k}\!\left(y^k-L_k^{-1}\nabla f(y^k)\right), choose x^{k+1}\in\mathbb E such that F(x^{k+1})\leq\min\{F(z^k),F(x^k)\}, set t_{k+1}=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4t_k^2}}{2}, and set y^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\frac{t_k}{t_{k+1}}(z^k-x^{k+1})+\frac{t_{k-1}}{t_{k+1}}(x^{k+1}-x^k).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: MFISTA takes a proximal-gradient step from the extrapolated point, accepts an iterate whose objective is no greater than either that step or the preceding iterate, updates the acceleration parameter, and forms the next extrapolated point. The extracted first extrapolation requires an unstated value or convention for t minus one.
assumptions_latex: f\text{ and }g\text{ satisfy properties (A) and (B) of Assumption 10.31}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x^{k+1})\leq\min\{F(z^k),F(x^k)\}\quad\text{and the stated proximal and extrapolation recurrences hold whenever all indexed quantities are defined.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: V-FISTA for strongly convex composite minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded fixed-momentum accelerated proximal-gradient iteration under the referenced composite assumptions; the surrounding restarted-FISTA subsection does not itself make this recurrence a restart scheme.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given \(x^0\in\mathbb E\), set \(y^0=x^0\), \(t_0=1\), and \(\kappa=L_f/\sigma\). For each \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), compute
\[
x^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\frac{1}{L_f}g}\!\left(y^k-\frac{1}{L_f}\nabla f(y^k)\right),
\qquad
y^{k+1}=x^{k+1}+\frac{\sqrt{\kappa}-1}{\sqrt{\kappa}+1}(x^{k+1}-x^k).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from y^0=x^0, V-FISTA applies a proximal-gradient step at y^k and then extrapolates using the fixed coefficient (sqrt(kappa)-1)/(sqrt(kappa)+1), where kappa=L_f/sigma.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) and \(g\) satisfy properties (A) and (B) in Assumption 10.31.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x^k,y^k\}_{k\geq 0}\) is generated by the stated V-FISTA recurrence.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: FISTA iteration and accelerated objective rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The stated FISTA recurrence for unconstrained convex composite minimization and its \(O(t^{-2})\) objective bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), where \(f\) is convex, differentiable, and \(\beta\)-smooth, \(g\) is convex, and the displayed proximal subproblem is attained and computationally accessible. Set \(\lambda_0=0\),
\[
\lambda_t=\frac{1+\sqrt{1+4\lambda_{t-1}^2}}{2},\qquad \gamma_t=\frac{1-\lambda_t}{\lambda_{t+1}},
\]
choose \(x_1=y_1\) arbitrarily, and iterate
\[
y_{t+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\left\{g(x)+\frac{\beta}{2}\left\|x-\left(x_t-\frac1\beta\nabla f(x_t)\right)\right\|_2^2\right\},
\]
\[
x_{t+1}=(1-\gamma_t)y_{t+1}+\gamma_t y_t.
\]
If \(x^*\in\operatorname*{argmin}F\), then for \(t\ge1\),
\[
F(y_t)-F(x^*)\le \frac{2\beta\|x_1-x^*\|_2^2}{t^2}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: FISTA combines proximal-gradient steps with the stated acceleration recurrence. Under the convex beta-smooth composite assumptions, its objective gap at y_t is at most 2 beta times the squared initial distance to a minimizer divided by t squared.
assumptions_latex: g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\text{ is convex and the proximal subproblem is attained and computationally accessible}

knowledge_statements.title: Monotone Accelerated Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated proximal-gradient proposals protected by an objective-decrease safeguard.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=f+g\) and let an accelerated proximal-gradient rule produce a proposal \(z_k\) from the current extrapolated point. Define \[x_k\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{u\in\{x_{k-1},z_k\}}F(u).\] If \(z_k\) is rejected, reset the inertial state by setting the next extrapolated point to \(x_k
e z_k\) and the momentum parameter to its initial value; otherwise update the momentum by the chosen accelerated recurrence. Starting from \(x_0\), repeat until a proximal-gradient residual is below tolerance and return the last accepted iterate. The safeguard guarantees \(F(x_k)\le F(x_{k-1})\), independently of whether the unsafeguarded proposals are monotone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compare each accelerated proposal with the previous accepted point, keep the lower-objective candidate, and reset momentum after rejection.
assumptions_latex: Each proposal \(z_k\) is a well-defined proximal-gradient point.
Both objective values used by the safeguard are finite and evaluable.
The inertial state can be reset after rejection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The accepted sequence is objective-monotone: \(F(x_k)\le F(x_{k-1})\) for every \(k\ge1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the monotone-variant leaf, and the two-candidate safeguard directly implies objective monotonicity. However, no source identifies this safeguard-plus-reset construction as the intended monotone accelerated family, and the generic proposal rule does not fix a recognized accelerated variant.

knowledge_statements.title: Restarted Accelerated Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scheduled or event-triggered restart of accelerated proximal gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Run an accelerated proximal-gradient method with accepted iterate \(x_k\), extrapolated point \(y_k\), and momentum state \(t_k\). At a prescribed restart time, or when a specified observable trigger \(R_k\) is true, erase accumulated inertia by setting \[y_{k+1}=x_k,\qquad t_{k+1}=1,\] and continue from \(x_k\). Otherwise apply the ordinary accelerated recurrence. A scheduled policy fixes restart indices in advance; an adaptive policy defines \(R_k\) from available quantities, such as objective increase or misalignment between the step and extrapolation. Output the final accepted iterate when the chosen residual or iteration budget is reached.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restart acceleration on a fixed schedule or observable trigger by resetting the extrapolated point and momentum while retaining the current iterate.
assumptions_latex: The underlying accelerated proximal-gradient update is well-defined.
Every adaptive trigger depends only on information available by iteration \(k\).
Restart preserves the current accepted iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At each restart, the next accelerated phase begins from \(x_k\) with zero inherited momentum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind is appropriate and the record correctly avoids a rate claim without trigger-specific hypotheses. A source is still required to support the scheduled and adaptive restart family, its state-reset convention, and the stated examples of observable triggers.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear cycle contraction and complexity of restarted FISTA
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extraction-grounded guarantee. The reviewed statement uses m for the restart-cycle index and q for the total number of inner FISTA iterations to disambiguate the source's reuse of k. Positivity of logarithm arguments is an implicit domain requirement for the displayed complexity formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose Assumption 10.31 holds and f is \sigma-strongly convex with \sigma>0. Let \kappa=L_f/\sigma, N=\lceil\sqrt{8\kappa-1}\rceil, and let restarted FISTA generate \{z^m\}_{m\geq0}. If x^* is the unique optimizer and R\geq\lVert z^{-1}-x^*\rVert, then, for every m\geq0, F(z^m)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\frac{L_fR^2}{2}(\frac12)^m. Moreover, if \epsilon>0, L_fR^2>0, and the total number q of inner FISTA iterations satisfies q\geq\sqrt{8\kappa}\left(\frac{\log(1/\epsilon)}{\log2}+\frac{\log(L_fR^2)}{\log2}\right), then F\!\left(z^{\lfloor q/N\rfloor}\right)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\epsilon.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With restart period equal to the ceiling of the square root of eight kappa minus one, restarted FISTA halves the objective gap after each completed cycle and reaches epsilon accuracy after the stated order square root of kappa times logarithmic number of inner FISTA iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Inexact Accelerated Variants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated proximal gradient with explicitly budgeted proximal-subproblem error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an extrapolated point \(y_k\) and stepsize \(\alpha_k>0\), define \[Q_k(x)=g(x)+\langle\nabla f(y_k),x-y_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\|x-y_k\|^2.\] Choose \(x_k\) satisfying \[Q_k(x_k)\le\inf_x Q_k(x)+\varepsilon_k,\] then update the extrapolated point using the selected accelerated momentum recurrence. Stop after the prescribed budget or when an inexact proximal-gradient residual is below tolerance. For the standard FISTA momentum scale, a sufficient error-control regime for retaining the usual accelerated objective order is that the weighted proximal errors decay so that \(\sum_{k=1}^{\infty}k\sqrt{\varepsilon_k}<\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve each proximal model only approximately, record its objective error, and make weighted square-root errors summable to preserve accelerated behavior.
assumptions_latex: Each proximal subproblem admits an \(\varepsilon_k\)-optimal point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under the displayed weighted summability condition, the proximal errors do not change the standard \(O(1/k^2)\) objective order.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the leaf, but the accelerated-rate conclusion depends materially on the precise proximal-error definition and momentum analysis. No citation supports the claimed sufficient condition sum k sqrt(epsilon_k) finite for the displayed objective-suboptimality model.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Euclidean Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bregman proximal gradient under relative smoothness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(h\) be differentiable and strictly convex on \(\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h)\), with Bregman divergence \[D_h(x,y)=h(x)-h(y)-\langle
abla h(y),x-yangle.\] Given \(x_k\) and \(\alpha_k>0\), compute \[x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{g(x)+\langle
abla f(x_k),x-x_kangle+\alpha_k^{-1}D_h(x,x_k)ight\}.\] Choose \(\alpha_k\le L^{-1}\) when \(f(x)\le f(y)+\langle
abla f(y),x-yangle+L D_h(x,y)\), or enforce this inequality by backtracking. Return the final iterate or stop when the associated Bregman-gradient residual meets tolerance.

\(f\) is convex, differentiable, and \(L\)-smooth relative to \(h\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Objective monotonicity and O(1/k) rate of non-Euclidean proximal gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence guarantee for constant-curvature and backtracking versions of the non-Euclidean proximal-gradient method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumptions 10.77 and 10.78 hold, and let \(\{x^k\}_{k\ge0}\) be generated by non-Euclidean proximal gradient using either \(L_k\equiv L_f\) or backtracking B5 with parameters \(s>0\) and \(\eta>1\). Then \(\{F(x^k)\}_{k\ge0}\) is nonincreasing and, for every \(k\ge1\) and every \(x^*\in X^*\),
\[
F(x^k)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\le \frac{\alpha L_f B_\omega(x^*,x^0)}{k},
\qquad
\alpha=\begin{cases}1,&L_k\equiv L_f,\\ \max\{\eta,s/L_f\},&\text{backtracking B5}.
\end{cases}
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 10.77 and 10.78, both the constant-inverse-stepsize and B5-backtracking non-Euclidean proximal-gradient methods produce nonincreasing objective values. For every solution and k at least one, the objective error is bounded by alpha times L_f times the initial Bregman distance divided by k, with the stated rule-dependent alpha.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\ge0}\text{ is generated by the non-Euclidean proximal-gradient method for the stated problem}.
\text{Either }L_k\equiv L_f\text{ for all }k\ge0\text{, or backtracking B5 with }s>0\text{ and }\eta>1\text{ is used}.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{F(x^k)\}_{k\ge0}\text{ is nonincreasing},\qquad F(x^k)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\le\frac{\alpha L_fB_\omega(x^*,x^0)}{k},\quad \alpha=1\text{ in the constant case and }\alpha=\max\{\eta,s/L_f\}\text{ under backtracking B5}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Non-Euclidean proximal-gradient iteration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Initialized iterative form of proximal gradient in the geometry generated by a convex kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Under Assumptions 10.77 and 10.78, choose \(x^0\in\operatorname{dom}(g)\cap\operatorname{dom}(\partial\omega)\). For every \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), choose \(L_k>0\) and compute
\[
x^{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb E}\left\{\left\langle \frac{1}{L_k}\nabla f(x^k)-\nabla\omega(x^k),x\right\rangle+\frac{1}{L_k}g(x)+\omega(x)\right\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Start where both g and the kernel subgradient are defined. At each iteration choose a positive scale and minimize the sum of the kernel, a scaled g term, and the linear term formed from the gradients of f and the kernel.

knowledge_statements.title: Variable-Metric Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward–backward iteration in a changing positive-definite metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F=f+g\) on \(\mathbb{R}^n\), and let \(H_k\) be symmetric positive definite. Given \(x_k\) and \(\alpha_k>0\), compute \[x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\left\{g(x)+\langle\nabla f(x_k),x-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\|x-x_k\|_{H_k}^2\right\}.\] Equivalently, \(x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}^{H_k}_{\alpha_k g}(x_k-\alpha_k H_k^{-1}\nabla f(x_k))\). A standard stable family requires uniform bounds \(mI\preceq H_k\preceq MI\) with \(0<m\le M<\infty\), together with stepsizes satisfying the applicable metric descent condition. Output the last iterate when a metric proximal-gradient residual is sufficiently small.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Precondition the forward gradient and proximal quadratic by a uniformly positive-definite metric that may change between iterations.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex.
Each \(\alpha_k\) satisfies a valid metric descent condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The update is the forward–backward step in the norm \(\|v\|_{H_k}^2=\langle v,H_kv\rangle\).

notation.meaning: proximal map in the H_k metric

knowledge_statements.title: Block Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-block proximal-gradient updates for separable composite regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=(x_1,\ldots,x_m)\) and \(F(x)=f(x)+\sum_{i=1}^m g_i(x_i)\). At iteration \(k\), select a block \(i_k\) cyclically or randomly and set \[x_{i_k}^{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k g_{i_k}}\!\left(x_{i_k}^k-\alpha_k\nabla_{i_k}f(x^k)\right),\qquad x_j^{k+1}=x_j^k\ \text{for }j\ne i_k.\] Choose \(\alpha_k\) using a valid block-Lipschitz bound or block backtracking rule. In the randomized form, the sampling distribution must assign positive probability to every block. Stop when a block or full proximal-gradient residual meets tolerance, and return \(x^k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Update one selected coordinate block by its proximal-gradient map while holding all other blocks fixed; selection may be cyclic or randomized.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is differentiable with blockwise Lipschitz partial gradients.
Each \(g_i\) is proper, closed, and convex with a computable proximal map.
Every block is selected repeatedly, deterministically or with positive probability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each iteration changes only block \(i_k\) according to its block proximal-gradient operator.

notation.meaning: partial gradient with respect to block i

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and single-block update match the leaf, and the deterministic and randomized cases are not assigned a shared convergence theorem. A citation is nevertheless required for the stated block-Lipschitz setup, cyclic/randomized family, and positive-probability sampling condition.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex CBPG objective-gap convergence bound
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit objective-gap and accuracy bounds for cyclic block proximal gradient under the source's stated assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumptions 11.1 and 11.15 hold, and let \(\{\mathbf{x}^k\}_{k\geq 0}\) be generated by CBPG for the stated problem. Set \(L_{\min}=\min_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i\), \(L_{\max}=\max_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i\), and \(R=R_{F(\mathbf{x}^0)}\). Then, for every \(k\geq 2\),
\[
F(\mathbf{x}^k)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq \max\left\{2^{-(k-1)/2}\bigl(F(\mathbf{x}^0)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\bigr),\frac{8p(L_f+L_{\max})^2R^2}{L_{\min}(k-1)}\right\}.
\]
Moreover, for every \(\varepsilon>0\), if \(n\geq 2\) and
\[
n\geq \max\left\{\frac{2}{\log 2}\left(\log\bigl(F(\mathbf{x}^0)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\bigr)+\log(1/\varepsilon)\right),\frac{8p(L_f+L_{\max})^2R^2}{L_{\min}\varepsilon}\right\}+1,
\]
then \(F(\mathbf{x}^n)-F_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumptions 11.1 and 11.15, the CBPG objective gap is bounded by the maximum of a geometrically decaying initial-gap term and an explicit reciprocal-iteration term. The stated iteration threshold guarantees objective accuracy epsilon.
assumptions_latex: \{\mathbf{x}^k\}_{k\geq 0}\text{ is generated by CBPG for the stated problem.}
L_{\min}=\min_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i,\quad L_{\max}=\max_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i,\quad R=R_{F(\mathbf{x}^0)}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Block-separable composite optimization model and notation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the product-space model and block-embedding notation used by block proximal-gradient methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(p\ge 1\), let \(\mathbb E_i\) be Euclidean spaces, and set \(\mathbb E=\prod_{i=1}^p\mathbb E_i\) with \(\|(u_1,\ldots,u_p)\|_{\mathbb E}= igl(\sum_{i=1}^p\|u_i\|_{\mathbb E_i}^2 igr)^{1/2}\). The block-separable composite model is \[\min_{x_i\in\mathbb E_i}\left\{F(x_1,\ldots,x_p)=f(x_1,\ldots,x_p)+\sum_{i=1}^p g_i(x_i)ight\}.\] Defining \(g(x)=\sum_{i=1}^p g_i(x_i)\), this is \(\min_{x\in\mathbb E}\{F(x)=f(x)+g(x)\}\). For each \(i\), define \(\mathcal U_i:\mathbb E_i	o\mathbb E\) by \(\mathcal U_i(d)=(0,\ldots,0,d,0,\ldots,0)\), with \(d\) in block \(i\). The partial gradient is denoted \(
abla_i f\), and whenever \(f\) is differentiable, \(
abla f(x)=(
abla_1f(x),\ldots,
abla_pf(x))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: On a finite product of Euclidean block spaces equipped with the product norm, the objective is the sum of a coupled function f and block-separable terms g_i. Their sum defines g, each block direction is inserted into the product space by the embedding U_i, and, whenever f is differentiable, its gradient is the tuple of its block partial gradients.
assumptions_latex: \mathbb E_i\text{ is a Euclidean space for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}

abla_pf(x))	ext{ whenever }f	ext{ is differentiable}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Nonconvex Convergence and Stationarity Complexity of CBPG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual convergence, a best-iterate residual bound, and stationarity of all accumulation points.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumption 11.1 holds, and let $\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}$ be generated by CBPG. Let
\[
L_{\min}=\min_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i,\qquad L_{\max}=\max_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i,
\]
and let
\[
C=\frac{L_{\min}}{2\left(L_f+2L_{\max}+\sqrt{L_{\min}L_{\max}}\right)^2}.
\]
Then
\[
G_{L_{\min}}(x^k)\to0\quad\text{as }k\to\infty,
\]
for every $k\geq0$,
\[
\min_{0\leq n\leq k}\|G_{L_{\min}}(x^n)\|\leq
\frac{\sqrt{p\bigl(F(x^0)-F_{\operatorname{opt}}\bigr)}}{\sqrt{C(k+1)}},
\]
and every limit point of $\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}$ is a stationary point of the stated problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 11.1, the CBPG proximal-gradient mapping converges to zero. The smallest residual among the first k+1 iterates satisfies the displayed inverse-square-root bound, and every limit point of the iterate sequence is stationary.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by CBPG for the stated problem}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G_{L_{\min}}(x^k)\to0;\quad \forall k\geq0:\ \min_{0\leq n\leq k}\|G_{L_{\min}}(x^n)\|\leq\frac{\sqrt{p(F(x^0)-F_{\operatorname{opt}})}}{\sqrt{C(k+1)}};\quad \text{every limit point of }\{x^k\}\text{ is stationary}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic Block Proximal Gradient Method
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One complete cyclic sweep of blockwise proximal-gradient updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose $x^0=(x_1^0,\ldots,x_p^0)\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f)$. For each $k=0,1,2,\ldots$, set $x^{k,0}=x^k$ and, successively for $i=1,\ldots,p$, compute
\[
x^{k,i}=x^{k,i-1}+U_i\bigl(T_{L_i}(x^{k,i-1})-x_i^{k,i-1}\bigr).
\]
After the sweep, set $x^{k+1}=x^{k,p}$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize in the interior of the domain of f. At each iteration, visit blocks 1 through p in order, perform the stated block proximal-gradient update using the most recently updated vector, and use the completed sweep as the next iterate.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Cyclic dual block proximal-gradient convergence rate
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual objective and primal-iterate bounds after complete cyclic sweeps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with \(\sigma>0\); every \(g_i:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex; \[\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^{p}\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g_i)\ne\varnothing;\] and for every \(\alpha>0\) there is \(R_\alpha>0\) satisfying the stated bounded dual upper-level-set distance condition. Let \(\{\mathbf x^k\}\) and \(\{\mathbf y^k\}\) be generated by DBPG with cyclic block selection for \(\min_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb E}\{f(\mathbf x)+\sum_{i=1}^{p}g_i(\mathbf x)\}\). Set \(R=R_{q(\mathbf y^0)}\). For every \(k\ge2\), \[q_{\mathrm{opt}}-q(\mathbf y^{pk})\le\max\left\{2^{-(k-1)/2}\bigl(q_{\mathrm{opt}}-q(\mathbf y^0)\bigr),\frac{8p(p+1)^2R^2}{\sigma(k-1)}\right\},\] and \[\|\mathbf x^{pk}-\mathbf x^*\|^2\le\frac{2}{\sigma}\max\left\{2^{-(k-1)/2}\bigl(q_{\mathrm{opt}}-q(\mathbf y^0)\bigr),\frac{8p(p+1)^2R^2}{\sigma(k-1)}\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strong convexity, closed convex component functions, the relative-interior qualification, and the bounded dual upper-level-set condition, cyclic dual block proximal gradient has an O(1/k) dual objective-gap bound after k complete sweeps. The squared distance of the associated primal iterate to the primal solution obeys the same bound multiplied by 2/sigma.

g_i:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}
\forall\alpha>0\ \exists R_\alpha>0:\ \max\{\|\mathbf y-\mathbf y^*\|:\mathbf y,\mathbf y^*\in\mathbb E^p,\ q(\mathbf y)\ge\alpha,\ \mathbf y^*\in\Lambda^*\}\le R_\alpha
\{\mathbf x^k\},\{\mathbf y^k\}\text{ are generated by DBPG with cyclic index selection}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CBPG Sufficient Decrease in the Full Proximal-Gradient Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A full-sweep decrease certificate expressed through the global proximal-gradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumption 11.1 holds, and let $\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}$ be generated by CBPG. Define
\[
L_{\min}=\min_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i,\qquad L_{\max}=\max_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i,
\]
and
\[
C=\frac{L_{\min}}{2\left(L_f+2L_{\max}+\sqrt{L_{\min}L_{\max}}\right)^2}.
\]
Then, for every $k\geq0$,
\[
F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\geq\frac{C}{p}\left\|G_{L_{\min}}(x^k)\right\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 11.1, every complete CBPG sweep decreases the objective by at least C divided by the number of blocks times the squared norm of the full proximal-gradient mapping at the current iterate, with C given by the displayed smoothness and block constants.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by CBPG for the stated problem}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: CBPG Per-Block and Full-Sweep Sufficient Decrease
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Per-block and full-sweep decrease estimates under Assumption 11.1.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose Assumption 11.1 holds, and let $\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}$ be generated by CBPG with the auxiliary iterates $x^{k,j}$. For every $k\geq0$ and $j\in\{0,\ldots,p-1\}$,
\[
F(x^{k,j})-F(x^{k,j+1})\geq \frac{1}{2L_{j+1}}\left\|G_{L_{j+1}}^{j+1}(x^{k,j})\right\|^2,
\]
or equivalently,
\[
F(x^{k,j})-F(x^{k,j+1})\geq \frac{L_{j+1}}{2}\left\|x^{k,j}-x^{k,j+1}\right\|^2.
\]
Moreover, for every $k\geq0$,
\[
F(x^k)-F(x^{k+1})\geq\frac{L_{\min}}{2}\|x^k-x^{k+1}\|^2,
\qquad L_{\min}=\min_{1\leq i\leq p}L_i.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under Assumption 11.1, each CBPG block update satisfies the stated decrease bound in either block-gradient-mapping or step-norm form. A complete cyclic sweep decreases the objective by at least half the smallest block constant times the squared full-sweep displacement.
assumptions_latex: \{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\text{ is generated by CBPG for the stated problem}

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal gradient applied to a Fenchel dual composite objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider \(\min_x\{p(x)+q(Ax)\}\), where \(p\) is strongly convex. Its Fenchel dual can be written as minimizing \[D(u)=p^*(-A^*u)+q^*(u).\] Since \(p^*\) is differentiable, define \(d(u)=p^*(-A^*u)\), so that \(
abla d(u)=-A
abla p^*(-A^*u)\). Given \(u_k\) and an admissible stepsize \(\alpha_k\), compute \[u_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k q^*}\!\left(u_k-\alpha_k
abla d(u_k)ight).\] Basic, accelerated, or block proximal-gradient recurrences may be applied to this dual decomposition. A corresponding primal candidate is \(x_{k+1}=
abla p^*(-A^*u_{k+1})\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Express a structured Fenchel dual as smooth plus proximable terms, apply proximal gradient in dual space, and recover a primal candidate from the conjugate gradient.
assumptions_latex: \(p\) is proper, closed, and strongly convex.
\(q\) is proper, closed, and convex, and \(\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha q^*}\) is computable.
A standard Fenchel qualification condition ensures strong duality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed update is proximal gradient for \(D=d+q^*\), with primal recovery \(x=\nabla p^*(-A^*u)\).

notation.meaning: adjoint of the linear operator A

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits the dual proximal-gradient leaf, and the conjugate decomposition, gradient sign, and primal recovery formula are internally consistent. No source supports this selected Fenchel-dual form, the required qualification, or the extension to basic, accelerated, and block recurrences.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Structured dual of a shared-variable sum
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation underlying dual block proximal-gradient updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the primal problem \(\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb E}\{f(\mathbf{x})+\sum_{i=1}^{p}g_i(\mathbf{x})\}\), the associated structured dual is \[q_{\mathrm{opt}}=\max_{\mathbf y=(\mathbf y_1,\ldots,\mathbf y_p)\in\mathbb E^p}\left\{-f^*\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{p}\mathbf y_i\right)-\sum_{i=1}^{p}g_i^*(-\mathbf y_i)\right\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual associated with minimizing f plus several functions evaluated at one shared primal variable maximizes the negative conjugate of f at the sum of the dual blocks minus the conjugates of the component functions at the negated blocks.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual block proximal-gradient method in primal representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-oracle implementation of cyclic or uniformly randomized dual block proximal gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathbf y^0=(\mathbf y_1^0,\ldots,\mathbf y_p^0)\in\mathbb E^p\). For each \(k\ge0\), choose \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\), compute \[\mathbf x^k=\operatorname*{argmax}_{\mathbf x\in\mathbb E}\left\{\left\langle\mathbf x,\sum_{j=1}^{p}\mathbf y_j^k\right\rangle-f(\mathbf x)\right\},\] and update \[\mathbf y_j^{k+1}=\begin{cases}\mathbf y_{i_k}^k-\sigma\mathbf x^k+\sigma\operatorname{prox}_{g_{i_k}/\sigma}\!\left(\mathbf x^k-\mathbf y_{i_k}^k/\sigma\right),&j=i_k,\\ \mathbf y_j^k,&j\ne i_k.\end{cases}\] The selection may be cyclic, \(i_k=(k\bmod p)+1\), or uniform random selection from \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, form a primal point from the current sum of dual blocks, update one selected dual block using the proximal map of its primal component function, and retain the other blocks. The indices may follow a cyclic order or be selected uniformly at random.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and }\sigma\text{-strongly convex},\quad\sigma>0
g_i:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex for }i=1,\ldots,p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf y_j^{k+1}=\begin{cases}\mathbf y_{i_k}^k-\sigma\mathbf x^k+\sigma\operatorname{prox}_{g_{i_k}/\sigma}(\mathbf x^k-\mathbf y_{i_k}^k/\sigma),&j=i_k,\\\mathbf y_j^k,&j\ne i_k,\end{cases}\quad i_k=(k\bmod p)+1\text{ or }i_k\sim\operatorname{Unif}\{1,\ldots,p\}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Evaluation Formula for a Dual Proximal-Gradient Step
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent primal-space evaluation of one proximal-gradient step for a conjugate-composite dual objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[
F(y)=f^*(A^Ty+b),\qquad G(y)=g^*(-y),
\]
where \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with \(\sigma>0\), \(g:\mathbb V\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex, \(A:\mathbb E\to\mathbb V\) is linear, and \(b\in\mathbb E\). For \(y,v\in\mathbb V\) and \(L>0\), let
\[
\widetilde x=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x\in\mathbb E}\{\langle x,A^Tv+b\rangle-f(x)\}.
\]
Then
\[
y=\operatorname{prox}_{\frac1L G}\!\left(v-\frac1L\nabla F(v)\right)
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
y=v-\frac1L A\widetilde x+\frac1L\operatorname{prox}_{Lg}(A\widetilde x-Lv).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For the stated conjugate-composite dual objective, a dual proximal-gradient update is equivalent to computing the associated primal maximizer and applying the proximal map of g to the resulting affine residual. The equivalence holds for every pair of dual vectors and every positive L.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and }\sigma\text{-strongly convex},\quad \sigma>0
g:\mathbb V\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Expected O(1/k) convergence of randomized dual block proximal gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected dual-objective and primal-recovery bounds for DBPG with randomized index selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty] be proper, closed, and \sigma-strongly convex with \sigma>0; let each g_i:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty] be proper, closed, and convex; and suppose \operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\bigcap_{i=1}^p\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g_i)\neq\varnothing. Let \mathbf{y}^* be a dual optimal solution, let \mathbf{x}^* be the associated primal optimal solution, and let (\mathbf{x}^k,\mathbf{y}^k) be generated by DBPG with randomized index selection. Then, for every k\geq0, q_{\mathrm{opt}}-\mathbb{E}_{\xi_k}[q(\mathbf{y}^{k+1})]\leq\frac{p}{p+k+1}\left(\frac{\|\mathbf{y}^0-\mathbf{y}^*\|^2}{2\sigma}+q_{\mathrm{opt}}-q(\mathbf{y}^0)\right), and \mathbb{E}_{\xi_k}\|\mathbf{x}^{k+1}-\mathbf{x}^*\|^2\leq\frac{2p}{\sigma(p+k+1)}\left(\frac{\|\mathbf{y}^0-\mathbf{y}^*\|^2}{2\sigma}+q_{\mathrm{opt}}-q(\mathbf{y}^0)\right).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For randomized DBPG under strong convexity, closed convexity, and the relative-interior qualification, the expected dual objective gap and expected squared primal-recovery error both decay at order 1/k with the displayed constants.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and }\sigma\text{-strongly convex, with }\sigma>0
g_i:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex for every }i\in\{1,\ldots,p\}
\mathbf{y}^*\text{ is a dual optimal solution and }\mathbf{x}^*\text{ is the associated primal optimal solution}
(\mathbf{x}^k,\mathbf{y}^k)\text{ are generated by DBPG with randomized index selection}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: FDPG Parameter for Diagonal Replication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specialization of the FDPG smoothness parameter to the p-fold diagonal replication operator when the primal term has strong-convexity modulus sigma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose \(f\) is \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with \(\sigma>0\), and let \(\mathcal{A}:\mathbb{E}\to\mathbb{E}^{p}\) be defined by
\[
\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{z})=(\mathbf{z},\ldots,\mathbf{z}).
\]
Using \(\|\mathcal{A}\|^{2}=p\), the FDPG parameter can be chosen as
\[
L=\frac{\|\mathcal{A}\|^{2}}{\sigma}=\frac{p}{\sigma}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If f has strong-convexity modulus sigma greater than zero, then for the p-fold diagonal replication operator the FDPG parameter can be chosen as L=p/sigma.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: O(1/k) Squared-Distance Rate for DPG Primal Iterates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Primal-sequence convergence for the basic dual proximal-gradient method under strong convexity and the stated relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with \(\sigma>0\); let \(g:\mathbb V\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex; and let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb E\to\mathbb V\) be linear. Assume that there exist \(\hat x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) and \(\hat z\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\) such that \(\mathcal A\hat x=\hat z\). Let \(\{x^k\}_{k\geq0}\) and \(\{y^k\}_{k\geq0}\) be the primal and dual sequences generated by DPG with \(L\geq\|\mathcal A\|^2/\sigma\). Then, for every optimal solution \(y^*\) of the dual problem and every \(k\geq1\),
\[
\|x^k-x^*\|^2\leq\frac{L\|y^0-y^*\|^2}{\sigma k}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated convexity, strong-convexity, linearity, and qualification assumptions, the squared distance from the DPG primal iterate to the primal optimum is bounded by a quantity proportional to 1/k. The bound holds for every dual optimum and every positive iteration index.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and }\sigma\text{-strongly convex},\quad \sigma>0
g:\mathbb V\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Primal Representation of Dual Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Implementation of DPG through a primal maximization followed by a proximal evaluation of g.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose \(y^0\in\mathbb V\) and \(L\geq\|\mathcal A\|^2/\sigma\). For each \(k=0,1,2,\ldots\), compute
\[
x^k=\operatorname*{argmax}_{x}\{\langle x,\mathcal A^Ty^k\rangle-f(x)\},
\]
and then set
\[
y^{k+1}=y^k-\frac1L\mathcal A x^k+\frac1L\operatorname{prox}_{Lg}(\mathcal A x^k-Ly^k).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Initialize a dual vector and choose L at least as large as the stated operator-norm bound. At each iteration, compute the primal maximizer associated with the current dual vector and then update the dual vector using its image under the linear map and the proximal map of g.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose p=2, f:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty] is proper, closed, and \sigma-strongly convex with \sigma>0, each g_i:\mathbb{E}\to(-\infty,+\infty] is proper, closed, and convex, and \operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g_1)\cap\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g_2)\neq\varnothing. knowledge_statements.statement_title: O(1/k) Dual Objective Rate of DPG
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual-objective convergence of the basic dual proximal-gradient method under strong convexity and the stated relative-interior qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and \(\sigma\)-strongly convex with \(\sigma>0\); let \(g:\mathbb V\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, closed, and convex; and let \(\mathcal A:\mathbb E\to\mathbb V\) be linear. Assume that there exist \(\hat x\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}f)\) and \(\hat z\in\operatorname{ri}(\operatorname{dom}g)\) such that \(\mathcal A\hat x=\hat z\). Define
\[
q(y)=-f^*(\mathcal A^Ty)-g^*(-y),\qquad q_{\mathrm{opt}}=\max_{y\in\mathbb V}q(y).
\]
If \(\{y^k\}_{k\geq0}\) is generated by DPG with \(L\geq\|\mathcal A\|^2/\sigma\), then for every dual optimal solution \(y^*\) and every \(k\geq1\),
\[
q_{\mathrm{opt}}-q(y^k)\leq\frac{L\|y^0-y^*\|^2}{2k}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the stated properness, closedness, convexity, strong-convexity, linearity, and relative-interior assumptions, basic dual proximal gradient has an O(1/k) dual-objective gap. The displayed bound holds for every dual optimum and every positive iteration index.

g:\mathbb V\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual block proximal-gradient update in dual variables
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-block proximal-gradient iteration for the structured dual objective under the standing DBPG convexity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(\mathbf y^0=(\mathbf y_1^0,\ldots,\mathbf y_p^0)\in\mathbb E^p\). For each \(k\ge0\), choose \(i_k\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and set \[\mathbf y_j^{k+1}=\begin{cases}\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma G_{i_k}}\!\left(\mathbf y_{i_k}^k-\sigma\nabla f^*\!\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^{p}\mathbf y_\ell^k\right)\right),&j=i_k,\\ \mathbf y_j^k,&j\ne i_k.\end{cases}\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Starting from p dual blocks, select one block at each iteration, apply a proximal-gradient step to that block using the gradient of the conjugate of f at the sum of all current blocks, and leave every other block unchanged.
assumptions_latex: f:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and }\sigma\text{-strongly convex},\quad\sigma>0
g_i:\mathbb E\to(-\infty,+\infty]\text{ is proper, closed, and convex for }i=1,\ldots,p
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbf y_j^{k+1}=\begin{cases}\operatorname{prox}_{\sigma G_{i_k}}\left(\mathbf y_{i_k}^k-\sigma\nabla f^*\left(\sum_{\ell=1}^{p}\mathbf y_\ell^k\right)\right),&j=i_k,\\\mathbf y_j^k,&j\ne i_k.\end{cases}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Diagonal Lifting of a Multi-Term Composite Objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-space representation that converts several functions of one variable into a separable function composed with a diagonal replication operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For
\[
\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{E}}\left\{f(\mathbf{x})+\sum_{i=1}^{p}g_i(\mathbf{x})\right\},
\]
set \(\mathbb{V}=\mathbb{E}^{p}\), define
\[
g(\mathbf{x}_1,\ldots,\mathbf{x}_p)=\sum_{i=1}^{p}g_i(\mathbf{x}_i),
\qquad
\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{z})=(\mathbf{z},\ldots,\mathbf{z}).
\]
Then the problem has the composite form
\[
\min_{\mathbf{x}\in\mathbb{E}}\{f(\mathbf{x})+g(\mathcal{A}(\mathbf{x}))\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introduce the product space E^p, the block-separable function g(x_1,...,x_p)=sum_i g_i(x_i), and the diagonal replication operator A(z)=(z,...,z). The original problem then equals the composite problem minimizing f(x)+g(A(x)).

children.title: Stochastic Proximal Gradient
children.top_down_role: Sample-gradient proximal methods for additive composite objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic Euclidean stochastic forward–backward iteration with an unbiased sampled gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=f(x)+g(x)\) on \(\mathbb{R}^d\), where \(f(x)=\mathbb{E}[f_\xi(x)]\) is differentiable and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}g\) and stepsizes \(\alpha_k>0\), sample \(\xi_k\), form \(v_k=\nabla f_{\xi_k}(x_k)\), and update
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k g}(x_k-\alpha_k v_k),\qquad \operatorname{prox}_{\alpha g}(z)=\arg\min_y\left\{g(y)+\frac{\|y-z\|^2}{2\alpha}\right\}.
\]
The standard unbiased-oracle condition is \(\mathbb{E}[v_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)\). After \(K\) iterations, output \(x_K\), a prescribed weighted average, or a randomly selected iterate, according to the convergence criterion being analyzed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sample a gradient estimate, take a forward step, and apply the proximal map of the nonsmooth term; return the terminal, averaged, or randomly selected iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[v_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)\) and the displayed conditional expectations exist.

notation.meaning: Information available before the sample at iteration k is drawn.
Euclidean proximal map of g with parameter alpha.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm is mathematically coherent and fits the stochastic proximal-gradient container, but no inspectable source supports the oracle assumptions and output variants.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stochastic proximal-gradient update for a finite-sum composite objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sample-gradient proximal update for a finite-sum objective with a proximable convex term. The extract provides no conditions sufficient for a convergence-rate statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \min_x\left\{\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N f^i(x)+h(x)\right\},\qquad i_n\ \text{sampled from }\{1,\ldots,N\},\qquad x_{n+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{a h}\!\left(x_n-a\nabla f^{i_n}(x_n)\right).

When the proximal term is an l1 norm, this map is soft thresholding.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_{n+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{a h}\!\left(x_n-a\nabla f^{i_n}(x_n)\right);\qquad \operatorname{prox}_{a\|\cdot\|_1}\text{ is a soft-thresholding map}

children.title: Variance-Reduced Proximal Gradient
children.top_down_role: Finite-sum proximal-gradient families using variance reduction.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduced Proximal Gradient
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proximal SVRG as a representative finite-sum variance-reduced forward–backward method.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)+g(x)\), where each \(f_i\) is differentiable and \(g\) is proper, closed, and convex. At epoch \(s\), choose a snapshot \(\widetilde x_s\), compute \(\widetilde\mu_s=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\nabla f_i(\widetilde x_s)\), and initialize \(x_{s,0}=\widetilde x_s\). For \(t=0,\ldots,m-1\), sample \(i_{s,t}\) uniformly and set
\[
v_{s,t}=\nabla f_{i_{s,t}}(x_{s,t})-\nabla f_{i_{s,t}}(\widetilde x_s)+\widetilde\mu_s,
\qquad x_{s,t+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha g}(x_{s,t}-\alpha v_{s,t}).
\]
Choose the next snapshot by a specified last-iterate or averaging rule and return the final snapshot.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A snapshot full gradient corrects sampled component gradients, producing an unbiased lower-variance estimator used in a proximal-gradient update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[v_{s,t}\mid x_{s,t},\widetilde x_s]=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\nabla f_i(x_{s,t})\), followed by the displayed proximal update.

notation.meaning: Number of inner updates per epoch.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed Prox-SVRG update fits the container, but the precise snapshot/output variant needs a source. The stated assumptions establish unbiasedness but do not alone establish that the estimator always has lower variance than an uncorrected sampled gradient.

children.title: Iterate-Averaging Policies
children.top_down_role: Output aggregation policies for stochastic forward–backward iterates.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterate-Averaging Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted output policies for stochastic proximal-gradient iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Given iterates \(x_0,\ldots,x_K\) in a convex set and deterministic or history-measurable weights \(w_k\ge 0\) satisfying \(W_K=\sum_{k=0}^K w_k>0\), the weighted iterate-average policy returns
\[
\bar x_K=\frac{1}{W_K}\sum_{k=0}^K w_kx_k.
\]
Uniform averaging uses \(w_k=1\); suffix averaging sets \(w_k=0\) before a prescribed burn-in index; stepsize weighting uses \(w_k=\alpha_k\). If averaging is required to preserve feasibility or convex-domain membership, all averaged iterates must lie in the same convex feasible set. The policy is part of the output rule and does not alter the underlying proximal updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Return a normalized weighted average of selected iterates, using uniform, suffix, or stepsize weights; convex feasibility is preserved when all iterates share a convex feasible set.
assumptions_latex: The averaged iterates belong to a common real vector space.
The feasible set is convex when feasibility preservation is asserted.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative weight assigned to iterate k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition and content kind fit iterate-averaging policies, but no source is supplied for the catalogued uniform, suffix, and stepsize-weighted policies.

children.title: Sampling Policies
children.top_down_role: Selection mechanisms for stochastic component access.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased component sampling with optional importance correction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\), let index \(i_k\) be drawn conditionally on \(\mathcal F_k\) with probabilities \(p_{k,i}>0\) satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^n p_{k,i}=1\). The importance-corrected single-sample estimator is
\[
v_k=\frac{\nabla f_{i_k}(x_k)}{n p_{k,i_k}}.
\]
A sampling policy is conditionally unbiased when
\[
\mathbb{E}[v_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\sum_{i=1}^n p_{k,i}\frac{\nabla f_i(x_k)}{n p_{k,i}}=\nabla f(x_k).
\]
Uniform sampling is the special case \(p_{k,i}=1/n\), for which no importance correction is needed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive conditional sampling probabilities and inverse-probability correction make a sampled finite-sum gradient unbiased; uniform sampling is the equal-probability special case.
assumptions_latex: \(f(x)=n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n f_i(x)\) and every sampled component is differentiable at \(x_k\).

notation.meaning: Conditional probability of sampling component i at iteration k.
History available before sampling at iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The importance-corrected estimator and conditional-unbiasedness calculation are precise and fit the sampling-policy container, but the record has no inspectable citation.

children.title: Mini-Batch Policies
children.top_down_role: Batch-size choices for stochastic proximal-gradient updates.

knowledge_statements.title: Mini-Batch Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent importance-corrected mini-batches for proximal stochastic gradients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At iteration \(k\), choose a batch size \(b_k\ge 1\), draw conditionally independent indices \(i_{k,1},\ldots,i_{k,b_k}\) with probabilities \(p_{k,i}>0\), and form
\[
v_k=\frac{1}{b_k}\sum_{j=1}^{b_k}\frac{\nabla f_{i_{k,j}}(x_k)}{n p_{k,i_{k,j}}},
\qquad x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k g}(x_k-\alpha_kv_k).
\]
If every summand has conditional mean \(\nabla f(x_k)\), then \(v_k\) is conditionally unbiased. Under conditional independence and finite second moments,
\[
\mathbb{E}[\|v_k-\nabla f(x_k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]=\frac{1}{b_k}\mathbb{E}[\|v_{k,1}-\nabla f(x_k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k].
\]
Return the iterate selected by the prescribed terminal or averaging rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Average independent importance-corrected component gradients, then take a proximal step; conditional variance decreases by the reciprocal batch size.
assumptions_latex: \(i_{k,1},\ldots,i_{k,b_k}\) are conditionally independent with common probabilities \(p_{k,i}>0\).
Each corrected sample has finite conditional second moment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb{E}[v_k\mid\mathcal F_k]=\nabla f(x_k)\) and the conditional estimator variance scales as \(1/b_k\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The independent mini-batch policy and reciprocal variance scaling are mathematically consistent under the stated conditional assumptions, but no source supports the policy or variance identity.

children.title: Sampling-Bias Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits arising from biased or poorly matched sampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Bias Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Persistent sampling bias can redirect proximal stochastic iterations to the wrong objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Uncorrected nonuniform sampling generally targets a reweighted objective rather than the intended finite-sum objective. Concretely, let \(g=0\), \(f_1(x)=\tfrac12(x-1)^2\), \(f_2(x)=\tfrac12(x+1)^2\), and \(F=(f_1+f_2)/2\). Then \(F\) has the unique minimizer \(x^\star=0\). If the policy always samples component \(1\), the stochastic update with \(0<\alpha_k<1\) is
\[
x_{k+1}=x_k-\alpha_k(x_k-1).
\]
For constant \(\alpha_k=\alpha\), this sequence converges to \(1\), not to \(x^\star\). Thus persistent conditional bias cannot generally be removed by iterate averaging alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Always sampling one component can make the method converge to that component’s minimizer rather than the finite-sum minimizer; averaging does not eliminate persistent bias.
assumptions_latex: The policy selects component \(1\) with probability one.

notation.meaning: Uniform average of the two component objectives.
Minimizer of the intended objective F.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit quadratic counterexample is correct and the failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, but the record supplies no external source as required by the evidence contract.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear distance contraction of proximal gradient under strong convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constant-step proximal-gradient convergence when the smooth component is strongly convex and smooth and the regularizer is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f\) have an \(L\)-Lipschitz gradient and strong-convexity modulus \(m>0\), let \(\psi\) be convex, and let \(x^*\) be the unique minimizer of \(\phi=f+\tau\psi\). For proximal-gradient iterates using \(\alpha=2/(m+L)\),
\[
\|x^k-x^*\|\leq \left(\frac{\kappa-1}{\kappa+1}\right)^k\|x^0-x^*\|,
\qquad \kappa=\frac{L}{m}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the smooth component has an L-Lipschitz gradient and strong-convexity modulus m>0, while the regularizer is convex, proximal gradient with stepsize 2/(m+L) converges linearly in distance to the unique composite minimizer, with contraction factor (κ−1)/(κ+1), where κ=L/m.
assumptions_latex: x^*\text{ is the unique minimizer of }\phi=f+\tau\psi
