children.title: Matrix-Free Jacobian Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Implementations based on Jacobian and adjoint-Jacobian products.

knowledge_statements.title: Matrix-Free Jacobian Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Oracle representation avoiding explicit storage of the prox-linear Jacobian.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
At an outer point \(x\), let \(A=F'(x)\). A matrix-free inner solver represents \(A\) through the two oracles \[\mathcal J_x(v)=F'(x)v,
\qquad \mathcal J_x^*(u)=F'(x)^*u.\] Thus the affine model is evaluated as \(F(x)+\mathcal J_x(y-x)\), while primal-dual and dual updates use \(\mathcal J_x^*(u)\). Any inner algorithm whose dependence on \(A\) is exclusively through products \(Av\) and \(A^*u\) can therefore be implemented without assembling or storing the Jacobian matrix. Correct adjoint pairing requires \(\langle\mathcal J_xv,u\rangle=\langle v,\mathcal J_x^*u\rangle\) in the selected inner products.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Jacobian-vector and adjoint-Jacobian-vector products supply every linear operation required by compatible inner solvers, eliminating explicit Jacobian storage.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is differentiable at the current outer point.
The primal and image spaces have specified inner products.
Both product oracles are available and mutually adjoint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatible prox-linear inner iterations can use \(F'(x)\) without forming its matrix representation.

notation.meaning: Jacobian F'(x) as a linear operator.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The matrix-free representation is precise and standard, but no citation or explicit standard-field rationale supports the implementation claim for compatible prox-linear inner algorithms.

children.title: Smoothed Accelerated Inner-Solver Family
children.top_down_role: Inner-solution frameworks combining smoothing with accelerated first-order methods.

children.title: Smoothing-Based Inner Solves
children.top_down_role: Inner methods using smoothed convex subproblem representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing-Based Inner Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual regularization smooths a nonsmooth affine composite inner term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose \(h(z)=\max_{u\in Q}\{\langle u,z\rangle-h^*(u)\}\), where \(Q\) is compact. Choose a nonnegative strongly convex prox-function \(d\) on \(Q\) and \(\mu>0\), and define \[h_\mu(z)=\max_{u\in Q}\{\langle u,z\rangle-h^*(u)-\mu d(u)\}.\] For the inner model \(P(y)=h(Ay+b)+r(y)\), minimize the smooth approximation \(P_\mu(y)=h_\mu(Ay+b)+r(y)\) by a smooth composite first-order method. At each iteration evaluate the unique maximizer \(u_\mu(Ay+b)\), so that \(\nabla(h_\mu\circ(A\cdot+b))(y)=A^*u_\mu(Ay+b)\). Stop when smoothing bias plus optimization error meets the prescribed inner tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strongly convex dual regularization produces a differentiable approximation that can be minimized by smooth composite first-order methods.
assumptions_latex: \(d\) is nonnegative and strongly convex on \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The nonsmooth inner term is replaced by a differentiable approximation with an adjoint-Jacobian gradient formula.

notation.meaning: Unique maximizer defining the smoothed gradient.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual-smoothing construction is plausible, but the differentiability and gradient claims depend on strong-convexity conventions and require a specific smoothing reference.

children.title: Accelerated Inner Solves
children.top_down_role: Accelerated first-order methods for prox-linear subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Accelerated Inner Solves
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accelerated proximal-gradient complexity for a smooth strongly convex inner approximation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P_\mu(y)=s_\mu(y)+r(y)\), where \(s_\mu\) is convex with \(L_\mu\)-Lipschitz gradient and \(P_\mu\) is \(\alpha\)-strongly convex. An accelerated proximal-gradient method using \(\nabla s_\mu\) and \(\operatorname{prox}_{r/L_\mu}\) produces an iterate with \(P_\mu(y^j)-P_\mu^*\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) after \[j=O\!\left(\sqrt{\frac{L_\mu}{\alpha}}\log\frac{C}{\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}}\right)\] gradient and proximal-oracle calls, where \(C\) is an initial-error constant. For a prox-linear inner model containing \((1/(2t))\lVert y-x\rVert^2\), one may take \(\alpha\geq1/t\). The bound controls optimization error for the smoothed problem; smoothing bias must be budgeted separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Acceleration solves a smooth strongly convex inner approximation in square-root condition-number times logarithmic-accuracy oracle complexity.
assumptions_latex: The proximal map of \(r/L_\mu\) is computable.

notation.meaning: Initial-error constant in the accelerated bound.

source_refs.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

source_witnesses.locator: 10.4 Analysis of the Proximal Gradient Method-The Convex Case p. 281

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cited convex proximal-gradient section does not clearly support the stated accelerated strongly-convex logarithmic complexity. A locator for the exact accelerated theorem and its initial-error constant is required.

children.title: Smoothing-Bias Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Balance between smoother inner geometry and approximation bias.

knowledge_statements.title: Smoothing-Bias Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Additive error decomposition for dual smoothing and numerical inner optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\) and \(h_\mu\) be defined by the unsmoothed and smoothed dual maxima over \(Q\), and suppose \(0\leq d(u)\leq D\\) for all \(u\in Q\). Then for every \(z\), \[0\leq h(z)-h_\mu(z)\leq\mu D.\] Hence, for \(P(y)=h(Ay+b)+r(y)\) and \(P_\mu(y)=h_\mu(Ay+b)+r(y)\), any point satisfying \(P_\mu(y)-\inf P_\mu\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\) obeys \[P(y)-\inf P\leq\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}+\mu D.\] Thus an inner target \(\varepsilon\) is met, for example, by choosing \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{opt}}\leq\varepsilon/2\) and \(\mu D\leq\varepsilon/2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total inner error is at most optimization error plus smoothing bias, so accuracy must be divided between the two contributions.
assumptions_latex: \(Q\) is compact and \(0\leq d(u)\leq D<\infty\) on \(Q\).
The primal objectives have finite infima.
The same convex term \(r\) appears in both objectives.

notation.meaning: Uniform upper bound on the dual prox-function.
Optimization error for the smoothed problem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The additive error decomposition is plausible but uncited and normalization dependent. The assumption also contains a malformed \\ command after D that must be repaired once the sourced version is established.

children.title: Warm-Start Accuracy Policy Coupling
children.top_down_role: Reuse and termination policies for successive prox-linear subproblems.

children.title: Warm-Start Reuse Policies
children.top_down_role: Reuse choices for transferring candidate solutions across successive prox-linear subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Warm-Start Reuse Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-gated reuse of the preceding approximate inner solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For outer iteration \(k\), let \(Q_k\) be the current strongly convex inner objective, let \(z_{k-1}\) be the preceding inner output, and choose a computable residual \(R_k\) satisfying \(R_k(z)=0\) exactly at minimizers of \(Q_k\). Given a reuse threshold \(\tau_k\), set \(z_k^{(0)}=z_{k-1}\) when \(R_k(z_{k-1})\le\tau_k\); otherwise set \(z_k^{(0)}=D_k\), where \(D_k\) is a prescribed cold start. Apply the inner solver from \(z_k^{(0)}\) until its certified error is at most \(\varepsilon_k\), and return the resulting \(z_k\) to the outer method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse the previous inner solution only when its residual for the new model passes a prescribed test; otherwise use a designated cold start.
assumptions_latex: Each inner problem \(Q_k\) has a minimizer.
The inner solver supplies an error certificate at tolerance \(\varepsilon_k\).

notation.meaning: inner objective at outer iteration k
reuse threshold and requested inner accuracy

review_flags: The path does not identify a canonical residual or cold-start rule.
REQUEST_SOURCES: authoritative warm-start policy for prox-linear inner solves required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a coherent residual-gated algorithmic policy and the content kind fits, but no evidence identifies it as an established prox-linear warm-start policy or specifies the residual and certificate.

children.title: Inner-Accuracy Schedules
children.top_down_role: Fixed, adaptive, and progressively tightened accuracy regimes for inner solves.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Accuracy Schedules
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summable and relative-error schedules for inexact prox-linear subproblem solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_k\) be the regularized prox-linear model and let \(z_k\) be its computed solution. An absolute-error schedule requires \(Q_k(z_k)-\inf Q_k\le\varepsilon_k\) with \(\varepsilon_k\ge0\). A summable schedule satisfies \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\varepsilon_k<\infty\). A relative schedule instead requires \(Q_k(z_k)-\inf Q_k\le\eta_k\lVert z_k-x_k\rVert^2\), where \(0\le\eta_k\le\bar\eta\) and \(\bar\eta\) is strictly smaller than the exact-model descent coefficient. Either predicate makes inner error subordinate to the outer descent mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner solves may use summable absolute errors or errors proportional to the squared outer step, provided the relative coefficient stays below the descent margin.
assumptions_latex: Each \(Q_k\) is bounded below and attains its infimum.
The exact prox-linear model has a positive descent coefficient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_k(z_k)-\inf Q_k\le\varepsilon_k\) with \(\sum_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\), or \(Q_k(z_k)-\inf Q_k\le\eta_k\lVert z_k-x_k\rVert^2\) with \(\eta_k\le\bar\eta\).
review_flags: The admissible descent coefficient depends on the precise prox-linear model convention.
REQUEST_SOURCES: inexact prox-linear convergence theorem required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The admissible relative-error coefficient depends on the precise prox-linear model and descent theorem. A prox-linear inexactness result is needed to support the assertion that either schedule preserves the outer descent mechanism.

children.title: Reuse–Accuracy Coordination
children.top_down_role: Interactions between initialization quality, termination precision, and cumulative inner work.

knowledge_statements.title: Reuse–Accuracy Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A verifiable test coupling warm-start quality to the requested inner tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume every inner objective \(Q_k\) is \(m_k\)-strongly convex and that a computable residual satisfies \(Q_k(z)-\inf Q_k\le R_k(z)^2/(2m_k)\). For requested objective accuracy \(\varepsilon_k>0\), the previous output \(z_{k-1}\) is an accuracy-compatible warm start whenever \(R_k(z_{k-1})\le\sqrt{2m_k\varepsilon_k}\). Under this test, \(Q_k(z_{k-1})-\inf Q_k\le\varepsilon_k\), so the reused point already meets the requested inner tolerance; otherwise further inner iterations or a cold start are required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A previous inner solution is immediately reusable when its current-model residual is small enough to certify the new requested objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(R_k(z)^2/(2m_k)\) is a valid upper bound on inner suboptimality.

notation.meaning: strong-convexity modulus of the current inner objective
certifying residual for the current inner objective

review_flags: The residual-to-suboptimality inequality requires a specified residual definition.
REQUEST_SOURCES: strong-convexity residual certificate source required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The implication is valid under the stated residual-to-suboptimality inequality, and certificate is the correct content kind. A source and concrete residual definition are required to establish that inequality for the intended inner solver.

children.title: Prox-Linear Convergence Theory
children.top_down_role: Global, nonasymptotic, convex, local, and inexact convergence families.

children.title: Global Stationarity Convergence
children.top_down_role: Global convergence toward composite stationarity.

knowledge_statements.title: Global Stationarity Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic prox-linear convergence under global model fidelity and bounded iterates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=g(x)+h(c(x))\), where \(g\) is proper closed convex, \(h\) is convex and \(L_h\)-Lipschitz, and \(c\) is continuously differentiable with \(\beta\)-Lipschitz Jacobian. Put \(\mu=L_h\beta\), choose \(0<t<1/\mu\), and let \(x_{k+1}\) minimize \(g(y)+h(c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)(y-x_k))+\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2/(2t)\). If \(F\) is bounded below and \((x_k)\) is bounded, then \(F(x_k)\) converges, \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\to0\), and every cluster point \(\bar x\) satisfies \(0\in\partial F(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a globally valid linearization bound and bounded iterates, exact prox-linear steps vanish and every accumulation point is composite stationary.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper closed convex, \(h\) is convex and Lipschitz, and \(c\) has Lipschitz Jacobian.
\(F\) is bounded below and the generated sequence is bounded.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F(x_k)\) converges, \(\lVert x_{k+1}-x_k\rVert\to0\), and \(0\in\partial F(\bar x)\) for every cluster point \(\bar x\).
review_flags: A prox-linear-specific stationarity theorem and chain-rule qualification must be source-checked.
REQUEST_SOURCES: exact global convergence theorem required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem has the correct local role, but its stationarity conclusion, chain-rule requirements, and exact step-size constant require a prox-linear convergence source.

children.title: Prox-Linear Stationarity Complexity
children.top_down_role: Nonasymptotic complexity measured through prox-linear and envelope residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Stationarity Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic outer-iteration bound measured by the prox-linear gradient mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the composite assumptions defining \(\mu=L_h\beta\), choose \(0<t<1/\mu\), let \(x_{k+1}\) be the exact prox-linear step, and define \(G_t(x_k)=(x_k-x_{k+1})/t\). If \(F_*=\inf F> -\infty\), model fidelity and optimality give \(F(x_{k+1})\le F(x_k)-t(1-t\mu)\lVert G_t(x_k)\rVert^2/2\). Consequently, for every integer \(N\ge1\), \(\min_{0\le k<N}\lVert G_t(x_k)\rVert^2\le 2(F(x_0)-F_*)/[t(1-t\mu)N]\). Hence at most \(O(\varepsilon^{-2})\) exact outer steps are needed to obtain \(\lVert G_t(x_k)\rVert\le\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The smallest prox-linear residual among the first N iterates is order one over square root N, yielding order epsilon-minus-two exact outer steps.
assumptions_latex: The objective has the globally Lipschitz convex-composite structure used in the exact prox-linear method.
review_flags: The constant depends on the precise step-size and model-error convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind and residual rate fit the node, but the descent coefficient depends on the exact model-error and step-size convention. A prox-linear stationarity-complexity theorem is required.

children.title: Convex Composite Convergence
children.top_down_role: Objective and solution convergence when the full composite objective is convex.

knowledge_statements.title: Convex Composite Convergence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex affine-composite specialization, where prox-linear iteration becomes proximal point iteration.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(m,n\ge 1\), let \(A:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be linear, let \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be convex functions such that \(F(x)=g(x)+h(Ax+b)\) is proper, closed, and has nonempty solution set \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}F\). For fixed \(t>0\), define \(x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^n}\{F(y)+\lVert y-x_k\rVert^2/(2t)\}\). Because the affine mapping is identical to its linearization, this is the corresponding exact prox-linear step. For every \(x_*\in S\) and every integer \(k\ge1\), the iterates satisfy \(F(x_k)-F_*\le\lVert x_0-x_*\rVert^2/(2tk)\), where \(F_*=\min F\); moreover, in finite dimensions, \((x_k)\) converges to a point of \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a proper closed convex affine composite with a minimizer, the exact prox-linear iteration is the proximal point iteration: objective error decays as one over k, and the iterates converge to a minimizer.
assumptions_latex: \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) are convex, and \(F=g+h\circ(A\cdot+b)\) is proper and closed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(x_*\in S\) and \(k\ge1\), \(F(x_k)-F_*\le\lVert x_0-x_*\rVert^2/(2tk)\), and \(x_k\to\bar x\in S\).

notation.meaning: solution set of the convex composite problem

source_refs.source_title: Large-Scale Convex Optimization: Algorithms & Analyses via Monotone Operators
source_refs.locator: 2.6 Proximal point method p. 44

review_flags: Scope is restricted to affine composition, for which the prox-linear model equals the objective.

children.title: Local Fast-Convergence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Improved local convergence under sharpness and variational regularity.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Fast-Convergence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharpness and metric-subregularity predicates associated with locally fast prox-linear behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\operatorname*{argmin}F\) be nonempty and let \(\bar x\in S\). A local sharpness regime holds if there exist \(\alpha>0\) and a neighborhood \(U\) of \(\bar x\) such that \(F(x)-F_*\ge\alpha\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\) for all \(x\in U\). A local metric-subregularity regime for stationarity holds if there exist \(\kappa>0\) and a neighborhood \(V\) of \(\bar x\) such that \(\operatorname{dist}(x,S)\le\kappa\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial F(x))\) for all \(x\in V\). Quantitative fast-convergence theorems additionally require compatibility between these bounds and the prox-linear model error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local fast regimes are characterized by sharp objective growth or an error bound converting stationarity residuals into distance to the solution set.
assumptions_latex: \(\partial F\) denotes a subdifferential supporting the stated error bound.
review_flags: These predicates do not alone select a unique linear, superlinear, or quadratic prox-linear theorem.
REQUEST_SOURCES: prox-linear sharpness or variational-regularity convergence result required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicates are plausible local regularity conditions and condition is an acceptable content kind, but the record does not establish which prox-linear fast rate follows. A source must specify the subdifferential, model compatibility, and resulting rate.

children.title: Approximate Prox-Linear Work Complexity
children.top_down_role: Total-work and sampling complexity for approximate prox-linear realizations.

children.title: Outer–Inner Total Work
children.top_down_role: Aggregate work regimes combining outer progress with approximate inner computation.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer–Inner Total Work
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total deterministic work obtained by summing iteration-dependent inner-solver costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an outer method needs \(K(\varepsilon)\) iterations to return an \(\varepsilon\)-stationary point. At iteration \(k\), suppose its inner objective is \(m_k\)-strongly convex with \(L_k\)-Lipschitz gradient and an accelerated solver reaches objective error \(\delta_k\) in at most \(C\sqrt{\kappa_k}\log(A_k/\delta_k)\) first-order oracle calls, where \(\kappa_k=L_k/m_k\) and \(A_k\) bounds the initial inner gap. Then total inner work is at most \(C\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}\sqrt{\kappa_k}\log(A_k/\delta_k)\). Uniform bounds \(\kappa_k\le\bar\kappa\), \(A_k\le\bar A\), and \(\delta_k\ge\underline\delta\) reduce this to \(O(K(\varepsilon)\sqrt{\bar\kappa}\log(\bar A/\underline\delta))\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Total approximate prox-linear work is the sum of all inner costs; uniform conditioning and accuracy bounds factor this into outer iterations times a worst-case inner cost.
assumptions_latex: The outer iteration bound \(K(\varepsilon)\) is valid for the chosen inner-error schedule.
Each inner objective satisfies the stated smooth strong-convexity conditions.
The displayed accelerated inner bound holds from the selected initialization.
review_flags: The bound is a composition rule; a source must verify compatibility of the outer guarantee with the inner schedule.
REQUEST_SOURCES: approximate prox-linear total-work theorem required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The summation is a valid conditional accounting identity, but a source must verify that the stated inner costs and accuracy schedule preserve the assumed outer bound for approximate prox-linear iteration.

children.title: Stochastic Oracle Complexity
children.top_down_role: Sampling-cost regimes for stochastic prox-linear realizations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Oracle Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic strongly convex stochastic inner-solver cost under bounded gradient variance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At outer iteration \(k\), let \(Q_k\) be \(m_k\)-strongly convex and \(L_k\)-smooth. Suppose a stochastic oracle returns \(G_k(z,\xi)\) with \(\mathbb{E}[G_k(z,\xi)]=\nabla Q_k(z)\) and \(\mathbb{E}\lVert G_k(z,\xi)-\nabla Q_k(z)\rVert^2\le\sigma_k^2\). Standard variance-controlled stochastic-gradient schemes can attain \(\mathbb{E}[Q_k(z_k)-\inf Q_k]\le\delta_k\) using \(O\!\left((L_k/m_k)\log(A_k/\delta_k)+\sigma_k^2/(m_k\delta_k)\right)\) stochastic-gradient samples. Summing this quantity for \(k<K(\varepsilon)\) gives the total stochastic inner-oracle complexity of the approximate outer method.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each stochastic inner solve pays a condition-number transient plus a variance-over-accuracy term; total oracle complexity sums these costs across outer iterations.
assumptions_latex: The stochastic gradient is unbiased with variance at most \(\sigma_k^2\).
The outer convergence theorem accepts expected inner error \(\delta_k\).
review_flags: The precise rate depends on the stochastic inner algorithm and oracle model.
REQUEST_SOURCES: stochastic approximate prox-linear oracle-complexity theorem required.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The precise stochastic rate depends on the selected algorithm and oracle model, while the quantity A_k is not defined. A stochastic approximate prox-linear complexity theorem is required.

children.title: Accuracy–Sampling Complexity Coupling
children.top_down_role: Complexity changes induced by coordinating inner precision with sampling effort.

knowledge_statements.title: Accuracy–Sampling Complexity Coupling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Batch-size rule ensuring stochastic noise remains below the requested inner accuracy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an averaged mini-batch gradient for an \(m_k\)-strongly convex inner problem have variance at most \(\sigma_k^2/B_k\), where \(B_k\) is the batch size. If the stochastic solver's noise-floor contribution to expected objective error is bounded by \(C\sigma_k^2/(m_kB_k)\), then compatibility with an inner target \(\delta_k>0\) requires \(C\sigma_k^2/(m_kB_k)\le\delta_k\). Equivalently, it suffices to choose \(B_k\ge\lceil C\sigma_k^2/(m_k\delta_k)\rceil\). Thus tightening inner accuracy forces reciprocal growth of batch size unless variance is reduced by another mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To keep sampling noise below the inner tolerance, batch size must grow at least proportionally to variance divided by strong convexity and requested accuracy.
assumptions_latex: Independent averaging reduces gradient variance to at most \(\sigma_k^2/B_k\).
The solver's expected objective-error floor is at most \(C\sigma_k^2/(m_kB_k)\).

notation.meaning: mini-batch size at outer iteration k

review_flags: The constant and noise-floor formula depend on the selected stochastic solver.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The batch-size implication is algebraically correct once the asserted noise-floor bound holds, but that bound and the constant C depend on the stochastic solver and require a source.

children.title: Linearization-Fidelity Failure Boundary

children.title: Linearization Validity Regime
children.top_down_role: Local regularity regimes where linearized inner mappings remain informative.

knowledge_statements.title: Linearization Validity Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic fidelity of the composite linearization under Lipschitz Jacobian and Lipschitz outer loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable with \(\beta\)-Lipschitz Jacobian, and let \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) be \(L_h\)-Lipschitz. For all \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\), Taylor's remainder satisfies \(\lVert c(y)-c(x)-\nabla c(x)(y-x)\rVert\le\beta\lVert y-x\rVert^2/2\). Consequently, the linearized composite model obeys \(\left|h(c(y))-h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))\right|\le L_h\beta\lVert y-x\rVert^2/2\). Hence linearization is quadratically faithful on any region where the two Lipschitz constants are valid.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz Jacobian and Lipschitz outer function make the composite linearization error at most quadratic in the step length.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable and \(\nabla c\) is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz.
\(h\) is \(L_h\)-Lipschitz on a set containing the exact and linearized images.

notation.meaning: smooth inner mapping of the composite objective

children.title: Model-Fidelity Loss
children.top_down_role: Sources of mismatch between the local model and the original composite objective.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Fidelity Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the quadratic prox-linear model-error estimate when the inner Jacobian lacks Lipschitz regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F=h\circ c+g\) and \(M_x(y)=h(c(x)+
abla c(x)(y-x))+g(y)\). If \(h\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz and \(
abla c\) is \( eta\)-Lipschitz, then \[|F(y)-M_x(y)|\leq  rac{L eta}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] This quadratic fidelity can fail without Lipschitz continuity of \(
abla c\). For \(c(t)=|t|^{3/2}\), \(h(z)=z\), \(g=0\), and \(x=0\), one has \(M_0(t)=0\) but \[ rac{|F(t)-M_0(t)|}{|t|^2}=|t|^{-1/2}\longrightarrow\infty\quad	ext{as }t	o0.\] Thus no finite local quadratic model-error constant exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Lipschitz Jacobian yields quadratic model error. The function |t|^(3/2) shows that this bound can fail when the Jacobian is only Hölder continuous.
assumptions_latex: \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is convex and Lipschitz in the validity regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla c\) failing to be Lipschitz may destroy every bound of the form \(|F(y)-M_x(y)|\leq C\|y-x\|^2\).

notation.meaning: Outer Lipschitz and inner-Jacobian Lipschitz constants.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary, quadratic estimate, and Hölder counterexample are mathematically coherent and fit the terminal container, but no inspectable citation supports the exact fidelity constant or boundary claim.

children.title: Prediction Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where model-based predictions cease to support reliable outer progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Prediction Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary at which model-predicted reduction no longer controls actual composite-objective reduction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F=h\circ c+g\), define \(M_x(y)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+g(y)\), \(\operatorname{pred}=F(x)-M_x(y)\), and \(\operatorname{ared}=F(x)-F(y)\). Whenever \(|F(y)-M_x(y)|\leq \kappa\|y-x\|^2/2\), \[|\operatorname{ared}-\operatorname{pred}|\leq \frac{\kappa}{2}\|y-x\|^2.\] Hence predicted descent guarantees actual descent only when \(\operatorname{pred}>\kappa\|y-x\|^2/2\). If this dominance condition fails, prediction may be inconclusive: for \(F(t)=t^2\), modeled at \(x=0\) through \(h(z)=z\) and \(c(t)=t^2\), the linearized model predicts zero change while every nonzero step increases \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Predicted reduction is reliable only when it dominates the model error. Otherwise a model may predict no change while the true objective increases.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is differentiable at the model base point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{pred}>\kappa\|y-x\|^2/2\) is sufficient for \(F(y)<F(x)\); without comparable control, model prediction need not determine the actual change.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The predicted-versus-actual reduction identity and example fit the failure-boundary container, but the record has no inspectable source for the model-error and acceptance claims.

children.title: Outer-Loss Regularity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of standard prox-linear structure beyond controlled convex outer losses.

knowledge_statements.title: Outer-Loss Regularity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of convex subproblems or quantitative fidelity beyond convex, locally Lipschitz outer losses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(F=h\circ c+g\) and the regularized prox-linear model \[Q_{x,\tau}(y)=h(c(x)+\nabla c(x)(y-x))+g(y)+\frac{1}{2\tau}\|y-x\|^2.\] Convexity of \(h\) and \(g\) makes \(Q_{x,\tau}\) convex, while local Lipschitz continuity of \(h\) converts inner linearization error into an objective-model error bound. Removing either property crosses the standard boundary: with \(h(z)=-|z|\), \(c(y)=y\), and \(g=0\), the model contains \(-|y|\) and is nonconvex for sufficiently weak quadratic regularization; without a finite local Lipschitz modulus for \(h\), an inner remainder bound alone supplies no finite linear error-transfer constant.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Outer convexity supports convex models, and outer Lipschitz continuity transfers inner approximation error. Dropping either property invalidates the corresponding standard guarantee.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Standard convexity and fidelity guarantees for \(Q_{x,\tau}\) require controlled convex outer-loss regularity.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content kind fits the boundary container, but no source supports the asserted standard boundary. Moreover, the example involving -|y| is nonconvex after adding any finite quadratic, so “sufficiently weak quadratic regularization” is imprecise.

children.title: Inner Subproblem Cost Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes where convexified subproblem cost dominates outer progress.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner Subproblem Cost Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outer iteration counts cease to represent computational cost when convexified models require expensive inner solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an outer prox-linear method performs \(K\) iterations and computes at iteration \(k\) an \(\varepsilon_k\)-accurate solution of its convex model using \(N_k(\varepsilon_k)\) inner oracle calls. Its total inner-oracle cost is \[N_{\mathrm{tot}}=\sum_{k=0}^{K-1}N_k(\varepsilon_k).\] An outer bound \(K=O(\epsilon^{-2})\) for producing an \(\epsilon\)-stationary point implies the same order in total oracle work only when \(N_k(\varepsilon_k)=O(1)\) uniformly. If required inner accuracy forces \(N_k(\varepsilon_k)\to\infty\), or if an inner problem lacks a certified complexity bound, the outer iteration rate alone gives no corresponding end-to-end complexity guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outer iteration rate is not an oracle-complexity rate unless inner model solves have uniformly controlled cost at the required accuracies.
assumptions_latex: \(N_k(\varepsilon_k)\) counts inner oracle calls needed for the prescribed model accuracy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K=O(\epsilon^{-2})\) does not imply \(N_{\mathrm{tot}}=O(\epsilon^{-2})\) without uniform control of \(N_k(\varepsilon_k)\).

notation.meaning: Required inner-solution accuracy at iteration k.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between outer iterations and total inner-oracle work fits the container, but no source is supplied. Uniform O(1) inner cost is sufficient, not necessary, for matching total order; bounded aggregate or average cost can also suffice.

children.title: Composite Stationarity Transfer Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on converting model residuals into stronger solution properties.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Stationarity Transfer Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Small model or envelope residuals transfer to first-order stationarity, not generally to local minimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a proper lower-semicontinuous \(\rho\)-weakly convex function \(f\) and \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), let \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\). Then \[(x-p)/\lambda\in\partial f(p),\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(p))\leq \|x-p\|/\lambda.\] Thus a small proximal or model residual certifies nearby first-order stationarity. It cannot, without additional curvature, error-bound, or regularity hypotheses, certify local minimality. Indeed, for \(f(t)=-\rho t^2/2\), the point \(x=0\) has zero proximal displacement and zero first-order residual for every \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), yet it is a strict local maximum rather than a local minimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small proximal residual yields nearby subdifferential stationarity, but stationarity alone cannot certify local minimality; a concave quadratic supplies a sharp counterexample.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|x-p\|/\lambda\) controls first-order stationarity at \(p\), but zero residual need not imply any local-minimum property.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stationarity-transfer limitation and counterexample fit the failure-boundary container, but the proximal inclusion and weakly convex parameter regime require an authoritative source. The case rho=0 also needs an explicit 1/0=+infinity convention.

children.title: Weak Convexity Proximal-Geometry Regimes
children.top_down_role: Problem classes, composite sources, and regularization regimes supporting weakly convex first-order analysis.

children.title: Weakly Convex Minimization
children.top_down_role: The base nonsmooth nonconvex problem class governed by lower curvature control.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Convex Minimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional extended-real formulation with Euclidean lower-curvature control.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A proper lower-semicontinuous function \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex, for \(\rho\geq0\), when \[x\longmapsto f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}\|x\|^2\] is convex. Weakly convex minimization is the problem \[\inf_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n} f(x)\] over such an \(f\). Equivalently, for every \(x,y\in\mathbb{R}^n\) and every \(v\in\partial f(x)\), the subgradient inequality \[f(y)\geq f(x)+\langle v,y-x\rangle-\frac{\rho}{2}\|y-x\|^2\] holds whenever the selected subdifferential admits this characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weakly convex minimization minimizes a function that becomes convex after adding a quadratic with curvature rho.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex exactly when \(f+(\rho/2)\|\cdot\|^2\) is convex.

notation.meaning: A subdifferential compatible with the stated inequality.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The primary definition fits the container and is standard, but no source is supplied. The asserted equivalent inequality does not specify a definite subdifferential, making that portion insufficiently precise.

children.title: Composite Sources of Weak Convexity
children.top_down_role: Smooth compositions, robust losses, and constrained models inheriting weak convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Composite Sources of Weak Convexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak convexity inherited by Lipschitz convex losses composed with smooth maps, with an added convex term.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex and \(L\)-Lipschitz, let \(c:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be continuously differentiable with \(\beta\)-Lipschitz Jacobian, and let \(g:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and convex. Then \[F(x)=h(c(x))+g(x)\] is \(L\beta\)-weakly convex on \(\mathbb{R}^n\). More generally, adding a \(\rho_g\)-weakly convex regularizer in place of convex \(g\) yields an \((L\beta+\rho_g)\)-weakly convex objective. Indicators of closed convex feasible sets are admissible convex choices of \(g\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A convex Lipschitz loss composed with a map having Lipschitz Jacobian is weakly convex; convex constraints and regularizers preserve this structure.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is convex, or more generally \(\rho_g\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h\circ c+g\) is \((L\beta+\rho_g)\)-weakly convex, with \(\rho_g=0\) for convex \(g\).

notation.meaning: Lipschitz constant of the outer loss.
Lipschitz constant of the inner Jacobian.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The inheritance property and content kind fit the composite-sources container, but no inspectable citation supports the L beta modulus or its extension to a weakly convex regularizer.

children.title: Convexified Proximal Subproblem Regime
children.top_down_role: The regularization range supporting convex proximal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexified Proximal Subproblem Regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal-parameter range in which quadratic regularization convexifies a weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex. For a center \(x\), define \[Q_{\lambda,x}(y)=f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2.\] The function \(Q_{\lambda,x}\) is convex whenever \(0<\lambda\leq1/\rho\), using the convention \(1/0=+\infty\). If \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), it is \((1/\lambda-\rho)\)-strongly convex and therefore has a unique minimizer. At \(\lambda=1/\rho\), convexity remains but uniqueness and even attainment are not guaranteed by weak convexity alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic proximal regularization convexifies a rho-weakly convex function for lambda at most 1/rho and is strongly convex below that threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q_{\lambda,x}\) is convex for \(\lambda\leq1/\rho\) and strongly convex with modulus \(1/\lambda-\rho\) for \(\lambda<1/\rho\).

notation.meaning: Proximal subproblem objective centered at x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convexification threshold, strong-convexity modulus, and endpoint qualification fit the condition container and appear mathematically precise, but no authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Weakly Convex Moreau-Envelope Geometry
children.top_down_role: The smoothed landscape underlying weakly convex stationarity and descent analysis.

knowledge_statements.title: Weakly Convex Moreau-Envelope Geometry
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differentiable Moreau geometry below the reciprocal weak-convexity threshold.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and choose \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). Define \[f_\lambda(x)=\min_y\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|y-x\|^2\right\},\qquad p_\lambda(x)=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x).\] The minimizer is unique, \(f_\lambda\) is continuously differentiable, and \[\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\frac{1}{\lambda}\bigl(x-p_\lambda(x)\bigr).\] Moreover, \(p_\lambda\) is \((1-\lambda\rho)^{-1}\)-Lipschitz, so the envelope gradient is Lipschitz and provides a smooth residual for the original nonsmooth problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Below the threshold 1/rho, the Moreau envelope is smooth and its gradient equals the scaled displacement from a point to its unique proximal point.

source_refs.locator: 6.7 The Moreau Envelope p. 163

source_witnesses.locator: 6.7 The Moreau Envelope p. 163

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property fits the Moreau-geometry container, but the cited Beck section is a convex Moreau-envelope reference and does not establish the stated weakly convex extension, threshold, or proximal Lipschitz constant.

children.title: Moreau-Envelope Stationarity
children.top_down_role: The principal stationarity and stopping system for weakly convex optimization.

children.title: Envelope-Gradient Stationarity
children.top_down_role: Stationarity measured on the smooth Moreau envelope.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope-Gradient Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximate stationarity measured by the norm of the smooth Moreau-envelope gradient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, with \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). A point \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stationary in the Moreau-envelope sense when \[\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon,\] where \(f_\lambda\) is the Moreau envelope. Exact envelope stationarity is the case \(\varepsilon=0\). Because \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x))\), exact envelope stationarity is equivalent to \(x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\), and hence to \(0\in\partial f(x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Envelope-gradient stationarity requires the Moreau-envelope gradient to be small; zero gradient is equivalent to a stationary fixed point of the proximal map.

source_refs.locator: 6.7 The Moreau Envelope p. 163

source_witnesses.locator: 6.7 The Moreau Envelope p. 163

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the stationarity container, but the cited convex Moreau-envelope section does not support the weakly convex smoothness regime or the claimed equivalence with limiting-subdifferential stationarity.

children.title: Proximal-Displacement Stationarity
children.top_down_role: The equivalent displacement-based stationarity interface.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Displacement Stationarity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent representation of envelope stationarity by scaled proximal displacement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the assumptions that \(f\) is proper, lower-semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex and that \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), the Moreau-envelope stationarity residual has the exact representation \[\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|=\frac{1}{\lambda}\left\|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\right\|.\] Consequently, \(x\) is \(\varepsilon\)-stationary in envelope gradient precisely when \[\left\|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\right\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon.\] The unscaled displacement depends on the choice of \(\lambda\), whereas the scaled displacement is exactly the envelope-gradient norm for that parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The envelope-gradient norm equals proximal displacement divided by lambda, so either quantity gives the same stationarity test after scaling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\leq\varepsilon\) if and only if \(\|x-\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\|\leq\lambda\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Proximal mapping of f with parameter lambda.

source_refs.locator: 6.7 The Moreau Envelope p. 163

source_witnesses.locator: 6.7 The Moreau Envelope p. 163

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation is internally consistent and fits the terminal container, but the cited convex reference does not support its use for proper lower-semicontinuous weakly convex functions.

children.title: Nearby-Point Stationarity Transfer
children.top_down_role: Transfer from envelope residuals to subdifferential stationarity at nearby proximal points.

knowledge_statements.title: Nearby-Point Stationarity Transfer
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Transfer of an envelope residual at one point to a subgradient residual at its proximal point.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^n	o\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, lower-semicontinuous, and \(ho\)-weakly convex, choose \(0<\lambda<1/ho\), and set \(p=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\). Proximal optimality gives \[v:= rac{x-p}{\lambda}\in\partial f(p).\] Since \(v=
abla f_\lambda(x)\), one obtains \[\|x-p\|=\lambda\|
abla f_\lambda(x)\|,\qquad \operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(p))\leq\|
abla f_\lambda(x)\|.\] Thus an envelope-\(\varepsilon\)-stationary point \(x\) produces a point \(p\) within distance \(\lambda\varepsilon\) having subdifferential residual at most \(\varepsilon\).

children.title: Stationarity Measure Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Relationships among envelope, subdifferential, slope, and model-based residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity Measure Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparison at a proximal point of a proper weakly convex function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex, and choose \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\). For \(x\in\mathbb{R}^d\), set \(\hat x=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)\). Then
\[
\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-\hat x)\in\partial f(\hat x),
\qquad
\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(\hat x))\le \|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|.
\]
Moreover, \(\|x-\hat x\|=\lambda\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\). Thus the envelope-gradient norm and proximal displacement are equivalent residuals, while either controls subdifferential stationarity at the nearby point \(\hat x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The envelope gradient equals the scaled proximal displacement and is a subgradient at the proximal point, so it bounds nearby subdifferential stationarity.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla f_\lambda(x)=\lambda^{-1}(x-\hat x)\in\partial f(\hat x)\) and \(\operatorname{dist}(0,\partial f(\hat x))\le\|\nabla f_\lambda(x)\|\).

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of f with parameter lambda

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The comparison is mathematically standard and fits the container, but no source is supplied for the weakly convex Moreau-envelope identity and nearby-point subdifferential bound.

children.title: Weakly Convex Model-Based Framework
children.top_down_role: A common regularized local-model organization for deterministic and stochastic weakly convex methods.

children.title: One-Sided Model Families
children.top_down_role: Local model classes organized by their approximation relationship to the objective.

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Model Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic upper-accurate local models with quadratic error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) and let \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}f\). A family \(\{f_x:x\in D\}\) is a \(\tau\)-one-sided model family for \(f\) on \(D\) if every \(f_x:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and lower semicontinuous, satisfies \(f_x(x)=f(x)\), and obeys
\[
f(y)\le f_x(y)+\frac{\tau}{2}\|y-x\|^2
\]
for all \(x,y\in D\). If each \(f_x\) is convex, the family is called a convex one-sided model family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-sided model is exact at its base point and underestimates the objective by no more than a prescribed quadratic error.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent and correctly categorized, but the orientation and exactness convention for a one-sided model family require a direct authoritative locator.

children.title: Deterministic Regularized Models
children.top_down_role: Deterministic local-model minimization under weak convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Regularized Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact minimization of a deterministic weakly convex local model over a convex feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D\subseteq\mathbb{R}^d\) be nonempty and convex, let \(x_0\in D\), and let \(\{f_x\}_{x\in D}\) be a deterministic model family such that each \(f_x:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho_m\)-weakly convex. Given \(0<\eta_k<1/\rho_m\), choose
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in D}\left\{f_{x_k}(y)+\frac{1}{2\eta_k}\|y-x_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
The minimized objective is \((1/\eta_k-\rho_m)\)-strongly convex. Consequently, if the displayed problem attains its minimum, its minimizer is unique. A declared residual or iteration budget determines termination and the output iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At each iteration, minimize the deterministic model plus quadratic regularization over a convex feasible set. Sufficiently strong regularization makes any attained minimizer unique.
assumptions_latex: Each \(f_x\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho_m\)-weakly convex.
The displayed subproblem attains its minimum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularized objective is \((1/\eta_k-\rho_m)\)-strongly convex, and its attained minimizer over \(D\) is unique.

notation.meaning: common weak-convexity modulus of the models

source_refs.locator: 10.5 The Proximal Point Method p. 288

source_witnesses.locator: 10.5 The Proximal Point Method p. 288

children.title: Stochastic Regularized Models
children.top_down_role: Sampled local-model minimization under weak convexity.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Regularized Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Regularized minimization of a sampled local model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_0\in D\). At iteration \(k\), draw a sample \(\xi_k\) conditionally on the history, form a measurable model \(f_{x_k}(\cdot;\xi_k)\), and choose
\[
x_{k+1}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in D}
\left\{f_{x_k}(y;\xi_k)+\frac{1}{2\eta_k}\|y-x_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
The sample may be replaced by a batch average. Stop after a prescribed sample budget or when a validated stationarity estimate meets tolerance, and output either the final iterate or an iterate selected by a declared probability rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Draw a sample or batch, minimize its local model plus quadratic regularization, and return an iterate according to a predetermined stopping and selection rule.
assumptions_latex: The sampled model is measurable and its regularized subproblem attains a minimizer almost surely.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is an almost-sure minimizer of the sampled regularized model displayed above.

notation.meaning: sample or minibatch drawn at iteration k
sampled local model based at x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The update is a plausible stochastic regularized-model algorithm and fits the container, but no source supports its measurability, sampling, stopping, and output conventions.

children.title: Model-Sampling Resource Allocation Policies
children.top_down_role: Choices among model strength, sampling cost, batching, and inner solution effort.

children.title: Model-Strength Selection
children.top_down_role: Choices among model families with differing local approximation strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Model-Strength Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic regularization strength sufficient to convexify a weakly convex model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(m_k:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper and \(\rho_k\)-weakly convex, with \(\rho_k\ge 0\), and let \(x_k\in\mathbb{R}^d\). Define
\[
Q_k(y):=m_k(y)+\frac{\gamma_k}{2}\|y-x_k\|^2.
\]
The model strength is admissible when \(\gamma_k>\rho_k\). Under this condition, \(Q_k\) is \((\gamma_k-\rho_k)\)-strongly convex. With \(\gamma_k=1/\eta_k\), this condition is \(0<\eta_k<1/\rho_k\) when \(\rho_k>0\), and any \(\eta_k>0\) is admissible when \(\rho_k=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose quadratic regularization strictly stronger than the model's weak-convexity modulus; the resulting model is strongly convex. For a convex model, every positive quadratic strength is admissible.

children.title: Sampling-Regime Selection
children.top_down_role: Choices among deterministic, stochastic, and mixed sampling regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Sampling-Regime Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbiased conditional sampling requirement for stochastic model updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\mathcal F_k\) contain all randomness revealed before iteration \(k\). A fresh-sampling regime is valid for an unbiased model statistic \(G(x,\xi)\) when \(\xi_k\) is conditionally independent of future randomness and
\[
\mathbb E[G(x_k,\xi_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]=\bar G(x_k)
\]
almost surely. In a finite-sum problem, uniform sampling with replacement satisfies this identity; deterministic cyclic sampling generally does not and must be analyzed through a bias or epochwise-error condition instead. The selected regime must therefore match the conditional expectation assumption used by the convergence statement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use fresh sampling when analysis requires conditional unbiasedness; cyclic or dependent sampling needs a separate bias or epochwise-error model.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[G(x_k,\xi_k)\mid\mathcal F_k]=\bar G(x_k)\) is the compatibility condition for conditionally unbiased sampling.

source_refs.locator: 8.3 The Stochastic Projected Subgradient Method p. 221

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 The Stochastic Projected Subgradient Method p. 221

children.title: Batch-Size Policies
children.top_down_role: Fixed and adaptive batch-size choices across model-based iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Batch-Size Policies
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance condition for iteration-dependent minibatch sizes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G(x,\xi)\) be conditionally unbiased with conditional variance at most \(\sigma^2\), and let \(\bar G_k=b_k^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^{b_k}G(x_k,\xi_{k,i})\) use conditionally independent samples. Then
\[
\mathbb E[\|\bar G_k-\bar G(x_k)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_k]\le\frac{\sigma^2}{b_k}.
\]
Consequently, a batch policy targeting conditional mean-square error at most \(v_k\) must choose \(b_k\ge\lceil\sigma^2/v_k\rceil\). For weighted stochastic errors, the sufficient summability condition \(\sum_k a_k^2/b_k<\infty\) determines how rapidly batches must grow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent averaging reduces conditional variance by the batch size; choose batches to meet a target variance or a required weighted summability condition.
assumptions_latex: Samples within each batch are conditionally independent and unbiased.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional variance reduction formula is standard, but no source is supplied. Moreover, the asserted weighted summability condition is only sufficient relative to a specified outer convergence analysis, which is not identified here.

children.title: Inner-Effort Allocation
children.top_down_role: Allocation of computational effort to regularized model subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Effort Allocation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accuracy schedule for inexact regularized-model subproblem solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the regularized model \(Q_k\), let \(Q_k^*=\inf_y Q_k(y)\), and let the inner solver return \(x_{k+1}\) satisfying
\[
Q_k(x_{k+1})-Q_k^*\le\varepsilon_k.
\]
An inner-effort schedule is summably accurate relative to outer weights \(a_k\ge0\) when \(\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}a_k\varepsilon_k<\infty\). If the inner method guarantees \(Q_k(z_t)-Q_k^*\le R_k(t)\), it suffices to allocate
\[
t_k=\min\{t\in\mathbb N:R_k(t)\le\varepsilon_k\}.
\]
This separates the required outer error budget from the inner solver’s rate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Set a summable outer error budget and run each inner solver only long enough for its certified rate to reach that iteration’s budget.
assumptions_latex: Each regularized subproblem has finite optimal value.
The inner solver has a valid error bound \(R_k(t)\).

notation.meaning: certified inner error after t steps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The rate-to-effort allocation formula is coherent, but the weighted summability requirement is convergence-framework dependent and lacks a direct source or an identified outer theorem.

children.title: Weakly Convex Algorithm Specializations
children.top_down_role: Classical subgradient, proximal-point, and prox-linear instances of the model-based framework.

children.title: Proximal Subgradient Methods for Weakly Convex Functions
children.top_down_role: Subgradient-based methods interpreted through weakly convex proximal geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal Subgradient Methods for Weakly Convex Functions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forward subgradient step followed by a proximal regularizer step.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=g(x)+r(x)\), where \(g\) is proper and \(\rho\)-weakly convex and \(r\) is proper, closed, and convex. Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}r\), choose \(v_k\in\partial g(x_k)\) and \(\alpha_k>0\), and update
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\alpha_k r}(x_k-\alpha_k v_k)
=\operatorname*{argmin}_y\left\{r(y)+\langle v_k,y-x_k\rangle+\frac{1}{2\alpha_k}\|y-x_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
Stop at a prescribed budget or residual threshold and output the declared final, averaged, or randomly selected iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Take a subgradient step for the weakly convex term and a proximal step for the convex regularizer, with a predetermined output rule.
assumptions_latex: \(g\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.

source_refs.locator: 9.3 Mirror Descent for the Composite Model p. 260
10.1 The Composite Model p. 269

source_witnesses.locator: 9.3 Mirror Descent for the Composite Model p. 260
10.1 The Composite Model p. 269

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proximal subgradient update is mathematically well defined and correctly categorized, but the cited convex composite-method sections do not directly support the stated weakly convex specialization with limiting subgradients.

children.title: Proximally Guided Subgradient Methods
children.top_down_role: Nested subgradient methods guided by approximate proximal-point targets.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximally Guided Subgradient Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inexact proximal-point iteration using an inner subgradient solver.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be \(\rho\)-weakly convex, choose \(\gamma>\rho\), and initialize \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}f\). At outer iteration \(k\), define
\[
Q_k(y)=f(y)+\frac{\gamma}{2}\|y-x_k\|^2.
\]
Starting from \(y_{k,0}=x_k\), apply a subgradient method to the strongly convex function \(Q_k\) until an iterate \(y_{k,T_k}\) satisfies a declared inner accuracy criterion. Set \(x_{k+1}=y_{k,T_k}\). Stop by an outer budget or proximal-displacement test and output the declared outer iterate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Approximately solve each strongly convex proximal subproblem by inner subgradient iterations, then use the approximate solution as the next outer iterate.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
The inner method can evaluate subgradients of \(Q_k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_{k+1}\) is the declared approximate minimizer of \(Q_k(y)=f(y)+(\gamma/2)\|y-x_k\|^2\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The nested proximal-subproblem structure fits the container, but no source is supplied and the inner accuracy criterion is left too unspecified to identify a particular proximally guided method.

children.title: Stochastic Proximal Point Methods for Weakly Convex Objectives
children.top_down_role: Sampled proximal models specialized to weakly convex stochastic objectives.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Proximal Point Methods for Weakly Convex Objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Samplewise proximal-point update for an expected weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=\mathbb E[f(x;\xi)]\), where almost every sample loss is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex. Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}F\), draw \(\xi_k\) from the prescribed sampling regime and choose \(0<\eta_k<1/\rho\). Compute
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_y
\left\{f(y;\xi_k)+\frac{1}{2\eta_k}\|y-x_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
The minimizer is unique whenever the subproblem attains its minimum. Stop after a declared oracle budget or validated residual test and output an iterate using the predetermined selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At every step, draw a sample loss and compute its proximal point; regularization stronger than sample weak convexity makes the attained minimizer unique.
assumptions_latex: Almost every \(f(\cdot;\xi)\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.
Each displayed subproblem attains its minimum almost surely.

source_refs.locator: 10.5 The Proximal Point Method p. 288

source_witnesses.locator: 10.5 The Proximal Point Method p. 288

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The samplewise proximal update and uniqueness condition are coherent, but the cited deterministic convex proximal-point section does not support the stochastic weakly convex method or its sampling and output rules.

children.title: Prox-Linear Methods for Weakly Convex Composites
children.top_down_role: Convex-linearized deterministic and stochastic models specialized to weakly convex compositions.

knowledge_statements.title: Prox-Linear Methods for Weakly Convex Composites
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic prox-linear iteration for a convex-Lipschitz outer function composed with a smooth inner mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(F(x)=h(c(x))+r(x)\), where \(h:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\) is proper, closed, convex, and \(L\)-Lipschitz, \(c:\mathbb{R}^d\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is continuously differentiable with \(\beta\)-Lipschitz Jacobian, and \(r:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper, closed, and convex. Then \(F\) is \(L\beta\)-weakly convex. Given \(x_0\in\operatorname{dom}r\) and \(t_k>0\), compute
\[
x_{k+1}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb{R}^d}\left\{h\bigl(c(x_k)+\nabla c(x_k)(y-x_k)\bigr)+r(y)+\frac{1}{2t_k}\|y-x_k\|^2\right\}.
\]
The displayed objective is strongly convex, so its attained minimizer is unique. Terminate according to a declared step-residual or iteration budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a weakly convex convex-over-smooth composite, linearize the smooth inner map, retain the convex outer function and regularizer, add a positive quadratic, and minimize the resulting strongly convex model.
assumptions_latex: \(c\) is continuously differentiable and its Jacobian is \(\beta\)-Lipschitz.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F=h\circ c+r\) is \(L\beta\)-weakly convex, and \(x_{k+1}\) is the unique minimizer of the displayed regularized convex-linearized model.

notation.meaning: Jacobian of c at the current iterate
Lipschitz constant of the Jacobian of c
