children.title: Weakly Convex Moreau-Envelope Descent Principle
children.top_down_role: The unifying convergence principle relating model quality, proximal regularization, and envelope progress.

children.title: Deterministic Model Descent
children.top_down_role: Envelope-progress guarantees for deterministic regularized local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Deterministic Model Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact proximal-point descent for a proper weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varphi:\mathbb{R}^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) be proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex. For \(0<\lambda<\rho^{-1}\), define \(\varphi_\lambda(x)=\min_y\{\varphi(y)+(2\lambda)^{-1}\|y-x\|^2\}\). Then, for every \(x\in\mathbb R^d\), with \(x^+=\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda\varphi}(x)\),
\[
\varphi_\lambda(x^+)\leq \varphi_\lambda(x)-\frac{1}{2\lambda}\|x-x^+\|^2
=\varphi_\lambda(x)-\frac{\lambda}{2}\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x)\|^2.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For every base point, an exact proximal step decreases the Moreau envelope by at least the squared proximal displacement divided by twice the proximal parameter, equivalently by one half of the parameter times the squared envelope-gradient norm.
assumptions_latex: \(\varphi\) is proper, lower semicontinuous, and \(\rho\)-weakly convex.

children.title: Expected Stochastic Model Descent
children.top_down_role: Expected envelope-progress guarantees for sampled local models.

knowledge_statements.title: Expected Stochastic Model Descent
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expected Moreau-envelope progress under a sampled-model descent inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((x_t)_{t\geq0}\) be adapted to \((\mathcal F_t)_{t\geq0}\), and let the differentiable function \(\varphi_\lambda\) satisfy \(\varphi_\lambda\geq\varphi_*>-\infty\). Suppose all displayed random variables are integrable and, for deterministic \(a_t>0\) and \(e_t\geq0\),
\[
\mathbb E[\varphi_\lambda(x_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq\varphi_\lambda(x_t)-a_t\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_t)\|^2+e_t.
\]
Then, for every integer \(T\geq1\),
\[
\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}a_t\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_t)\|^2\leq\mathbb E[\varphi_\lambda(x_0)]-\varphi_*+\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}e_t.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional expected envelope descent telescopes, bounding cumulative expected envelope-stationarity by the expected initial gap plus accumulated errors.
assumptions_latex: \(x_t\) is \(\mathcal F_t\)-measurable and all displayed random variables are integrable.
\(\varphi_\lambda\) is differentiable and bounded below by \(\varphi_*>-\infty\).
The displayed conditional inequality holds for deterministic \(a_t>0\) and \(e_t\geq0\).

children.title: Fidelity-Dependent Stationarity Complexity
children.top_down_role: Complexity families distinguished by local approximation fidelity.

children.title: Local Approximation Fidelity
children.top_down_role: Model-quality regimes distinguished by the accuracy of local objective approximation.

knowledge_statements.title: Local Approximation Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hölder-order fidelity of a local model to a target objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varphi:\mathbb R^d\to(-\infty,+\infty]\), and let \(m_x\) be a local model indexed by a base point \(x\). For \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), the model family has local approximation fidelity of order \(1+\alpha\) with constant \(L\geq0\) on \(D\subseteq\operatorname{dom}\varphi\) if \(m_x(x)=\varphi(x)\) and
\[
|m_x(y)-\varphi(y)|\leq \frac{L}{1+\alpha}\|y-x\|^{1+\alpha}
\]
for every \(x,y\in D\) for which the local model is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A model has order-one-plus-alpha fidelity when its error near the base point is bounded by the corresponding power of displacement.

source_refs.locator: 10.1 The Composite Model p. 269

source_witnesses.locator: 10.1 The Composite Model p. 269

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but the cited composite-model section is not enough to establish that it supports this two-sided Hölder-order fidelity definition and its normalization. A specific supporting definition or theorem is needed.

children.title: Fidelity-Dependent Stationarity Rates
children.top_down_role: Stationarity-complexity families indexed by local model fidelity.

knowledge_statements.title: Fidelity-Dependent Stationarity Rates
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic stationarity rate obtained from order-(1+\alpha) model errors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_R(\eta,T)\) be a randomized output produced after \(T\geq1\) iterations using a constant parameter \(\eta>0\). Suppose that, for every admissible \(\eta>0\),
\[
\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_R(\eta,T))\|^2\leq \frac{A}{\eta T}+B\eta^\alpha,
\]
where \(A,B>0\) and \(\alpha\in(0,1]\). If \(\eta_T=(A/(\alpha BT))^{1/(1+\alpha)}\) is admissible, then
\[
\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_R(\eta_T,T))\|^2\leq C_\alpha A^{\alpha/(1+\alpha)}B^{1/(1+\alpha)}T^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)},
\]
where \(C_\alpha=\alpha^{1/(1+\alpha)}+\alpha^{-\alpha/(1+\alpha)}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the two-term master bound holds at the balancing parameter, order-alpha model error yields squared envelope-stationarity proportional to T to the minus alpha over one plus alpha.
assumptions_latex: The displayed estimate holds for every admissible \(\eta>0\), with \(A,B>0\).

notation.meaning: randomized output generated with parameter eta in T iterations

children.title: Low-Fidelity Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Complexity limitations arising when local models provide weak predictive accuracy.

knowledge_statements.title: Low-Fidelity Complexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonvanishing stationarity floor when model errors have zero decay exponent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider the master estimate
\[
\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_R)\|^2\leq \frac{A}{\eta T}+B\eta^\alpha,
\]
with \(A,B>0\), \(0<\eta\leq\bar\eta\), and fidelity exponent \(\alpha\geq0\). At the boundary \(\alpha=0\), the estimate becomes \(A/(\eta T)+B\). Consequently, no choice of admissible \(\eta\) and \(T\) can make this certificate smaller than \(B\). Vanishing stationarity therefore requires either \(\alpha>0\), a fidelity constant \(B\) that decreases across iterations, or a sharper error mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With zero-order fidelity decay, the standard master bound retains a fixed stationarity floor, so increasing the iteration count alone cannot certify convergence.
assumptions_latex: The displayed master estimate is the available stationarity certificate.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and the infimum calculation are correct for the displayed master certificate. A source is needed for that certificate and for its connection to local-model fidelity; the conclusion must remain explicitly limited to this error model.

children.title: Weakly Convex Complexity Families
children.top_down_role: Complexity results separated by oracle, model specialization, and stationarity certificate.

children.title: Proximal-Subgradient Complexity
children.top_down_role: Envelope-stationarity complexity for deterministic and stochastic subgradient access.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Subgradient Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Envelope-stationarity complexity for bounded stochastic proximal-subgradient steps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varphi=f+r\) be proper and lower semicontinuous, with \(f\) \(\rho\)-weakly convex and \(r\) closed convex. Suppose \(g_t\) is conditionally unbiased with \(\mathbb E[\|g_t\|^2\mid x_t]\leq G^2\), and set
\[
x_{t+1}=\operatorname{prox}_{\eta r}(x_t-\eta g_t).
\]
For a suitable constant \(\eta=\Theta(T^{-1/2})\) and \(R\) uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\), the standard weakly convex analysis yields \(\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_{1/(2\rho)}(x_R)\|^2=O(T^{-1/2})\). Thus \(T=O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) suffices for \(\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_{1/(2\rho)}(x_R)\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded stochastic proximal-subgradient access gives an inverse-square-root squared-stationarity rate and an inverse-fourth-power iteration bound for envelope-gradient accuracy.
assumptions_latex: \(f\) is \(\rho\)-weakly convex and \(r\) is closed convex.
The oracle is conditionally unbiased with uniformly bounded second moment.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits, but conditional unbiasedness alone does not state that the oracle mean is a subgradient of f at x_t. The specialized weakly-convex theorem, admissible stepsize, and constants require an authoritative source before the mathematical hypotheses can be fixed reliably.

children.title: Stochastic Proximal-Point Complexity
children.top_down_role: Stationarity complexity for sample-dependent proximal subproblems.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Proximal-Point Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional envelope-stationarity complexity for sampled proximal subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(x_{t+1}\) solve a sample-dependent proximal subproblem, and suppose its population Moreau envelope obeys
\[
\mathbb E[\varphi_\lambda(x_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq\varphi_\lambda(x_t)-c\eta\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_t)\|^2+C\eta^2
\]
for constants \(c,C>0\), constant \(\eta\), and \(\inf\varphi_\lambda=\varphi_*>-\infty\). If \(R\) is uniform on \(\{0,\ldots,T-1\}\), then
\[
\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_R)\|^2\leq\frac{\varphi_\lambda(x_0)-\varphi_*}{c\eta T}+\frac{C\eta}{c}.
\]
Choosing \(\eta=\Theta(T^{-1/2})\) gives \(O(T^{-1/2})\) squared stationarity and \(O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) sampled subproblems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stochastic proximal-point method with linear progress and quadratic sampling error needs inverse-fourth-power sampled subproblems for expected envelope-gradient accuracy epsilon.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional envelope-descent inequality holds.
Each iteration solves one sampled proximal subproblem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The telescoping consequence is algebraically plausible, but the sampled proximal subproblem and the range over which the master inequality holds are not defined. A stochastic proximal-point theorem is needed to support the claimed algorithmic complexity.

children.title: Stochastic Prox-Linear Complexity
children.top_down_role: Stationarity complexity for stochastic convex-composite models.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Prox-Linear Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional stationarity rate for sampled convex-composite linearization models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\varphi(x)=h(F(x))+r(x)\), where \(h\) and \(r\) are proper closed convex functions and \(F\) is differentiable. At iteration \(t\), form an unbiased sampled approximation of the prox-linear model \(h(F(x_t)+F'(x_t)(y-x_t))+r(y)\), regularize it quadratically, and compute \(x_{t+1}\). If the resulting stationarity measure \(\mathcal G_t\) satisfies
\[
\mathbb E\|\mathcal G_R\|^2\leq\frac{A}{\eta T}+B\eta
\]
for uniform \(R\), then \(\eta=\Theta(T^{-1/2})\) yields \(\mathbb E\|\mathcal G_R\|^2=O(T^{-1/2})\), and \(T=O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) ensures \(\mathbb E\|\mathcal G_R\|\leq\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the standard prox-linear master estimate, stochastic convex-composite modeling attains inverse-square-root squared stationarity and inverse-fourth-power iteration complexity.
assumptions_latex: The composite model is well-defined and its regularized sampled subproblem is solvable.
The sampled model is unbiased with controlled second moment.
The displayed master estimate holds with \(A,B>0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound kind fits, but the sampled prox-linear construction, stationarity mapping normalization, regularity assumptions, and master estimate are too underspecified to constitute a stochastic prox-linear complexity theorem. These details require a supporting source.

children.title: Sampling Variance-Reduction Complexity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Sampling regimes altering oracle cost and envelope-stationarity complexity.

children.title: Mini-Batch Regimes
children.top_down_role: Complexity regimes arising from fixed or adaptive mini-batch sampling.

knowledge_statements.title: Mini-Batch Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Variance and oracle-complexity scaling under independent mini-batching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Suppose independent oracle samples \(g(x,\xi_i)\) satisfy \(\mathbb E[g(x,\xi_i)]=g(x)\) and \(\mathbb E\|g(x,\xi_i)-g(x)\|^2\leq\sigma^2\). For the mini-batch estimator \(\bar g_b(x)=b^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^b g(x,\xi_i)\),
\[
\mathbb E\|\bar g_b(x)-g(x)\|^2\leq\frac{\sigma^2}{b}.
\]
Consequently, any envelope-descent estimate of the form \(A/(\eta T)+C\eta\sigma^2/b\) is minimized at \(\eta=\Theta(\sqrt{b/T})\), when admissible, and yields \(O((bT)^{-1/2})\) squared stationarity. Achieving norm accuracy \(\varepsilon\) therefore uses \(bT=O(\varepsilon^{-4})\) samples in this regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent batches reduce variance by their size, improving iteration count while leaving the basic inverse-fourth-power total sample scaling unchanged.
assumptions_latex: Batch samples are conditionally independent and identically distributed.
The oracle has variance at most \(\sigma^2\).
The stated envelope-descent estimate and optimized parameter are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E\|\bar g_b-g\|^2\leq\sigma^2/b\) and the master bound scales as \(O((bT)^{-1/2})\).

source_refs.locator: 8.3 The Stochastic Projected Subgradient Method p. 221

source_witnesses.locator: 8.3 The Stochastic Projected Subgradient Method p. 221

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The independent mini-batch variance calculation is standard, but the cited stochastic projected-subgradient section does not presently establish the weakly-convex envelope master bound or its admissible parameter regime. A specific source for that extension is required.

children.title: Variance-Reduced Regimes
children.top_down_role: Oracle-complexity regimes using variance-reduction mechanisms.

knowledge_statements.title: Variance-Reduced Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Summability condition under which estimator error preserves deterministic-rate envelope descent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(v_t\) estimate \(g(x_t)\), and suppose deterministic numbers \(V_t\geq0\) satisfy
\[
\mathbb E[\|v_t-g(x_t)\|^2\mid\mathcal F_t]\leq V_t
\]
almost surely. Suppose also that, for constants \(c,C>0\) and deterministic \(\eta_t>0\),
\[
\mathbb E[\varphi_\lambda(x_{t+1})\mid\mathcal F_t]
\leq \varphi_\lambda(x_t)-c\eta_t\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_t)\|^2+C\eta_tV_t,
\]
where \(\varphi_\lambda\geq\varphi_*>-\infty\). If
\[
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\eta_tV_t<\infty
\quad\text{and}\quad
\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\eta_t=+nfty,
\]
then
\[
\frac{\sum_{t<T}\eta_t\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_t)\|^2}{\sum_{t<T}\eta_t}
\leq
\frac{\mathbb E[\varphi_\lambda(x_0)]-\varphi_*+C\sum_{t<T}\eta_tV_t}{c\sum_{t<T}\eta_t}
\longrightarrow0.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Variance reduction preserves vanishing weighted expected stationarity when deterministic conditional variance bounds are stepsize-summable while the cumulative progress weights diverge.
assumptions_latex: The displayed conditional variance and envelope-descent inequalities hold and are integrable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sum_t\eta_tV_t<\infty\) and \(\sum_t\eta_t=+nfty\) imply vanishing weighted average expected stationarity.

notation.meaning: deterministic upper bound on conditional mean-square estimator error

children.title: Sample-Complexity Transitions
children.top_down_role: Crossovers in sampling cost as batch scale or variance control changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Sample-Complexity Transitions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crossover between iteration reduction and total-sample reduction under batching.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Assume a mini-batch method has the stationarity certificate
\[
S_T(b)\leq \frac{A}{\eta T}+\frac{C\eta\sigma^2}{b},
\]
where \(A,C,\sigma>0\), \(b\in\mathbb N\), and \(S_T(b)=\mathbb E\|\nabla\varphi_\lambda(x_R)\|^2\). If \(\eta_* = \sqrt{Ab/(C\sigma^2T)}\) is admissible, then
\[
S_T(b)\leq 2\sqrt{AC}\,\frac{\sigma}{\sqrt{bT}}.
\]
Thus, within this certificate, increasing \(b\) reduces the required iteration count proportionally but does not improve the order in the total sample count \(N=bT\). A better order in \(N\) requires a different governing bound, such as one arising from additional variance structure, finite-sum reuse, or a deterministic-term regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Within the stated two-term certificate, batching trades more samples per iteration for fewer iterations without improving the total-sample order; a transition requires a different governing bound.
assumptions_latex: The displayed two-term mini-batch certificate holds with \(A,C,\sigma>0\) and \(b\in\mathbb N\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_T(b)=O(\sigma/\sqrt{N})\) with \(N=bT\), so this certificate gives no sample-order improvement from batching alone.

notation.meaning: total number of sampled oracle calls

children.title: Oracle-Inner Work Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Work comparisons among subgradient, prox-linear, and direct stochastic proximal models.

children.title: Oracle Work Profiles
children.top_down_role: Oracle-use profiles across subgradient, prox-linear, and stochastic proximal models.

knowledge_statements.title: Oracle Work Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Accounting identity for outer oracle work in model-based methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an outer method run for \(T\) iterations, let \(q_t^{(j)}\) be the number of calls to oracle type \(j\in\{1,\ldots,J\}\) at iteration \(t\), and assign nonnegative unit cost \(c_j\) to that oracle. Its oracle-work profile is
\[
Q_T=\left(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}q_t^{(1)},\ldots,\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}q_t^{(J)}\right),
\]
and its scalar weighted oracle work is
\[
W_T^{\mathrm{oracle}}=\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_j(Q_T)_j
=\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\sum_{j=1}^{J}c_jq_t^{(j)}.
\]
For one oracle type and a constant mini-batch size \(b\), the one-dimensional profile is \(Q_T=(bT)\), and the unweighted call count is \(bT\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An oracle-work profile counts each oracle type separately, while a weighted sum converts the vector into scalar work; one constant-size batch per iteration gives bT calls.
assumptions_latex: Each \(q_t^{(j)}\) is a nonnegative integer and each \(c_j\geq0\).

notation.meaning: type-j calls made at iteration t

children.title: Inner-Solve Work Profiles
children.top_down_role: Subproblem-computation profiles across competing weakly convex methods.

knowledge_statements.title: Inner-Solve Work Profiles
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counts inner iterations needed by an inexact proximal-composite method to reach a prescribed outer stationarity tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K(\varepsilon)\) be the number of outer iterations required for stationarity tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), and let the inner problem at iteration \(k\) be solved to accuracy \(\delta_k\) using \(m_k(\delta_k)\) elementary inner steps. The inner-solve work profile is
\[W_{\mathrm{in}}(\varepsilon)=\sum_{k=0}^{K(\varepsilon)-1}m_k(\delta_k).\]
If \(m_k(\delta)\leq m(\delta)\) uniformly and the accuracy schedule satisfies \(\delta_k\geq\delta_{K(\varepsilon)}\), with \(m\) nonincreasing in its accuracy argument, then
\[W_{\mathrm{in}}(\varepsilon)\leq K(\varepsilon)m(\delta_{K(\varepsilon)}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inner work is the sum of per-outer-iteration solution costs; a uniform inner bound gives outer iteration count times the finest required inner cost.
assumptions_latex: \(K(\varepsilon)<\infty\) and every prescribed inner accuracy is attainable.
\(m(\delta)\) is nonincreasing as the permitted error \(\delta\) decreases.

notation.meaning: Outer iterations required for tolerance epsilon.
Required accuracy of the kth inner solve.
Elementary work used by the kth inner solve.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the work-profile leaf, and the displayed bound is mathematically consistent when larger delta means looser accuracy and m is nonincreasing in delta. However, no citation supports the inexact-solve work model, accuracy convention, or work unit. The wording of the monotonicity assumption should also be checked against the eventual source.

children.title: Total-Work Crossover Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes where differences in oracle cost or inner effort alter total-work preference.

knowledge_statements.title: Total-Work Crossover Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when reduced outer-oracle work compensates for additional inner-solve work.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For algorithm families \(A\) and \(B\) attaining the same tolerance \(\varepsilon\), assign unit costs \(c_o>0\) and \(c_i>0\) to outer-oracle calls and elementary inner steps. With counts \(N_o^j(\varepsilon)\) and \(N_i^j(\varepsilon)\), define
\[W_j(\varepsilon)=c_oN_o^j(\varepsilon)+c_iN_i^j(\varepsilon),\qquad j\in\{A,B\}.\]
Family \(A\) has smaller total work precisely when
\[c_o\bigl(N_o^B-N_o^A\bigr)>c_i\bigl(N_i^A-N_i^B\bigr).\]
When both differences are positive, the crossover occurs at
\[\frac{c_o}{c_i}=\frac{N_i^A-N_i^B}{N_o^B-N_o^A}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A method’s oracle savings outweigh its extra inner work exactly above the displayed relative-cost crossover threshold.
assumptions_latex: Both families use the same stationarity criterion and tolerance \(\varepsilon\).
The additive cost model assigns fixed positive costs \(c_o\) and \(c_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_A(\varepsilon)<W_B(\varepsilon)\) exactly under the displayed cost-difference inequality.

notation.meaning: Elementary inner-step count for family j.
Total weighted work for family j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition role fits the crossover-regime leaf, and the crossover inequality follows from the stated additive cost model. No source is cited for using this fixed two-resource model in the weakly convex proximal-composite setting, so the intended mathematical model cannot be validated.

children.title: Algorithm-Family Work Comparisons
children.top_down_role: Work-based comparisons among subgradient, prox-linear, and direct stochastic proximal families.

knowledge_statements.title: Algorithm-Family Work Comparisons
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares weakly convex algorithm families only after normalizing accuracy criteria and computational work units.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each family \(j\in\mathcal J\) return \(x_j\) satisfying the same criterion \(\mathbb E[R(x_j)]\leq\varepsilon\). If its resource-count vector is \(n_j(\varepsilon)=(N_{j,1},\ldots,N_{j,p})\) and the positive unit-cost vector is \(c=(c_1,\ldots,c_p)\), compare families through
\[W_j(\varepsilon)=c^{\mathsf T}n_j(\varepsilon).\]
Family \(A\) weakly dominates family \(B\) for all positive cost assignments exactly when \(N_{A,r}(\varepsilon)\leq N_{B,r}(\varepsilon)\) for every resource \(r\). If their count vectors are incomparable componentwise, their ordering necessarily depends on the cost ratios.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform work dominance requires no more use of every resource; otherwise the preferred algorithm family depends on relative resource costs.
assumptions_latex: Every family is evaluated at the same tolerance \(\varepsilon\) for the same residual \(R\).
Resource counts are nonnegative and total work is additive with \(c_r>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_A(\varepsilon)\leq W_B(\varepsilon)\) for every \(c>0\) if and only if \(n_A(\varepsilon)\leq n_B(\varepsilon)\) componentwise.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the algorithm-family comparison leaf. The componentwise-dominance equivalence is correct for finite resource vectors and all strictly positive cost vectors, but no cited source supports the chosen residual normalization, resource taxonomy, or comparison framework.

children.title: Weakly Convex Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits of proximal regularization, sampled models, and envelope-based stationarity.

children.title: Beyond-Weak-Convexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Objectives for which standard quadratic regularization does not recover the required proximal geometry.

knowledge_statements.title: Beyond-Weak-Convexity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A concrete objective for which no finite quadratic regularization yields convex proximal geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
On \(\mathbb R\), let \(f(x)=-x^4\). For every finite \(\rho\geq0\),
\[x\longmapsto f(x)+\frac{\rho}{2}x^2=-x^4+\frac{\rho}{2}x^2\]
is not convex, so \(f\) is not weakly convex. Moreover, for every \(\lambda>0\) and center \(x\in\mathbb R\),
\[\inf_{y\in\mathbb R}\left\{-y^4+\frac{1}{2\lambda}(y-x)^2\right\}=-\infty.\]
Thus quadratic regularization neither convexifies the objective nor produces a nonempty proximal map, and the ordinary Moreau envelope is not finite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The objective minus the fourth power overwhelms every quadratic regularizer, making all proximal subproblems unbounded below.

notation.meaning: Minimizers of the quadratically regularized proximal subproblem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role and example match the exact container: the negative quartic is not weakly convex and every quadratically regularized proximal subproblem is unbounded below. The record nevertheless supplies no inspectable citation for the weak-convexity boundary or the example.

children.title: Proximal-Map Well-Posedness Boundary
children.top_down_role: Loss of stable envelope and displacement interpretations.

children.title: Set-Valued Proximal Maps
children.top_down_role: Regimes where proximal subproblems admit multiple relevant outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Set-Valued Proximal Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows that a proper lower-semicontinuous objective may have a genuinely set-valued proximal map at the curvature boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\lambda>0\) and define the proper continuous function \(f(y)=-y^2/(2\lambda)\) on \(\mathbb R\). At the center \(x=0\), the proximal objective satisfies
\[f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}(y-x)^2=0\qquad\text{for every }y\in\mathbb R.\]
Consequently,
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=\operatorname*{argmin}_{y\in\mathbb R}\left\{f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}y^2\right\}=\mathbb R,\]
so the proximal map is not single-valued. At any \(x\neq0\), the same proximal objective is affine and unbounded below, hence the proximal map is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the exact curvature boundary, every real number minimizes the centered proximal problem, while off-center proximal problems have no minimizer.

notation.meaning: Boundary-curvature objective used in the example.
Set of minimizers of the proximal subproblem.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role fits the set-valued proximal-map leaf, and the stated proximal map is all of R at zero and empty off zero. No source reference or specific locator is attached; the general inventory entries cannot be treated as citations for this record.

children.title: Proximal-Map Instability
children.top_down_role: Sensitivity of proximal outputs to perturbations in inputs or regularization.

knowledge_statements.title: Proximal-Map Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies loss of proximal-map conditioning as the regularization parameter approaches the weak-convexity boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(y)=-\rho y^2/2\) on \(\mathbb R\), where \(\rho>0\). For \(0<\lambda<1/\rho\), the proximal subproblem is strongly convex and direct minimization gives
\[\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(x)=\frac{x}{1-\lambda\rho}.\]
Hence its global Lipschitz modulus is
\[\operatorname{Lip}(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f})=\frac{1}{1-\lambda\rho},\]
which diverges as \(\lambda\uparrow1/\rho\). At \(\lambda=1/\rho\), the proximal map becomes all of \(\mathbb R\) at \(x=0\) and empty at every \(x\neq0\), demonstrating the sharp loss of well-posedness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proximal map’s sensitivity grows without bound as the stepsize reaches the reciprocal weak-convexity constant.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the instability leaf. The proximal formula, Lipschitz modulus, divergence at the critical parameter, and endpoint behavior are internally correct, but there is no cited source with a locator supporting the sharp boundary interpretation.

children.title: Envelope Interpretation Failure
children.top_down_role: Loss of reliable Moreau-envelope interpretations outside stable proximal regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Envelope Interpretation Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Demonstrates failure of the finite differentiable-envelope interpretation at the critical proximal parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(y)=-\rho y^2/2\) with \(\rho>0\), and take the critical parameter \(\lambda=1/\rho\). The Moreau-envelope objective at \(x\in\mathbb R\) reduces to
\[f(y)+\frac{1}{2\lambda}(y-x)^2=\frac{\rho x^2}{2}-\rho xy.\]
Therefore \(f_\lambda(0)=0\), with every \(y\in\mathbb R\) minimizing, while \(f_\lambda(x)=-\infty\) for every \(x\neq0\). Thus the envelope is not finite on any neighborhood of zero and cannot supply a differentiable merit function or the usual proximal-gradient identity there.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At the critical stepsize, the Moreau envelope is finite only at zero and therefore cannot serve as a smooth stationarity measure.

notation.meaning: Moreau envelope of f with parameter lambda.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role matches the envelope-interpretation leaf, and the critical-parameter envelope calculation is correct. The claim lacks an attached authoritative source and specific locator for the usual finite differentiable-envelope interpretation and its failure at the boundary.

children.title: Displacement Ambiguity
children.top_down_role: Loss of a consistent stationarity interpretation for proximal displacement.

knowledge_statements.title: Displacement Ambiguity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shows why proximal displacement is not a well-defined stationarity vector when the proximal map is multivalued.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(\lambda>0\) and let \(f(y)=-y^2/(2\lambda)\). Since \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=\mathbb R\), selecting a proximal point \(p\) produces the displacement and residual
\[d_p=0-p=-p,\qquad r_p=\lambda^{-1}(0-p)=-\frac{p}{\lambda}.\]
As \(p\) ranges over the proximal map, both \(d_p\) and \(r_p\) range over all of \(\mathbb R\); their norms can be zero or arbitrarily large at the same base point. Hence neither proximal displacement nor its norm is selection-independent without uniqueness or an explicit selection rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different minimizers of one proximal subproblem yield residuals ranging from zero to arbitrarily large values at the same point.

notation.meaning: Scaled proximal residual associated with p.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role fits the displacement-ambiguity leaf. The selection-dependent displacement and residual indeed range over all of R, but no source or inspectable locator is provided for the proximal-residual interpretation.

children.title: Stationarity without Solution Quality
children.top_down_role: The boundary between envelope stationarity and stronger optimality guarantees.

knowledge_statements.title: Stationarity without Solution Quality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Moreau-envelope stationarity alone does not distinguish minimizers from other stationary points of a weakly convex objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(f(x)=(x^2-1)^2\) on \(\mathbb R\). Since \(f''(x)=12x^2-4\geq-4\), the function is \(4\)-weakly convex. For \(0<\lambda<1/4\), the proximal objective centered at zero is
\[f(y)+\frac{y^2}{2\lambda}=y^4+\left(\frac{1}{2\lambda}-2\right)y^2+1,\]
whose unique minimizer is \(y=0\). Hence \(\operatorname{prox}_{\lambda f}(0)=0\) and \(\nabla f_\lambda(0)=0\). Nevertheless, \(f(0)=1\), whereas the global minimizers \(x=\pm1\) satisfy \(f(\pm1)=0\); envelope stationarity therefore gives no global solution-quality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A point can have zero Moreau-envelope gradient yet remain one unit above the global minimum.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample role fits the stationarity-without-solution-quality leaf. The quartic is 4-weakly convex, zero is the unique proximal point for the stated parameter range, and envelope stationarity coexists with a unit global objective gap. No authoritative citation and locator are supplied for the envelope identity or counterexample.
